chapters.title: Chapter 1101
paragraphs: For ages, people had called the lands north and south of the Yellow River the Central Plains and considered them the heart of the world.
The birthplace of the earliest civilization. Fertile land, abundant resources, and the staggering productivity they made possible.
With advantages like those, people were bound to flock there from every direction.
The problem was that among them were foreign peoples from distant borderlands, who often wanted to “borrow” the Central Plains’ gold and silver treasures.
By their own methods: plunder or occupation.
Naturally, the people of the Central Plains weren’t too fond of that.

So they built the Great Wall, stretching a full ten thousand li. They strengthened the armies stationed along the borders, raised impregnable fortresses and walled cities throughout the land, and kept reinforcing them generation after generation.
All the more so in Xining, the capital of Qinghai—the farthest of the borderlands, practically the continent’s GOP.

But the rulers who gave those orders, and the craftsmen and laborers who sweated to carry them out, could never have dreamed there were madmen who would hurl themselves bodily against walls built of solid stone, stacked layer upon layer and sealed tight with lime.
Or that those madmen would be enormous monsters, hideous and monstrously strong.
*Rumble, rumble!*
The ground—or rather, the city—shook.
Several thousand monsters battered the wall with their bare bodies or with huge logs and clubs they’d gotten from who knew where. The sight alone was enough to freeze the blood.
It doused the defenders’ fighting spirit just as it had begun to blaze.
“Don’t break formation! Hold your positions!”
Choked breaths escaped here and there amid a storm of shouted commands.
And this wasn’t happening only at the West Gate, where I was stationed.
The North Gate and South Gate were the same. So was the East Gate, though the assault there was comparatively light.
Countless enemies had encircled Xining for dozens of li. Now, with those stubbornly resilient monsters in front, they were beginning their siege in earnest.
“Archers, ready!”
“Loose! Loose!”
*Shhk, thud-thud!*
Our response was swift, too.
A dense rain of arrows fell at nearly direct-fire angles, holding back the Dark Heaven followers, while we brought out the countermeasure we’d prepared for the monsters.
“Is it ready?”
One of the commanders answered my quiet question. Sweat had already soaked the inside of his helmet.
“Everything’s prepared, just as the Marquis of Shangshan ordered.”
Then there was no need to hesitate any longer.
I turned to the tense commander and the imperial troops standing by.
“Pour it all out. Give them the works.”
The moment I gave the order—
*Groan.*
Signal flags swung vigorously. With a heavy metallic groan, the great iron cauldrons set along the wall tipped and disgorged their contents.
Thick, black, boiling oil.
*Splash! Ssssss!*
—*GRAAAAH!*
Acrid smoke mingled with the smell of burning, and the monsters’ screams rose over it all.
But I knew better than anyone that oil alone wouldn’t be enough to destroy creatures that were practically undead monsters already.
And with the sorcerers controlling them still nowhere to be seen, this was the right moment for me to act.
*Fwoosh.*
I drew a deep breath, and the fire dragon coiled deep inside me awoke.

It had left its longtime home in my Lower Dantian. Now the enormous flame had made a nest atop the peak of my Middle Dantian, a peak that touched the heavens. It stirred and flowed into every part of my body.
Endlessly. Fiercely.
And at the same time, as swiftly as a ray of light.
*Whoosh.*
The moment I stepped forward, a spine-chilling sensation of weightlessness swept through me.
Before I knew it, everything lay beneath my feet.
The city wall, rising a dozen or so jang like a barrier at the edge of the world. The monsters and fanatics blackening the ground below.
Only one thing was level with my eyes.
A spear, wreathed in the flames of dark blue Force.
*Grind.*
Every muscle in my body drew taut as a bowstring. My senses, sharper than ever, focused at my fingertips.
I sought the most destructive, most perfect path for the spear to take as it cut slowly through the air and plunged down.
*Now.*
With that thought, I sent White Flame hurtling toward the distant ground.
*Whoosh!*
A flash of light. Through the air warped by searing heat, a streak of dark blue flame slipped among the enemies near the wall.
Then came a roar like the sky splitting open.
*BOOM!*
A vast pillar of fire surged up along the wall, defying the heavy rain pouring down without end.
Beneath it lay ground soaked with the oil we’d poured out so freely—and the enemies’ flesh and bones.
“Ghk, aaagh!”
“Keugh...!”
For better or worse, enemies who had barely escaped death were engulfed in flames and let out terrible screams.
Hundreds of them, at a rough count.
Maybe more.
But before the enormous roar that had shaken heaven and earth could even fade, my body was already dropping over their heads.
*Bang! Bang! Ba-bang!*
The air burst beneath my feet with each successive step.
The ground that had seemed impossibly far away rushed toward me. I reached into the empty air, where only wind and rain whipped past.
*Inventory open. Summon.*
*Ding.*
A System notification sounded, and something solid filled my empty hand. The enemies who had rushed toward the spot where I was descending from the sky stared wide-eyed.
“What the—”
*Shhk!*
One stroke, two halves.
The enemies proved those four words with their lives as their bodies split left and right.
A fountain of blood, vivid red even beneath the dark sky, spurted up. Madness glinted in the eyes of the enemies, already losing their focus.
“Heaven above and earth below, all demons bow!”
“Attack!”
*Shh-shh-shhk!*
A wind of blades swept in, colder than the rain.
The enemies had me surrounded on all sides, from every direction, and rushed in without regard for their lives.
Like moths drawn helplessly toward a flame.
*Shhk!*
Sharp Sword Energy slashed in from all sides.
Every streak was blood-red and looked dangerously unstable, as though its wielder had reached into a realm he had no business touching. Yet their power and speed rivaled a Peak master’s.
I still remembered seeing the same thing before.
*Temporary Strength Pills.*
A person’s final flame, fed with their own life.
I knew how tremendous the pills’ effects were, even if they lasted only a short time. Their danger matched their power.
I also knew that their hastily stacked kindling couldn’t match the heat of the furnace I’d built by surviving countless brushes with death.
*Thump!*
To conserve my strength, I hadn’t put so much as a trace of internal energy into the blow.
It was enough.
My body had already surpassed human limits by several steps. My senses, honed in the face of death, made it possible.
*Grrk.*
The Dark Heaven follower clutched at his throat, split open in an instant. By then, I’d already passed him and leaped toward the others.
*Whoosh!*
Half a step left.
Three streaks of Sword Energy missed me by a hair and tangled in midair. The rough broad-bladed saber that had been rusting in Xining’s armory left my hand.
*Wham!*
Without an ounce of internal energy behind it, the blade spun with sheer, terrifying force and cut through three necks.
No—it smashed through them.
At the same time, a command rang out in my mind, and new blades appeared in both hands.
A straight sword in my left. A narrow-bladed sword in my right.
They were unfamiliar. Yet somehow, impossibly familiar.
*Shreeeek! Thud-thud!*
Just the right amount of strength and speed, guided by movements that followed the flow of battle.
I fell into a Trance and swept through the enemies beneath the wall. Each swing of my sword and saber brought blood and screams. With every step, corpses spread beneath my feet like a carpet.
*Come.*
I spared even the single breath I might have let out without thinking.
With that single thought, I cut down the enemies surging at me from every direction. I cut and kept cutting.

I dodged a thrusting sword and pierced its wielder’s heart with the narrow-bladed sword. With nothing but a straight sword gone red with rust, I controlled the blades of five swords imbued with Sword Energy.
*Clang-clang-clang!*
I pressed against the flats of their blades and twisted. That was enough to knock the swords into one another in a tangle and cut off their wielders’ breath.
Strength when strength was needed. Softness when softness was needed.

When the narrow-bladed sword broke, I summoned an axe from the nearly infinite storeroom of my Inventory. With the broken straight sword, I wielded a blade technique infused with the principles of the Flame Divine Palm.
Even I couldn’t understand it. In that moment, I was free of every restriction and limit.
And suddenly, I understood.
*So that’s what he meant.*
Jeok Cheongang had once told me that when one’s understanding of martial arts reached a certain realm, every living, moving thing became a martial art.
Even a weak, bending reed would be no different from a Divine Sword.
Of course, I hadn’t reached that realm. But at last, I felt I could faintly grasp what he’d meant.
*Shhk!*
With the sensation of death running through my fingertips, I started to turn toward another enemy—then blinked.
There was no one. Everything was quiet.
The Dark Heaven followers who had taken Temporary Strength Pills. The enormous monsters that could no longer be called human.
Beneath the western wall, I was the only one left standing on two feet.
The blood-soaked scene before me meant one thing.
I had wiped out the enemy vanguard, at least a thousand strong.
All by myself.
*Ding. Ding. Ding.*

**System** You have met the activation conditions for the Title **One Against a Hundred**! You have met the activation conditions for the Title **One Against a Thousand**! **Intimidation** rises significantly! Your enemies are rapidly cowed by your powerful **Intimidation**! The status effect **Fear**, applied to some allies, is removed! Allied morale rises significantly!
System notifications poured into my ears like a dam breaking. A tremendous cheer erupted from atop the wall.
Then—
*BWOOOOO!*
A horn sounded with a deep note that made me shudder. At its call, Dark Heaven’s main force—some hundred thousand strong—began advancing toward the city walls.
And I realized what their movement meant.
The monsters.
No—the giants.
Each stood well over a jang tall. Their corpses had already piled halfway up the wall.

chapters.title: Chapter 1102
paragraphs: Looking back over the whole of human history, sieges had always overwhelmingly favored the defenders.
If you wanted to take what belonged to someone else, you had to pay a fitting price.
An attacking force needed at least three times as many soldiers to capture an ordinary castle or fortress. And even with more than that, the chances of losing a siege were still considerable.
To some people, though, that was nothing but old, rusted history.
“‘Impregnable’ is just nonsense left behind by weak losers.”
*Rumble.*
A vast rumble rolled over the Blood Lord’s low voice.
At that moment, Dark Heaven’s enormous army advanced toward the city wall like a single wave, turning the once-green expanse of land pitch-black.
They would use the corpses of humans and monsters as footholds to scale that towering wall.
They would write a new history of their own.
*The vanguard was annihilated faster than I expected...but it doesn’t matter. As long as we take Xining and cut that bastard’s throat.*
Jin Taekyung, defending the West Gate, hadn’t been the only one to stop the vanguard.

The Bow Saint and Slaughter Saint had defended the South Gate and East Gate, respectively, while the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, held the area around the North Gate. Four other Supreme Peak masters supported them from behind.
Yet even after thousands in the vanguard had vanished in reckless charges against the walls on all four sides, the Blood Lord remained unmoved.
*This much loss is nothing if it means achieving my goal.*
The monsters had been prepared for a moment just like this.
They would have been powerful assets in a battle on open ground, but the best use for an expendable asset depended on the situation.
Though he had lost nearly half the monsters, the Blood Lord was certain he’d made the right choice.
If he had sent ordinary followers—mere humans—out in front, they would have lost not thousands but tens of thousands before they could begin a proper siege like this.
“What about the mages? Are they all in their assigned positions?”
The Grand Sorceress nodded at the Blood Lord’s sudden question.
The hundred or so mages under her command were a core part of their forces, no different from a modern magic corps. They also had a vital role in this battle.
Under the ironclad protection of their allies, they were to keep the Supreme Peak masters off balance.
“Keep up the pressure. Make sure they have to spend their strength without a moment’s rest.”
Even with an overwhelming advantage, the Blood Lord wasn’t letting his guard down.
The four Demon Lords and the Demon Empress who had already met their ends had taught him a valuable lesson. And even without them, the defenders were an impressive lot.
No fewer than eight Supreme Peak masters.

One of them, the fool they called Great Sir, seemed so far gone that it was hard to imagine he could even function. But so many powerful fighters had rarely gathered in one place, even during the countless battles of the Great Faction War.
No—for that matter, the total number of troops assembled on this battlefield might be unprecedented in the history of Murim.
That was why the Blood Lord couldn’t allow even the slightest variable.
Especially not the one person who had created more variables than anyone else, time and again.
*Jin Taekyung.*
His gaze grew deep and still.
In the distance, he saw the young man standing in the path of his charging followers, whose cries shook heaven and earth.
He saw the fountains of blood erupting ceaselessly around him, too.
*Fwoosh!*
With every flash, another life flickered out.
His movements had reached an astonishing realm: simple, swift, and utterly overwhelming.
And yet—
*Nothing lasts forever.*
Jin Taekyung was undoubtedly strong.
He might even be growing stronger, little by little, at this very moment.
But everything had its limits.
*In the end, he’ll grow tired. Jin Taekyung, the Fire King, and all the other old men.*
Unless the Blood Lord gave the order, the wheels of this enormous war of attrition, turning on the back of overwhelming numbers and strength, would never stop.
Not until the eight Supreme Peak masters—the defenders’ heads and hearts—were exhausted.
The Blood Lord sensed that moment was drawing near.
And he knew what he needed to prepare to cut Jin Taekyung’s throat.
“From now on, the West Gate is mine alone.”
The Grand Sorceress understood the meaning behind his sudden announcement.
“For some reason, that sounds like you’re ordering me to leave. Am I imagining things?”
“That’s exactly what it is. Your imagination.”
“Then why should I leave the West Gate?”
“Do you need a reason? I’m the commander in chief.”
“I know. I just have my doubts.”
“Doubts? What exactly are you trying to say?”
“Well. For instance...”
The Grand Sorceress let her voice trail off. She looked from Jin Taekyung, fighting desperately to defend the western wall, to the Blood Lord.
“I worry that someone who’s always claimed to be *that person’s* most devoted servant might be a little too devoted—even to the point of defying his master’s wishes.”
It was as if she’d seen straight through him.
But the Blood Lord showed not the slightest hint of agitation.
He had considered that the Grand Sorceress might suspect his intentions from the moment he decided to kill Jin Taekyung.
“That’s beyond imagining things. You’re going senile. Do I look like an idiot who’d commit such an act of disloyalty?”
His reply was calm, without a trace of hesitation. The Grand Sorceress studied him for a moment, then shrugged.
“True. Disloyal is the last thing I’d call you. Though your loyalty has made you look like an idiot now and then.”
In the past, the Blood Lord would have bared his teeth and snarled at that. But his mind was colder than ever.
“So, what’s your answer?”
“Fine. Where should I go?”
“Take the South Gate.”
“The South Gate? The Bow Saint?”
“I’ll assign you three Black Ghosts. No, four. With that much force, even the Bow Saint won’t have many options.”
What the Blood Lord said was true, but the Grand Sorceress frowned.
“Black Ghosts? Four of them?”
Nine Black Ghosts had yet to enter the battle.

Even after one had been lost to the Fire King and Slaughter Saint’s surprise attack, assigning her four was hard to understand. They retained all the martial prowess they’d possessed in life and could recover from almost any wound.
And it wasn’t merely a question of her safety. Sending four to the South Gate would leave a gap in the forces available to break through the walls on all sides when the time came.
But her doubts vanished at the Blood Lord’s next words.
“Don’t hold back. You and the mages—press them hard. Once the Black Ghosts appear as well, the enemy will commit more of their strength to the South Gate.”
The Grand Sorceress finally understood and let out a quiet laugh.
“So I’m bait to draw in the Fire King or the Slaughter Saint?”
“Half right, half wrong.”
“What?”
“The Fire King won’t go to the South Gate. He’ll be busy greeting an unexpected guest.”
The Blood Lord answered without hesitation. He turned his cold gaze toward the Dalai Lama, who had been watching the northern wall all this time.
“Isn’t that right, Palace Lord?”
The Dalai Lama’s eyes trembled.
The moment of revenge he had waited so long for had finally arrived. Slowly, he parted his lips.
“What should this humble monk do?”
“Show that old man, the Fire King, the resentment and strength the Potala Palace has built through long years of endurance.”
“I have waited my whole life for this moment alone.”
The Dalai Lama pressed his palms together with heartfelt sincerity, then leaped atop a massive elephant.
“Come. The time has come to avenge our ancestors.”
His quiet voice, infused with internal energy, carried on without end.
The Twelve Secret Monks, including two Supreme Peak masters, and the Potala Palace’s ten thousand monks answered with a roar loud enough to make their ears ring.
*Bwooooo!*
A horn sounded, shaking the battlefield.
The great army of Tibet’s Murim, now a single religious state, charged through the torrential rain toward the North Gate.
To trample the descendants of the Fire Gate Clan, sworn enemies with whom they could never share the same sky.
To offer the head of Jeok Cheongang, the current Sect Leader of the Fire Gate Clan and heir to that accursed lineage, before the spirits of their ancestors.
As the Dalai Lama’s forces receded into the distance, the Grand Sorceress’s voice reached the Blood Lord.
“Does that leave only the East Gate?”
“I’ll send two Black Ghosts to the East Gate.”
“Two? An awkward number. The Slaughter Saint might even take them down.”
“But that won’t happen. I’ll order them to avoid a direct fight with the Slaughter Saint as much as possible and stick to a cautious attack.”
“I take back what I said about the number being awkward.”
The Grand Sorceress’s lips curved softly beneath her veil.
“It’s just the right number to let the Slaughter Saint leave his post to rescue the South Gate when it’s in danger.”
The Blood Lord gave a faint smile to match hers.
“And that will keep them from suspecting us.”
If Dark Heaven sent no significant force to the East Gate, that alone would arouse suspicion.

But if they sent a substantial force and merely kept the pressure a little lighter, the troops at the East Gate, including the Slaughter Saint, would have some room to breathe. They would have time to look around.
Time to help their allies elsewhere, who would be on the verge of collapse.
The gap left at that moment would be the crack that brought down that massive, solid dam in an instant.
*Whoosh!*
Wind and rain whipped at the Blood Lord’s clothes.
An ordinary person would have been soaked through and shivering from the cold that bit to the bone. The Blood Lord smiled and reached out his hand.
An east wind.
A fiercer east wind than ever was blowing along a tributary of the Yellow River.
And with it came more guests, riding the surging river waters to bring this battle to its grand finale after the Potala Palace.
*Preee!*
An eagle flew in from the east through the dark, rain-filled sky. It gave a powerful cry and landed on the Blood Lord’s shoulder.
Bones showed white through its body in patches, and its blood-red eyes gleamed.

sentences.text: Looking back over the whole of human history, sieges had always overwhelmingly favored the defenders.
If you wanted to take what belonged to someone else, you had to pay a fitting price.
An attacking force needed at least three times as many soldiers to capture an ordinary castle or fortress.
And even with more than that, the chances of losing a siege were still considerable.
To some people, though, that was nothing but old, rusted history.
“‘Impregnable’ is just nonsense left behind by weak losers.”
*Rumble.*
A vast rumble rolled over the Blood Lord’s low voice.
At that moment, Dark Heaven’s enormous army advanced toward the city wall like a single wave, turning the once-green expanse of land pitch-black.
They would use the corpses of humans and monsters as footholds to scale that towering wall.
They would write a new history of their own.
*The vanguard was annihilated faster than I expected...but it doesn’t matter.
As long as we take Xining and cut that bastard’s throat.*
Jin Taekyung, defending the West Gate, hadn’t been the only one to stop the vanguard.
The Bow Saint and Slaughter Saint had defended the South Gate and East Gate, respectively, while the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, held the area around the North Gate.
Four other Supreme Peak masters supported them from behind.
Yet even after thousands in the vanguard had vanished in reckless charges against the walls on all four sides, the Blood Lord remained unmoved.
*This much loss is nothing if it means achieving my goal.*
The monsters had been prepared for a moment just like this.
They would have been powerful assets in a battle on open ground, but the best use for an expendable asset depended on the situation.
Though he had lost nearly half the monsters, the Blood Lord was certain he’d made the right choice.
If he had sent ordinary followers—mere humans—out in front, they would have lost not thousands but tens of thousands before they could begin a proper siege like this.
“What about the mages?
Are they all in their assigned positions?”
The Grand Sorceress nodded at the Blood Lord’s sudden question.
The hundred or so mages under her command were a core part of their forces, no different from a modern magic corps.
They also had a vital role in this battle.
Under the ironclad protection of their allies, they were to keep the Supreme Peak masters off balance.
“Keep up the pressure.
Make sure they have to spend their strength without a moment’s rest.”
Even with an overwhelming advantage, the Blood Lord wasn’t letting his guard down.
The four Demon Lords and the Demon Empress who had already met their ends had taught him a valuable lesson.
And even without them, the defenders were an impressive lot.
No fewer than eight Supreme Peak masters.
One of them, the fool they called Great Sir, seemed so far gone that it was hard to imagine he could even function.
But so many powerful fighters had rarely gathered in one place, even during the countless battles of the Great Faction War.
No—for that matter, the total number of troops assembled on this battlefield might be unprecedented in the history of Murim.
That was why the Blood Lord couldn’t allow even the slightest variable.
Especially not the one person who had created more variables than anyone else, time and again.
*Jin Taekyung.*
His gaze grew deep and still.
In the distance, he saw the young man standing in the path of his charging followers, whose cries shook heaven and earth.
He saw the fountains of blood erupting ceaselessly around him, too.
*Fwoosh!*
With every flash, another life flickered out.
His movements had reached an astonishing realm: simple, swift, and utterly overwhelming.
And yet—
*Nothing lasts forever.*
Jin Taekyung was undoubtedly strong.
He might even be growing stronger, little by little, at this very moment.
But everything had its limits.
*In the end, he’ll grow tired.
Jin Taekyung, the Fire King, and all the other old men.*
Unless the Blood Lord gave the order, the wheels of this enormous war of attrition, turning on the back of overwhelming numbers and strength, would never stop.
Not until the eight Supreme Peak masters—the defenders’ heads and hearts—were exhausted.
The Blood Lord sensed that moment was drawing near.
And he knew what he needed to prepare to cut Jin Taekyung’s throat.
“From now on, the West Gate is mine alone.”
The Grand Sorceress understood the meaning behind his sudden announcement.
“For some reason, that sounds like you’re ordering me to leave.
Am I imagining things?”
“That’s exactly what it is.
Your imagination.”
“Then why should I leave the West Gate?”
“Do you need a reason?
I’m the commander in chief.”
“I know.
I just have my doubts.”
“Doubts?
What exactly are you trying to say?”
“Well.
For instance...”
The Grand Sorceress let her voice trail off.
She looked from Jin Taekyung, fighting desperately to defend the western wall, to the Blood Lord.
“I worry that someone who’s always claimed to be *that person’s* most devoted servant might be a little too devoted—even to the point of defying his master’s wishes.”
It was as if she’d seen straight through him.
But the Blood Lord showed not the slightest hint of agitation.
He had considered that the Grand Sorceress might suspect his intentions from the moment he decided to kill Jin Taekyung.
“That’s beyond imagining things.
You’re going senile.
Do I look like an idiot who’d commit such an act of disloyalty?”
His reply was calm, without a trace of hesitation.
The Grand Sorceress studied him for a moment, then shrugged.
“True.
Disloyal is the last thing I’d call you.
Though your loyalty has made you look like an idiot now and then.”
In the past, the Blood Lord would have bared his teeth and snarled at that.
But his mind was colder than ever.
“So, what’s your answer?”
“Fine.
Where should I go?”
“Take the South Gate.”
“The South Gate?
The Bow Saint?”
“I’ll assign you three Black Ghosts.
No, four.
With that much force, even the Bow Saint won’t have many options.”
What the Blood Lord said was true, but the Grand Sorceress frowned.
“Black Ghosts?
Four of them?”
Nine Black Ghosts had yet to enter the battle.
Even after one had been lost to the Fire King and Slaughter Saint’s surprise attack, assigning her four was hard to understand.
They retained all the martial prowess they’d possessed in life and could recover from almost any wound.
And it wasn’t merely a question of her safety.
Sending four to the South Gate would leave a gap in the forces available to break through the walls on all sides when the time came.
But her doubts vanished at the Blood Lord’s next words.
“Don’t hold back.
You and the mages—press them hard.
Once the Black Ghosts appear as well, the enemy will commit more of their strength to the South Gate.”
The Grand Sorceress finally understood and let out a quiet laugh.
“So I’m bait to draw in the Fire King or the Slaughter Saint?”
“Half right, half wrong.”
“What?”
“The Fire King won’t go to the South Gate.
He’ll be busy greeting an unexpected guest.”
The Blood Lord answered without hesitation.
He turned his cold gaze toward the Dalai Lama, who had been watching the northern wall all this time.
“Isn’t that right, Palace Lord?”
The Dalai Lama’s eyes trembled.
The moment of revenge he had waited so long for had finally arrived.
Slowly, he parted his lips.
“What should this humble monk do?”
“Show that old man, the Fire King, the resentment and strength the Potala Palace has built through long years of endurance.”
“I have waited my whole life for this moment alone.”
The Dalai Lama pressed his palms together with heartfelt sincerity, then leaped atop a massive elephant.
“Come.
The time has come to avenge our ancestors.”
His quiet voice, infused with internal energy, carried on without end.
The Twelve Secret Monks, including two Supreme Peak masters, and the Potala Palace’s ten thousand monks answered with a roar loud enough to make their ears ring.
*Bwooooo!*
A horn sounded, shaking the battlefield.
The great army of Tibet’s Murim, now a single religious state, charged through the torrential rain toward the North Gate.
To trample the descendants of the Fire Gate Clan, sworn enemies with whom they could never share the same sky.
To offer the head of Jeok Cheongang, the current Sect Leader of the Fire Gate Clan and heir to that accursed lineage, before the spirits of their ancestors.
As the Dalai Lama’s forces receded into the distance, the Grand Sorceress’s voice reached the Blood Lord.
“Does that leave only the East Gate?”
“I’ll send two Black Ghosts to the East Gate.”
“Two?
An awkward number.
The Slaughter Saint might even take them down.”
“But that won’t happen.
I’ll order them to avoid a direct fight with the Slaughter Saint as much as possible and stick to a cautious attack.”
“I take back what I said about the number being awkward.”
The Grand Sorceress’s lips curved softly beneath her veil.
“It’s just the right number to let the Slaughter Saint leave his post to rescue the South Gate when it’s in danger.”
The Blood Lord gave a faint smile to match hers.
“And that will keep them from suspecting us.”
If Dark Heaven sent no significant force to the East Gate, that alone would arouse suspicion.
But if they sent a substantial force and merely kept the pressure a little lighter, the troops at the East Gate, including the Slaughter Saint, would have some room to breathe.
They would have time to look around.
Time to help their allies elsewhere, who would be on the verge of collapse.
The gap left at that moment would be the crack that brought down that massive, solid dam in an instant.
*Whoosh!*
Wind and rain whipped at the Blood Lord’s clothes.
An ordinary person would have been soaked through and shivering from the cold that bit to the bone.
The Blood Lord smiled and reached out his hand.
An east wind.
A fiercer east wind than ever was blowing along a tributary of the Yellow River.
And with it came more guests, riding the surging river waters to bring this battle to its grand finale after the Potala Palace.
*Preee!*
An eagle flew in from the east through the dark, rain-filled sky.
It gave a powerful cry and landed on the Blood Lord’s shoulder.
Bones showed white through its body in patches, and its blood-red eyes gleamed.
The Blood Lord knew what good news the eagle’s arrival heralded.
He stroked the hilt of the sword at his waist and murmured, “The time has come.”

chapters.title: Chapter 1103
paragraphs: One Against a Thousand.
Just a few years ago, my life couldn’t have been further from the meaning of those four words.

I’d scraped together some secondhand gear at a bargain price after a few rounds of haggling. I couldn’t even afford a decent supply of the cheapest potions. The most I could handle was a few dozen small monsters in the dark, damp caves inside the subspaces known as Gates.
But a lot had changed since then.
More than I could put into words.
*Thwack!*
The rusty iron sword I swung on instinct sank into the crown of an enemy approaching from the side. His skull split, and bright red blood sprayed in every direction.
*Plop.*
A sticky, hot sensation brushed my cheek.
Once, that chilling touch would have made me flinch. Then the foul stench that crawled into my nose would have made me recoil again.
But that rookie Hunter, who’d thrown up at the horrible stench of blood he’d never smelled before, existed only in my memories now.
*Thrust!*
I drove my blade into the throat of an enemy charging straight at me, twisted it, and yanked it free. Blood poured from the gaping wound.
*Grrk.*
His body trembled as a wet rattle rose from his throat.
But to the fanatics, drunk on years of brainwashing and the strength of the Temporary Strength Pills, their comrade’s gruesome death was martyrdom—and another chance to catch me off guard.
*Shh-shh-shhk!*
Blood-red Sword Energy rained down from every direction. The dense, destructive strands tangled together like a net and closed over my entire body.
Or at least, that was what it must have looked like to them.
*Tap.*
One step.
With that single step, the space between my enemies and me vanished.
I spun, and the iron sword in my hand traced a perfect, deadly arc.
*Whoosh!*
For an instant, the world seemed to stop.
The enemies realized that instead of retreating, I’d plunged straight into their midst. Their eyes slowly widened.
And then—
*BOOM!*
As the Sword Energy they’d already unleashed exploded, dozens of heads shot into the air like fireworks.
*Shhk, fwoosh!*
Red.
Everything I could see. The whole world.
Yet even now, every sense and every part of my body kept working without pause.
*Whoosh.*
Everything caught in the diagonal sweep of my sword split apart.
As I crossed the rising mound of corpses, sticky blood and screams—darker still—spilled around my feet.
*Thwack! Thrust-thrust!*
I cut, stabbed, and smashed without pause.
It didn’t matter what I held.
An axe, a sword, even an oddly shaped weapon like a mace or a scythe—all of them were made to kill.
*Crack!*
A storm of blood and flesh swept through the air.

The weapons left to rust deep in Xining’s armory became masterworks steeped in a craftsman’s blood and sweat the moment they landed in my hands. They might break against Sword Energy, but they fulfilled their purpose to the end.
They took my enemies’ lives, just as their owner intended.
Shouts rang out from the enemies surrounding me and the allies on the wall above.
But I couldn’t make out what any of them were saying.
My ears felt muffled, though my senses were sharp enough to catch every sound. The world before my eyes moved so slowly it was almost boring, yet every detail was clear.
I had no idea how many enemies I’d taken down or how many weapons I’d broken.
I was certain of only one thing.
Insight.
I was climbing toward another moment of enlightenment.
Wrapped in a fog of No-self, forgetting not only what was happening around me but even myself, I moved through a battlefield where life and death hung in the balance.
*More. Just a little more.*
As if bewitched, I kept repeating the words to myself.
At some point, everything around me had begun to feel hazy, like a dream.
A sensation I couldn’t tell from pain or pleasure ran down my spine like an electric current.
I’d felt it before.
Now the Trance was more intense than ever, taking over my entire body.
*Come.*

As though they’d heard the quiet whisper in my mind, the enemies charged at me as one. They recited those eight words, that curse of a creed—“Heaven above and earth below, all demons bow!”—then roared and swung their weapons with all their might.
In the same instant, every one of them became a lonely soul.
*Shhk. Shhk. Shhk.*
Was this what the prophet in the old myths had been like?
Everything split apart as I strode forward without hesitation.
There was no sea before me, but the blood pouring from my enemies surged like waves. It was another kind of Red Sea.
And at the end of those red waves spilling away on either side, an insight awaited—one that would lift me to a higher level.
*I can do this. I know I can.*
Instinct spread over my fading reason.
Without looking, I dodged a blade swung at me from behind. With one stroke, I cut down five enemies charging from the side and the front.
But still, it wasn’t enough.
I suddenly wanted this dreamlike sensation to last forever. This dream belonged only to me, and it was the sweetest sleep I’d ever known.
Even if I woke from it, I’d sell my soul just to see this story through to the end.
If I could make the insight drawing closer with every step my own, I could fall into this same sweet sleep whenever I wanted.
But then I remembered something I’d briefly forgotten.
If there was someone dreaming, then there was someone who could wake them.
*Whoooooosh!*
A sharp whistle cut through the distant echo that every other sound had become.
The ferocity in it, the enormous force drawing closer by the moment, dragged me out of my dream and hurled me into reality.
Along with someone’s urgent, unfinished shout, suddenly bursting from somewhere in the open air.
“Dodge—!”
At that very moment—
*Fwoosh.*
The fog of No-self that had taken over my mind and body scattered in an instant.
No—it burst apart.
At the same time, a blood-red flash hurtled toward me from far away, its dazzling light staining my vision a thick red.
My eyes widened. An alarm blared in my head, whispering:
*Too late. You can’t dodge it.*
The flash was terrifyingly fast. Torn from that sweet sleep and thrown straight into reality, I couldn’t move quickly enough to evade it.
Unlike the person who’d warned me half a beat earlier—who might have been watching over me all along.
*Whoosh!*
In the slowed-down world, I saw someone drop through the air.
A snow-white blade blocked the flash, which was already almost at my nose. Violet Sword Force scattered around it like flower petals.
*Cheongpung.*
The instant his name surfaced in my frozen thoughts—
*BOOM!*
A tremendous shock wave shook the air with a roar like the sky splitting apart.
*Cough.*
In the pale dust cloud that covered everything, Jin Taekyung gave a dry cough, blinked dazedly, and wondered:
*Am I still alive?*
The question had come to him suddenly. The answer came at once.
Pains large and small stabbed through his body like needles, accompanied by a System alert only he could hear.
No—*warning sirens* would be more accurate.
*Beep! Beep-beep!*
Trying to ignore the sirens drilling into his ears, Jin Taekyung struggled to his feet.
*Pat-pat.*
Stone dust slid off his body.
He felt heavy. Everything hurt.
Maybe it was because he’d suddenly woken from a Trance in which every sense had been pushed to its limit.
His body sagged like waterlogged cotton. But despite the barrage of warning sirens, he didn’t seem to have any serious injuries.
He had the person who’d blocked the flash for him at the last moment to thank for that.
“Cheongpung.”
His tired, cracked voice slipped past his lips. But in the dust cloud, so thick he couldn’t see a hand in front of his face, all he heard were groans from people he couldn’t identify.
“...Cheongpung?”
He called several more times. When no answer came, dread crept over him.
Jin Taekyung took a deep breath and swept out his arm, its sleeve already torn to shreds.
*Boom!*
Compressed air exploded outward. A gust imbued with internal energy drove away some of the dust, revealing what lay beyond it.
A gaping hole in the city wall, wide enough for five grown men to stand shoulder to shoulder. Allies lay sprawled all around it, groaning in pain.
But there was still no sign of Cheongpung.
*Dammit.*
Jin Taekyung clenched his teeth without realizing it.
Then he stretched out his hand toward the enemies charging through the ruins of the broken wall and the dust cloud.
More precisely, toward his beloved weapon, which lay behind them.
*Vooooom.*
His Middle Dantian opened. With a low hum, a spear buried deep in the ground shot upward and returned to its master’s grasp.
It pierced every obstacle in its path.
*Crack!*
Blood spouted into the air.
Dozens of enemies, their spirits high as they charged, fell like rotten logs. In that brief opening, the allies formed ranks and fought with all their might to fill the gap.
*Clang-clang!*
*Thrust!*
“Gaaagh!”
“Hold them! Don’t let a single one through!”
“Cough—Archers! Where are the archers?”
Chaos spread in an instant.
Even as the melee broke out around the breached wall, Jin Taekyung cut down enemies with all his strength and shouted one person’s name.
“Young sir! Cheongpung!”
But no matter how keenly he strained his senses, there was no answer.
Only the screams and shouts of friend and foe rang out around him. That damned innocent voice was nowhere to be heard.
His heart pounded like thunder. With every moment, it grew harder to breathe.
*...No way.*
No. It couldn’t be.
Cheongpung—he wasn’t the kind of guy who’d go down this easily.
Like the hero in a fairy tale, he’d find some way to survive and live happily ever after.
Then why?
Why did this inexplicable dread keep growing heavier and darker?
“You... bastards!”
Jin Taekyung charged with a furious shout.
It was anger at the invaders who’d caused all this—but also blame directed at himself, the idiot who’d been consumed by a single-minded pursuit of enlightenment.
And the dazzling point of his spear, cutting through the enemy and raising a storm of blood, was drawing closer to one person approaching at a leisurely pace.
The Blood Lord.

Cheongpung—he wasn’t the kind of guy who’d go down this easily.
Like the hero in a fairy tale, he’d find some way to survive and live happily ever after.
Then why?
Why did this inexplicable dread keep growing heavier and darker?
“You... bastards!”
Jin Taekyung charged with a furious shout.
It was anger at the invaders who’d caused all this—but also blame directed at himself, the idiot who’d been consumed by a single-minded pursuit of enlightenment.
And the dazzling point of his spear, cutting through the enemy and raising a storm of blood, was drawing closer to one person approaching at a leisurely pace.
The Blood Lord.

paragraphs: *Splash. Splash.*
Footsteps crossed ground covered in blood, rainwater, and countless corpses. Each one landed with a peculiar weight.
Tens of thousands.
No—even on this vast battlefield, where friend and foe together numbered well over a hundred thousand, his presence was utterly overwhelming.
*Vooooom.*
Qi spread through the space around him with every step.

Even now, rain and arrows poured unceasingly from the sky, only to bounce off an invisible barrier of energy. The Dark Heaven followers charging toward the collapsed western wall split to either side and prostrated themselves.
As if bewitched, they murmured their eight-character creed.
“Heaven above and earth below.”
“All demons bow!”
It was reverence.
Reverence offered to the true ruler of this world, their god—and permitted only to the six Apostles he had personally favored.
The creed, begun with a few quiet murmurs, soon became a tremendous roar that swallowed the battlefield.
A ripple became a current, then a wave sweeping in every direction.
The pounding rain, the thunder flashing between the dark clouds, even the arrows raining down to fill the sky—nothing could stop the creed pouring from their lips.
“Now! Attack!”
“Archers! Loose together!”
*Shhk! Thud-thud-thud!*
Blades flashed, and heads flew across the battlefield.
Nor was that all.
Severed arms and legs plunged into the mud. Arrows streaked in like flashes of light and buried themselves in backs and waists.
But that was all.
Even when their limbs were cut off, even when arrowheads pierced their backs and poked out through their chests, they stubbornly continued reciting the creed.
Right up to the moment death fell over them.
“Heaven above and earth below—cough. All demons bow...”
*Thud.*
Only after forcing out the last words, blood pouring from him, did the Dark Heaven follower die. The Kunlun Sect Daoist who had stabbed him through the chest stood with trembling lips.
“P-Primordial Heavenly Venerable.”
A wave of fanaticism beyond words.
And fanatics who didn’t even fear death were everywhere.
No—every enemy darkening this vast battlefield was like that.
“This... What in the world is this?”
The words someone managed to squeeze out spoke for them all. They carried the utmost fear and horror a person could feel.
*Splash. Clatter.*
Weapons slipped from suddenly slack hands and sank into the mud.
For an instant, some of the Murim warriors and imperial troops lost their will to fight without even realizing it. Their trembling eyes stared blankly at the enemy.
They were afraid. So afraid they shuddered.
Not of some huge, savage monster, but of people who looked just like them.
Those mad fanatics, stripped of the joy, anger, sorrow, and pleasure every human being ought to feel, who followed only the Lord of Heaven with blind devotion.
And at their center, at the head of their ranks, walked a man wreathed in rippling, blood-red qi.
“What a bunch of worthless bastards.”
His soft sneer revealed a row of white teeth.
At the same time, as the Blood Lord gently extended his fingertips, countless weapons that had been rolling across the ground rose upright.
No—they shot forward at their new master’s command.
Toward the enemies frozen in place.
“You don’t deserve to live.”
At that moment—
*Pa-pa-pa-pat!*
Hundreds of weapons tore through the air at once.
A wave of steel swept through the ruins of the collapsed wall.
Those facing that blinding flash had no choice left. They weren’t granted time to close their eyes, let alone draw one last breath.
All they could do was stare, eyes wide, at the death bearing down on them.
Then a streak of searing wind swept over their heads.
*Gooooom.*
Space warped.
Terrifying heat and dark blue light-flames filled everyone’s sight.
And at last—
*Fwoosh—KRAAASH!*
The wave of steel met a wall of fire.
They struck each other head-on, unleashing the unimaginable power held within them in a burst of blinding light and sound.
*Rumble-rumble-rumble...!*
Would a volcano, ripe to erupt and roaring awake from a long sleep, sound like this?
Would a storm like this sweep across the land if an ancient giant exhaled with all its might?
No one could say.
No one, that is, except the two people standing tall as iron towers in the fierce light and shock wave that heated and drove back everything within dozens of jang.
“Good. You, at least, deserve to live.”
The Blood Lord brought the edge of his hand down as he murmured. The dust cloud coiling around the western wall split apart, revealing what it had concealed.
A young man, drenched from head to toe in blood and rain, stood perfectly steady, aiming a pure silver-white spear at him.
“Which is precisely why I can’t let you live.”
Admiration tinged the Blood Lord’s voice as he regarded the young man.
“Blazing Flame Divine Dragon, Jin Taekyung.”
At that moment, Jin Taekyung’s tightly closed lips parted.
“Appreciate the sudden worship, but...”
*Squelch.*
He pulled out the shards of blades that had somehow pierced his body in several places as they flew through the wall of fire, then continued:
“No matter how I look at it, you don’t deserve to live, you son of a bitch. That’s why you have to die.”
His voice was calm. Flames streamed from his eyes.
The Blood Lord gave a quiet laugh as he looked at him.
“Do you think you can do that? In your current condition?”
The Blood Lord wasn’t exaggerating.
Jin Taekyung’s appearance alone made him look like a man drenched in blood.
Given how many enemies he had cut down, that was only natural. But that didn’t mean he’d come away unscathed.
He was exhausted and injured, too.
So were the others now rising one by one behind his back, which stood as imposing as a mountain.
But Jin Taekyung wasn’t afraid.
He had already been afraid enough.
He had acknowledged and accepted every negative feeling that had weighed down his body and mind.
And so he managed a faint smile even as the Blood Lord approached.
“Sure, you could think that. But you know something?”
“What are you talking about?”
“Your precious friends all pulled that same shit on me before they died.”
“That’s what you call a death flag, you moron. Ah, would you even understand if I explained it?”
Jin Taekyung laughed. Whatever his words meant, the sneer vanished from the Blood Lord’s face.
“But I’m different from those idiots. I gave up on the idea of halfheartedly letting you live long ago.”
*Fwoosh.*
Blood-red qi rose in wisps with every step he took.
His red-glinting eyes reflected only Jin Taekyung.
“You die today. No question.”
“Wouldn’t the Lord of Heaven be upset to hear that? He must’ve been fond of you, raising you as his obedient little dog.”
“He will understand. This choice I make today comes from loyalty alone.”
“Is that so? Or is that just what you hope?”
“What?”
The Blood Lord stopped walking for an instant. Jin Taekyung’s voice slid into his ear.
“You don’t think he’ll understand. You think you’re screwed if he finds out, so you’re going ahead and doing it anyway. You even sent the Grand Sorceress far away, just in case.”

“Why are you staring at me with those rabbit eyes? You look disgusting enough already. Anyone would think you’d been slapped awake from a good night’s sleep. Hadn’t you already got a rough picture of it in your dream?”
*Crunch.*
The Blood Lord clenched his teeth without realizing it.
It wasn’t Jin Taekyung’s relentless taunts that made him do it. It was the truth he’d tried to ignore, stabbing into his heart like an awl.
“You know perfectly well what your master—that damned Lord of Heaven—wants most.”
He had to refute him.
That insolent brat was openly insulting the master he worshiped like a god and questioning his intentions. The Blood Lord should tear his mouth apart right now and rip out that wicked tongue.
But he couldn’t refute him.
Blazing Flame Divine Dragon, Jin Taekyung.
The Blood Lord had a vague sense that everything coming from that impertinent mouth was true.
He didn’t know when it had begun. He hadn’t even been told why.
But everything that had led them here pointed to one painful truth.
“What your master wants most isn’t the world. It sure as hell isn’t the lives of hunting dogs he uses and throws away, like you.”
Jin Taekyung’s voice burrowed into his ears. The truth in it shook him to the core.
“It’s me. Only me.”
“So go on, try to kill me. If I can screw the Lord of Heaven over by using you, I don’t care how it happens.”
At that instant, the Blood Lord’s slowly reddening eyes turned completely bloodred, their white pupils swallowed up.
And countless corpses scattered across the ground within some ten jang convulsed and spewed blood.
*Swoosh.*
The blood mixed with rainwater writhed as if alive and gathered at one man’s feet.
As he began walking again, it flowed together and joined, climbed his calves, and wrapped around his entire body.
No.
It was absorbed into him.
As if it had been part of him since the distant past.
*Fwoosh.*
Feeling an endless surge of vitality and strength rise from deep within him, the Blood Lord’s eyes blazed red.
“I heard your last words.”
Jin Taekyung stared blankly at the sight he hadn’t expected. Then he smacked his lips.
“Uh, could I maybe say a little more?”
The Blood Lord answered that ridiculous question with a massive flash of blood-red light.
*Whoooosh!*
In an instant, the world turned red.

chapters.title: Chapter 1105
paragraphs: Was it because Xining had endured one foreign invasion after another over the years?
The four walls surrounding the city now ran a full ten ri in length, enclosing a vast area behind fortifications whose strength was rarely seen even in the Central Plains.
But everything had its advantages and drawbacks.
The walls had been reinforced little by little over time, making them better at keeping invaders out. They had also given the defenders far more ground to cover.
To communicate across those distances, the defenders relied on war drums and flags stationed along the walls.
But at this moment, the blood-red flash that suddenly erupted in the west rendered them all useless.
*Fwoooosh.*
Would it look like this if dozens—hundreds—of sunsets overlapped?
In the slowing world, countless eyes widened at a sight none of them could describe.
The soldiers on a dozen or more watchtowers, beating their assigned war drums and waving their flags with all their strength.
The people hiding in Xining’s Inner City, clutching their families and peering through cracks in the doors.

The combined forces of the imperial troops and Murim warriors, fighting back the enemies surging toward them like waves—even the Supreme Peak masters at the heart and forefront of their ranks, cutting down enemy after enemy without pause.
And the moment they all felt a chill climb their spines—
*Pop.*
The blood-red flash rising over the western wall swelled.
No—it exploded in a vivid, horrifying burst of red light.
*Rumble-rumble-rumble!*
A roar left their ears ringing.
The ground shook. The entire stone wall trembled.
Then a colossal shock wave surged over the western wall and crashed down on the people frozen like statues.
“Watch out—!”
*KA-BOOOOM!*
The rushing wind swallowed someone’s single shout and swept across everything.
The North Gate was no different.
Dust, shattered rock, even blades that had lost their owners flew through the air. Everyone ducked and threw themselves toward cover.
Everyone except one man, still holding the front line.
*Fwoosh—BOOM!*
He drove out a fist, and flames burst forth, devouring the space before him.
Even that storm, like a natural disaster, bowed before the heat. Everything hurtling toward the defenders at the North Gate evaporated in an instant.
*Shhhhh.*
Ash drifted slowly away on the now-gentle breeze.
But the eyes of the man who had protected his allies from the unexpected threat—Fire King Jeok Cheongang—were more somber than ever.
*...What in the world was that?*
Though he held the chief seat among the Ten Kings, he had already reached a realm where he could stand shoulder to shoulder with the Three Saints.
He could feel it against his skin, with every one of his senses: the immense power contained in that distant blood-red flash.
And if the blast had reached the North Gate, more than two hundred jang away, what state must the West Gate—the source of it all—be in?
*Blood Lord, how did you...?*
Jeok Cheongang bit his lip without realizing it.
The Blood Lord’s martial prowess had advanced unmistakably since their encounter at Mount Song. But what weighed on his heart was the voice of someone he couldn’t stop thinking about.
“I’ll take the West Gate.”
Jin Taekyung.
When his Disciple had said that just before the battle, Jeok Cheongang had answered without a moment’s hesitation.
“Absolutely not. Instead of spouting that nonsense, do one more complete circulation. And don’t go getting yourself stabbed because you were fooling around.”
“My internal energy’s in great shape, and I can take a few stabs. So I’ll take responsibility for the West Gate.”
“I said no.”
“Why not?”
“You have to ask? That damned bastard has been mine for a long time. Today, I’ll finally collect the blood debt from that day.”
Jeok Cheongang’s answer had been both true and untrue.
He did want revenge for Hong Dao, his old friend. But the more important reason was that the enemy’s main force, including the Blood Lord, was stationed at the West Gate.
His Disciple was a reckless brat who’d long since thrown manners out the window. But he was his one and only Disciple.
He’d become more precious to Jeok Cheongang than anything else in the world. Jeok couldn’t leave him alone in the most dangerous place.
Of course, Taekyung knew his Master far too well for Jeok Cheongang to hide that bashful concern behind roundabout words.
“There you go worrying again. You don’t have to do that anymore.”
“Worry? Don’t be ridiculous. Just know that it’s absolutely out of the question.”
“I’ll be fine. I have no intention of dying a pointless death. Do you think I’m crazy? I wouldn’t be doing this if I didn’t have something to count on.”
“And what would that be?”
“You know already. As long as the Lord of Heaven wants me this badly, those guys can’t lay a finger on me. Well, I might get a little hurt.”
“That...”
Even Jeok Cheongang couldn’t easily argue with that.

Ever since the incidents at Mount Song and Sichuan, powerful enemies—including the Southern Heaven Demon Empress—had been decidedly reluctant to take Jin Taekyung’s life. The battle in Gansu had confirmed his suspicions.
Seeing his Master waver, Jin Taekyung drove in the final nail.
“No matter which gate I take, they’ll follow me. I’m their most important target. So I might as well take the West Gate—it’s the best-defended. Right?”
Every word he’d said had been right from beginning to end. In the end, Jeok Cheongang had no choice but to give in and head reluctantly to the North Gate.
But—
*I shouldn’t have done it.*
Now he regretted that decision with all his heart.
He’d judged wrong.
The Blood Lord’s martial prowess far exceeded anything he’d imagined, and Jin Taekyung, knowing exactly how his Master would react, had lied without batting an eye.
*At this rate... that boy’s in danger.*
The attack they had all just witnessed could only have come from someone intent on killing.
So, though his body had grown young again, his heart was still that of an old man. Feeling himself grow impatient, Jeok Cheongang turned toward the west.
No—he was about to turn.
Until the next instant, when he sensed a sharp thread of killing intent shooting like a needle from beyond the wall.
“Where are you rushing off to, donor?”
The voice was low.
Yet the several jiazi of internal energy within it were enough to shake the area around the North Gate.
So was the terrifying aura emanating from the old monk standing atop a colossal elephant, the likes of which Jeok Cheongang had never seen even at the Nanman Beast Palace.
“If you leave now, donor, I’ll have come all this way for nothing.”
His frame was tiny, his skin deeply wrinkled with age.
But his presence was like that of a giant, and Jeok Cheongang already knew who he was.
He also knew what it meant that this old monk—the Dalai Lama, Palace Lord of the Potala Palace—had appeared at the North Gate leading all those troops.
“...You planned this. From the beginning.”
The words escaped him in a low groan.
Then the Dalai Lama spoke, turning his ominous suspicion into certainty.
“The Fire Gate Clan’s line will end. Right here, today.”
At that moment—
*Bwaaaaaaa!*
A war horn sounded. As the Potala Palace forces surged toward him, Jeok Cheongang gritted his teeth without realizing it.
*Crack.*
His lips went white. His nails dug deep into his skin, and hot blood ran from beneath them. His turmoil had no other outlet.
It wasn’t too late.
He had to go. Even now.
To his Disciple. To Jin Taekyung.
But—
“P-Potala Palace! They’ve joined the battle!”
“Arrows! Bring more arrows!”
“Form a defensive line! Don’t retreat, even if it costs us our lives!”
“Sir Jeok, we don’t have time to hesitate!”
Shouts and screams from every direction held him in place.
Eyes full of fear, resolve, or faith seemed to seize his hands and close around his throat. The urgent voice of Perfected Being Hyeoncheon, defending the North Gate alongside him, pierced his ears.
*What would he have done? What would that boy have done?*
Jeok Cheongang put the question to himself and squeezed his eyes shut.
In that brief, profound darkness, he recalled the conversation he’d had with his Disciple the day before.
“I never wanted to be a hero.”
“That doesn’t matter. You don’t become a hero just because you want to. You earn the right when the world calls you one.”
“Like people call you a Great Hero, Old Master?”
“What?”

“You just said it yourself. You didn’t set out to follow some great cause. You just went where your feet led you, where the wind took you, and before you knew it, people were calling you a Great Hero.”
He remembered it clearly.
The bright smile Taekyung had given him when he was left speechless. His playful expression. His clear eyes.
Perhaps that was what Jeok Cheongang feared more than anything else.
Perhaps the thought that he might never see that face again had come first.
But when Jeok Cheongang had asked whether he was still afraid of the enemy, his Disciple had nodded without hesitation and added:
“Even so, I won’t turn away from that fear.”
Calm. Resolute.
And everything that had happened that day was the answer to the question Jeok Cheongang had just asked himself.
*Fwoooosh.*
In an instant, tremendous heat swallowed the space.
His eyelids rose slowly. His eyes glowed red with heat, blazing like flames.
He faced the Dalai Lama and the Twelve Secret Monks flying through the air toward him.
Toward the two Black Ghosts who had appeared, and the vast enemy army surging in behind them.
*Grnnnnk.*
As the space warped under the unbearable heat, the giant of fire roared with all his might.
“Come!”
As if he meant to burn the whole world.
“This old man is Jeok Cheongang, the eighteenth Sect Leader of the great Fire Gate Clan—the Fire King!”
He hoped his roar would reach his Disciple.
