The combined forces of the imperial troops and Murim warriors, fighting back the enemies surging toward them like waves—even the Supreme Peak masters at the heart and forefront of their ranks, cutting down enemy after enemy without pause.
And the moment they all felt a chill climb their spines—
*Pop.*
The blood-red flash rising over the western wall swelled.
No—it exploded in a vivid, horrifying burst of red light.
*Rumble-rumble-rumble!*
A roar left their ears ringing.
The ground shook.
The entire stone wall trembled.
Then a colossal shock wave surged over the western wall and crashed down on the people frozen like statues.
“Watch out—!”
*KA-BOOOOM!*
The rushing wind swallowed someone’s single shout and swept across everything.
The North Gate was no different.
Dust, shattered rock, even blades that had lost their owners flew through the air.
Everyone ducked and threw themselves toward cover.
Everyone except one man, still holding the front line.
*Fwoosh—BOOM!*
He drove out a fist, and flames burst forth, devouring the space before him.
Even that storm, like a natural disaster, bowed before the heat.
Everything hurtling toward the defenders at the North Gate evaporated in an instant.
*Shhhhh.*
Ash drifted slowly away on the now-gentle breeze.
But the eyes of the man who had protected his allies from the unexpected threat—Fire King Jeok Cheongang—were more somber than ever.
*...What in the world was that?*
Though he held the chief seat among the Ten Kings, he had already reached a realm where he could stand shoulder to shoulder with the Three Saints.
He could feel it against his skin, with every one of his senses: the immense power contained in that distant blood-red flash.
And if the blast had reached the North Gate, more than two hundred jang away, what state must the West Gate—the source of it all—be in?
*Blood Lord, how did you...?*
Jeok Cheongang bit his lip without realizing it.
The Blood Lord’s martial prowess had advanced unmistakably since their encounter at Mount Song.
But what weighed on his heart was the voice of someone he couldn’t stop thinking about.
“I’ll take the West Gate.”
Jin Taekyung.
When his Disciple had said that just before the battle, Jeok Cheongang had answered without a moment’s hesitation.
“Absolutely not.
Instead of spouting that nonsense, do one more complete circulation.
And don’t go getting yourself stabbed because you were fooling around.”
“My internal energy’s in great shape, and I can take a few stabs.
So I’ll take responsibility for the West Gate.”
“I said no.”
“Why not?”
“You have to ask?
That damned bastard has been mine for a long time.
Today, I’ll finally collect the blood debt from that day.”
Jeok Cheongang’s answer had been both true and untrue.
He did want revenge for Hong Dao, his old friend.
But the more important reason was that the enemy’s main force, including the Blood Lord, was stationed at the West Gate.
His Disciple was a reckless brat who’d long since thrown manners out the window.
But he was his one and only Disciple.
He’d become more precious to Jeok Cheongang than anything else in the world.
Jeok couldn’t leave him alone in the most dangerous place.
Of course, Taekyung knew his Master far too well for Jeok Cheongang to hide that bashful concern behind roundabout words.
“There you go worrying again.
You don’t have to do that anymore.”
“Worry?
Don’t be ridiculous.
Just know that it’s absolutely out of the question.”
“I’ll be fine.
I have no intention of dying a pointless death.
Do you think I’m crazy?
I wouldn’t be doing this if I didn’t have something to count on.”
“And what would that be?”
“You know already.
As long as the Lord of Heaven wants me this badly, those guys can’t lay a finger on me.
Well, I might get a little hurt.”
“That...”
Even Jeok Cheongang couldn’t easily argue with that.
Ever since the incidents at Mount Song and Sichuan, powerful enemies—including the Southern Heaven Demon Empress—had been decidedly reluctant to take Jin Taekyung’s life.
The battle in Gansu had confirmed his suspicions.
Seeing his Master waver, Jin Taekyung drove in the final nail.
“No matter which gate I take, they’ll follow me.
I’m their most important target.
So I might as well take the West Gate—it’s the best-defended.
Right?”
Every word he’d said had been right from beginning to end.
In the end, Jeok Cheongang had no choice but to give in and head reluctantly to the North Gate.
But—
*I shouldn’t have done it.*
Now he regretted that decision with all his heart.
He’d judged wrong.
The Blood Lord’s martial prowess far exceeded anything he’d imagined, and Jin Taekyung, knowing exactly how his Master would react, had lied without batting an eye.
*At this rate... that boy’s in danger.*
The attack they had all just witnessed could only have come from someone intent on killing.
So, though his body had grown young again, his heart was still that of an old man.
Feeling himself grow impatient, Jeok Cheongang turned toward the west.
No—he was about to turn.
Until the next instant, when he sensed a sharp thread of killing intent shooting like a needle from beyond the wall.
“Where are you rushing off to, donor?”
The voice was low.
Yet the several jiazi of internal energy within it were enough to shake the area around the North Gate.
So was the terrifying aura emanating from the old monk standing atop a colossal elephant, the likes of which Jeok Cheongang had never seen even at the Nanman Beast Palace.
“If you leave now, donor, I’ll have come all this way for nothing.”
His frame was tiny, his skin deeply wrinkled with age.
But his presence was like that of a giant, and Jeok Cheongang already knew who he was.
He also knew what it meant that this old monk—the Dalai Lama, Palace Lord of the Potala Palace—had appeared at the North Gate leading all those troops.
“...You planned this.
From the beginning.”
The words escaped him in a low groan.
Then the Dalai Lama spoke, turning his ominous suspicion into certainty.
“The Fire Gate Clan’s line will end.
Right here, today.”
At that moment—
*Bwaaaaaaa!*
A war horn sounded.
As the Potala Palace forces surged toward him, Jeok Cheongang gritted his teeth without realizing it.
*Crack.*
His lips went white.
His nails dug deep into his skin, and hot blood ran from beneath them.
His turmoil had no other outlet.
It wasn’t too late.
He had to go.
Even now.
To his Disciple.
To Jin Taekyung.
But—
“P-Potala Palace!
They’ve joined the battle!”
“Arrows!
Bring more arrows!”
“Form a defensive line!
Don’t retreat, even if it costs us our lives!”
“Sir Jeok, we don’t have time to hesitate!”
Shouts and screams from every direction held him in place.
Eyes full of fear, resolve, or faith seemed to seize his hands and close around his throat.
The urgent voice of Perfected Being Hyeoncheon, defending the North Gate alongside him, pierced his ears.
*What would he have done?
What would that boy have done?*
Jeok Cheongang put the question to himself and squeezed his eyes shut.
In that brief, profound darkness, he recalled the conversation he’d had with his Disciple the day before.
“I never wanted to be a hero.”
“That doesn’t matter.
You don’t become a hero just because you want to.
You earn the right when the world calls you one.”
“Like people call you a Great Hero, Old Master?”
“What?”
“You just said it yourself.
You didn’t set out to follow some great cause.
You just went where your feet led you, where the wind took you, and before you knew it, people were calling you a Great Hero.”
He remembered it clearly.
The bright smile Taekyung had given him when he was left speechless.
His playful expression.
His clear eyes.
Perhaps that was what Jeok Cheongang feared more than anything else.
Perhaps the thought that he might never see that face again had come first.
But when Jeok Cheongang had asked whether he was still afraid of the enemy, his Disciple had nodded without hesitation and added:
“Even so, I won’t turn away from that fear.”
Calm.
Resolute.
And everything that had happened that day was the answer to the question Jeok Cheongang had just asked himself.
*Fwoooosh.*
In an instant, tremendous heat swallowed the space.
His eyelids rose slowly.
His eyes glowed red with heat, blazing like flames.
He faced the Dalai Lama and the Twelve Secret Monks flying through the air toward him.
Toward the two Black Ghosts who had appeared, and the vast enemy army surging in behind them.
*Grnnnnk.*
As the space warped under the unbearable heat, the giant of fire roared with all his might.
“Come!”
As if he meant to burn the whole world.
“This old man is Jeok Cheongang, the eighteenth Sect Leader of the great Fire Gate Clan—the Fire King!”
He hoped his roar would reach his Disciple.

chapters.title: Chapter 1106
paragraphs: *BOOM!*
The flash that filled my vision was red as blood.
*Pwoom!*
Unfathomable power seethed in every strike.
*Krrrunch!*
The world kept turning upside down, then righting itself.
No—not the world. Me.
*Fwoooooosh—BOOM!*
A tremendous shock shot up my spine and spread through my entire body.
After dozens of exchanges in the space of a lightning flash, I ended up buried deep in the layered rubble of the wall.
*Cough.*
Blood surged up against my will and spilled past my lips.
A System warning chime sounded through the ringing in my ears. The pain coming from every part of my body told me the warning was real.
*I’m sure I heard something.*
I muttered it weakly to myself, remembering a familiar voice that had rung out somewhere in the distance just before the assault sent me flying.
But I must have imagined it.
One of those hallucinations that came to me every now and then when I was exhausted and hurting.
“...Damn it.”
Blood kept welling up. My torn-up hands tingled.
Even so, I forced my aching body upright with a quiet curse.
No. I had to.
If I didn’t stop that monster, none of the thousands of allies risking their lives to defend the West Gate could.
*Splash. Splash.*
Heavy footsteps approached, neither fast nor slow.
With every step, the blood swirling ankle-deep in the downpour trembled like a living thing.
*Shhhhhh.*
It was enough to chill anyone who saw it.
Hundreds of snakes, red from head to tail, seemed to slide across the surface of the water.
And at the end of their eerie advance stood a monster, ready to take in more power.
*Hssss.*
The blood seeped into his skin as though it had never existed outside him.
Then the monster’s eyes blazed a fiercer red through the pounding rain.
They were fixed on one person among the countless allies frozen like statues.
Me.
“Didn’t I tell you?”
His low voice reached me clearly.
The monster of blood had absorbed every drop within a radius of more than a hundred feet, devouring the life and strength it held. He gazed at me, eyes bright with delight.
“You can never be my equal. No one on this battlefield can.”
Veterans who’d survived for years in Murim, a mountain of sabers and a forest of swords, had a saying.
Too much confidence became conceit and arrogance. Go further still, and it became hubris. Those were the feelings a martial artist had to guard against most.
And if an enemy fell prey to them, you seized on that weakness to find a way out alive.
The advice had been passed down among martial artists like a maxim. Jeok Cheongang had often told me much the same thing.
But—
*This isn’t conceit.*
I knew it instinctively.
No—I was facing that monster myself. I knew better than anyone.
This wasn’t arrogance or hubris. It was certainty.
A certainty even I, who had created more possibilities and variables than anyone under heaven, couldn’t deny.
The monster who had become the Blood Lord in the truest sense approached, crushing everything around him with power and presence greater than anyone else’s on this battlefield.
*Krrr.*
The air trembled. The ground shook.
Neither the torrential rain nor the arrows loosed by archers who’d scraped together their courage atop the parts of the wall still standing could touch a hair on his head.
They had only irritated him.
*Vmmmm.*
The hundred or so arrows that had stopped above the Blood Lord’s head as though caught by an invisible hand trembled. Then their points turned.
Toward the insects who deserved to die for daring to bar the path of a monster who had drawn close to the absolute ruler.
“Get out of the way!”
The warning burst from my lips on instinct.
*Fwhoosh! Thud-thud-thud!*
The arrows streaked through the air in a flash, their fierce whistle merging into one.
Through the shield-bearers protecting the archers with iron-plated shields. Through the archers sheltering behind them.
Through everything in their path.
*Thud.*
The unit commander at the front was the first to drop to one knee.
The others stared blankly at one another.
Eyes wide with disbelief, they looked back and forth between the huge holes in their bodies and the monster standing hundreds of feet away. Then they breathed their last.
“T-This can’t be...”
*Thump. Clatter.*
One by one, bodies fell onto the ground slick with blood and rain.
Some stumbled backward in terror. Some tried to advance, refusing to accept that they were dying. Some crumpled where they stood without even a final cry.
They met death in different ways, but not one escaped it.
They all died.
Two hundred of our allies—archers, shield-bearers, even martial artists.
In a single instant.
*Slide. Splash!*
Someone whose name I didn’t know rolled down from the wall and landed in a pool of blood.
“Heaven above and earth below.”

In the suffocating silence that settled over everything, Dark Heaven’s followers had entered past the broken ranks and wall ruins that had crumbled with the Blood Lord’s arrival. As if bewitched, they began reciting their creed.
“All demons bow!”
They no longer shouted.
The killing intent they’d given off while struggling to cross the wall was gone, too.
*Shhk!*
They simply swung the blades in their hands without a word.
“Heaven above and earth below...!”
Rapture filled their faces as they marveled at the miracle before their eyes.
“All demons bow...!”
They praised the one ruler who wasn’t on this battlefield, yet could bring all under heaven to its knees from within that deep darkness.
Even if death awaited them.
*Crunch!*
“Hea—khhk. Lord of Heaven.”
Even when a stray blade cut their throats, when their arms and legs were severed, when their chests were pierced, they never lost the smiles etched across their lips.
The dozen fanatics charging at me without a hint of fear were no different.
“A-at last. The glory of martyrdom...”
*Stab! Krrrunch!*
In the end, humans were made of flesh. Once their heads were gone, they couldn’t speak.
It didn’t matter whether they’d taken a Temporary Strength Pill, drawing on strength beyond their limits at the cost of their lives, or swallowed anything else.
But why?
I’d swung my hand like a blade and taken their heads off in one stroke, yet I could still hear their unfinished words.
Over and over. Without a moment’s pause.
“These... crazy bastards.”
The curse slipped out between breaths that had somehow grown ragged.
It felt as though every drop of blood in my body had turned to ice.
I’d thought I’d seen and dealt with enough lunatics to last a lifetime.
The twenty-first-century world I’d been born and raised in had its own kind of barbarity, different from Murim’s.

Skyscrapers soared above the clouds. More than half a century had passed since humanity first ventured into space. A civilization combining cutting-edge science and Magic had grown brighter and more powerful than ever.
But none of that changed a thing.
The modern world was still full of madmen.
People were murdered in broad daylight. Judges’ gavels and reporters’ cameras swayed under the weight of money and liquor.
And that wasn’t all.
Dictators, relics of a bygone age, prepared for wars—and started them.
Plenty of people tried to bridge the distance between their religions and sects with missiles and terror instead of forgiveness and reconciliation.
In the world I’d seen, they were all fanatics.
Madmen who’d lost their minds by attaching themselves blindly to their own goals. They saw and felt only what they wanted, swaying as they got drunk on it.
Of course, the most extreme had been the fanatics who followed the Doppelganger. But now I could say this with certainty.
The madness I’d seen in them, in both its scale and its purity, was nothing next to that of the Dark Heaven followers before me.
And at the center of this bloody storm of madness, a monster came hurtling forward with the momentum of a great mountain.
“Have you ever seen moths?”
I could feel it.
The Blood Lord was at ease, but he hadn’t let his guard down.
His red eyes were fixed solely on me, as though he had no interest in the battles raging around us. They brimmed with certainty and killing intent.
“I have. Countless times, before the Tianshan Mountains fell under that person’s control. I saw those foolish things fly toward torches and burn to death.”
I didn’t answer.
Instead, I drove the shaft of White Flame, still in my grip, deep into the ground at my feet. Then I kicked up the weapons strewn around me and sent them flying at him.
*Fwoooooosh—BOOM!*
*Krrrunch!*
The blades, wreathed in Force, cut through the air one after another. Then an immense shock wave slammed into the space around them with a deafening roar.
Not where I’d aimed—the Blood Lord—but somewhere in the air and ground.
“But one day, while watching the moths, a question occurred to me.”
The Blood Lord swung his Red Blade at lightning speed, casually knocking aside everything flying toward him, and continued in a clear voice.
“Did they fly toward the torch knowing they would burn to death? Or did they fly toward it because they didn’t know?”
*Crunch!*
I cut down the enemies charging at me from every direction. After the wall, our ranks were now collapsing fast, too.
The fanatics came on crying out for martyrdom. The sight of them—and the wave of fear they stirred up—was overpowering even the effect of One Against a Thousand.
“I still haven’t found the answer. No—I never bothered looking. It wasn’t long before I met that person and gained enough power that I had no need to wonder how moths felt.”
At that moment—
*Whoooooom!*
The Blood Lord lifted his Red Blade high. A massive Force surged along its scarlet edge.
An energy unlike anything I’d ever seen—or imagined could exist.
“But I think you might know the answer.”
Certainty in himself.
Killing intent sharp as a blade. Hatred beyond anger. The elation of finally achieving his purpose.
All of it—every feeling, every ounce of his aura and power—was directed at me.
My breath caught. My hand trembled.
But I was ready.
I’d prepared the best strike I could manage. Perhaps my last.
I took a deep breath and said what had been on the tip of my tongue.
“I’m not one of them.”
“What?”
“I’m the kind of bastard who doesn’t burn to death even if he flies into the flames. Who flies in first whether he knows what’ll happen or not. That’s me.”
The silence felt like an eternity, though it lasted only an instant.
At its very end, the Blood Lord answered.
No—he moved.
So did I.
*Pop.*
More than a hundred feet of space vanished between us in an instant, and his Red Blade carved a massive blood-red line.

More than a hundred feet of space vanished between us in an instant, and his Red Blade carved a massive blood-red line.

chapters.title: Chapter 1107
paragraphs: Murim warriors spend their whole lives lingering at the crossroads of life and death.
Some live out their natural years thanks to their skill and the luck they were born with. Others get dragged into some petty squabble and die like dogs in an instant.
That was probably why.
They lived closer to death than anyone, so they’d even coined a grand term like *life-and-death duel*, trying to make their own uncertain end sound a little more solemn.
But at some point, I realized that no matter how many flowery words people used, or how many valorous titles they bestowed on one another, the nature of it never changed.
In the end, this was just a fight.
Each person gave everything they had to bring down the opponent in front of them, driven by their own cause, circumstances, or private feelings.
It could be fair. It could be unfair.
That was why it was a fight.
A simple, straightforward process: the one who was even half a step faster, ten geun stronger, and far more ruthless and calculating won.
And I knew that very well.
I knew how wide the gap was between my opponent and me. I knew the best I could do right now.
*And the worst, too.*
Watching the Blood Lord cross a dozen or so jang through the slowed world, I muttered to myself.
Did I regret this choice? Was I afraid of dying?
I didn’t know.
More precisely, I didn’t have enough time to answer.
Even in the sluggish flow of time, the Blood Lord moved like a flash of light—and I was definitely slower.
Half a step.
No. At least a full step stood between us now, a gap I could never close. It was an iron wall.
So there was nothing else I could do.
I could only charge at him like a moth.
Before that torch, reeking of blood, swallowed everyone, I had to put it out with one last beat of my wings, giving it everything I had.
*Grnnk.*
Every muscle in my body contracted at once.

At the same time, the internal energy I had left—less than a third—surged from my Lower Dantian to my Middle Dantian, then awakened the hundreds of large and small acupoints and the Eight Extraordinary Meridians lying dormant in my body.
*Hoo.*
I was so hot I felt as if I’d become a fire dragon myself. If I opened my mouth and roared, lava might pour out.
But I couldn’t do that.
I had only one chance to let that lava loose.
It wouldn’t be my first time, but it was all but certain to be my last.
The System warning chime that suddenly pierced my ears seemed to say as much.
*Beeeeeeep.*
Slowed along with the passage of time, it stretched into a long ringing, like the flatline of a heart monitor announcing a patient’s cardiac arrest. That hardly seemed an exaggeration.
One Annihilation.
The colossal mass of lava boiling up from deep within me held enough destructive power to turn even me to ash.
*Fwoooosh.*
Heat slowly surged outward, warping the space around me.
Flames that had seared my Lower Dantian, Middle Dantian, hundreds of acupoints, and Eight Extraordinary Meridians layered themselves over the spearhead.
All for one final chance.
*This is it. The only way to bring him down.*
Of course, this wasn’t the first time I’d used One Annihilation against the Blood Lord.
During the Shaolin Bloodshed, he’d taken the full force of it and still gotten back up, thanks to his incredible regenerative ability.
But an almost unfathomable gulf separated the me who’d been stuck at the Peak realm back then from the me I was now.
One Annihilation had grown just as much—powerful enough to devour even its wielder’s life.
*Unlike last time, he won’t get back up.*
One blow would render even the Blood Lord’s terrifying recovery useless.
Blue-black flames that would turn his body and even his soul to ash in an instant flickered along the spearhead of White Flame, drawn far back. And then—
*Fsssss.*
A sudden chill crept down my spine.
What was this feeling?
I was the archer. My body was the bow, and the string was already drawn all the way back.
All I had to do was let go.
All I had to do was thrust my spear at the Blood Lord, now just one jang away, as if to blow up the whole world—and it would all be over.
Then why, at the most important moment, had this inexplicable sense of wrongness come over me?
Fear of the death that was all but certain now?
Regret for the life I’d lived and the people I’d leave behind?
Or my life flashing before my eyes as I sensed the end?
No.
That wasn’t it.
This feeling was different from any of those I’d experienced before.
It was a warning.
A signal from the other me—the one that followed nothing but instinct.
And at last, the moment reason and instinct met inside me—
Time, held back until now, and everything around me—the noise and the surroundings—came crashing down all at once, like a massive wave breaking through a dam.
Through it all, a blurred afterimage flashed between the Blood Lord and me as we shot toward each other.
*Fwoooosh!*
From outside my field of vision came a fierce whistle, cutting through the wind and rain.
I realized too late that someone was there, clad from head to toe in pitch-black armor. No—*something*.
The blood in my body turned cold.
*Black Ghost...!*
So that was it.
That was what the unease I’d felt earlier meant.
The card the Blood Lord had kept hidden until the very end. He had grown stronger than before, and his planning had grown sharper still.
*He planned it. He’d been waiting for this moment from the start.*
The realization struck like lightning through my skull.
Only then did I understand.
It wasn’t the Blood Lord who’d let his guard down. It was me.
The other side could learn from past mistakes, too.

Despite his inhuman regenerative ability and overwhelming martial prowess, the Blood Lord had waited for One Annihilation until the very last moment, then put the Black Ghost he’d kept hidden in front of him as a shield.
As if he wouldn’t allow even the smallest variable.
And the price of my carelessness was shoving me hard in the back, right at the edge of a cliff.
There was no other way.
I’d already come too far to turn back.
“Damn it.”
With no choices left, I spat out the curse I’d been holding back and thrust my spear forward. My entire past and future rested on its tip.
*Gooooom.*
Space warped.
The fire dragon’s flames let out a tremendous roar, flooding everything I could see in blue-black.
At the last moment, as that dreadful heat was about to devour everything in its path, a streak of light swept past the Black Ghost like an apparition.
*Shhk.*
A faint sound of air being cut—so faint I wouldn’t have heard it if my senses hadn’t been sharper than ever.
And it wasn’t an apparition or a hallucination.
One Annihilation.
When that terrifying strike—the one that had briefly cornered him in the not-so-distant past—shot toward him, the Blood Lord thought:
*It’s over.*
Certainty in a life-and-death duel was no different from poison.
But even he, who’d endlessly turned over the final moments of the four Demon Lords and the Demon Empress who had fallen to Jin Taekyung, couldn’t help feeling certain now.
Blazing Flame Divine Dragon Jin Taekyung.
His sickening history with that damned brat, who made him feel foul just to think about, ended here.
The plan was perfect. It was as good as done.
*You’ll never kill me.*
There was no mistaking it: Jin Taekyung had grown beyond recognition.
And so, the Blood Lord had no doubt that the strike he couldn’t begin to understand had grown terrifyingly powerful, too.
It had become so powerful that even the Blood Lord, who now considered himself all but immortal, had thought of death when he felt the unprecedented energy wrapped around the spearhead.
But this was as far as it went.
*The lion uses all its strength, even when hunting a rabbit.*
Even a predator gives everything it has to catch a single rabbit.

It had taken the loss of an arm and a long period of humiliation for the Blood Lord to learn that lesson and put it into practice. But thanks to that, he could avoid the sharp teeth the rabbit had hidden.
The one Black Ghost he’d kept by his side for this moment alone.

He’d sent as many as eight Black Ghosts to the three gates other than the West Gate, then entered through the breached wall alone. It was all to pin down the enemy and make that brat let his guard down.
So Jin Taekyung would focus solely on him.
So he would believe the Blood Lord was his only enemy.
And the Blood Lord’s plan had worked.
No—more accurately, he thought it had worked.

The vast flames bursting from the spearhead swallowed the space around them. At that moment, a streak of light flew in from somewhere and swept past the Black Ghost that had moved between Jin Taekyung and the Blood Lord at his command.
*Shhk.*
*...What?*
A ripple of shock disturbed the Blood Lord’s unwavering gaze.
His eyes trembled, then slowly turned to the Black Ghost’s neck as it rose into the air.
In the gap between the two halves of its body, separated by empty space, a handful of purple Force scattered like flower petals.
*That’s...*
There was no mistaking it.
That distinctive light, spreading like plum blossoms or the colors of the sunset, belonged to the Zaha Divine Technique alone.
Staring blankly at the scene, stunned as if the world had stopped, the Blood Lord remembered a face he’d momentarily forgotten.
The man bore a striking resemblance to the one who had taken his arm. Yet he’d vanished from the battlefield so anticlimactically that he’d hardly seemed worthy of inheriting that man’s teachings.
But before the Blood Lord could speak the other brat’s name, the blue-black flames swallowed the Black Ghost’s body without a trace—and engulfed him.
*KWA-AAAAA!*
A colossal pillar of fire surged upward, sweeping across heaven and earth.

chapters.title: Chapter 1108
paragraphs: He was dead.
No—he’d thought he was dead.
Fifteen minutes earlier, the young man who had rushed in front of Jin Taekyung, lost in a Trance and unable to sense the danger, had been certain he was about to die.
But he hadn’t.
A blood-red flash charged with an unprecedented force had struck him, followed by a tremendous impact that battered his entire body.
When he finally opened his eyes, clinging to the thread of consciousness that had briefly been severed, the young man buried beneath a pile of stones—or rather, Cheongpung—muttered to himself:
*This is the most dangerous thing I’ve ever been through... No, it isn’t.*
If this had happened before—more precisely, if he hadn’t gone through what happened on Mount Song—he might have trembled with fear.

Overwhelmed by the terror of death, something he’d never experienced before, and frozen by the killing intent and madness he’d never felt amid the clear streams and plum blossoms of Lotus Peak, he might have been unable to move.
But—
*I have to move.*
Things were different now.
The child who had wandered through Huashan’s beautiful scenery had entered the martial world and learned how to run.
He’d faced the world’s ugliness and learned what anger felt like. He’d spent time with good people and come to understand what it meant to do right by others.
So even knowing that countless threats and hardships awaited him, he could rise again.
That was the right path his grandfather had raised him to follow. It was the chivalry he had learned from watching Jin Taekyung.
*Go. To my Benefactor. To them.*
Cheongpung pushed himself to his feet, unsteady.
He shoved aside the stones weighing down his body and endured the pain of bones broken here and there, moving slowly.
And more stealthily than ever before.
“You want me to teach you martial arts?”
Perhaps it was the blood trickling from the large and small wounds etched across his body. In his wavering vision, a conversation he’d once had with the Slaughter Saint seemed to echo in his ears.
“Do you even know what you’re asking?”
“Uh, I think so.”
“Unbelievable. The Sword Saint’s Disciple, of all people, wants to become a mere assassin.”
“Huh?”
“You idiot. I don’t practice martial arts. I practice the art of killing. It’s not for someone like you.”
Back then, the Slaughter Saint had shaken his head with a bitter smile.
At least, until he heard Cheongpung’s reply.
“Huh. I don’t think so.”
“What?”

“My grandfather told me it’s not the tool that matters, but the person holding it. And there was an assassin I saw a long time ago who didn’t seem like the kind of person who’d hurt someone for no reason.”
“Oh, and he said everyone I cross paths with in this world could become my teacher and Benefactor.”
“Please take care of me, Granduncle!”
Remembering how the Slaughter Saint had silently watched him, then spoken with an expression that grew complicated, Cheongpung let out a quiet breath.
*Hoo.*
His heart, pounding from pain and blood loss, grew calm. The blood flowing from his wounds gradually stopped, and he erased all trace of his presence.
“It won’t be easy to master even one technique. You don’t have the time, and the situation won’t allow for it.”
“Wow, so you’re saying yes, right? You are, aren’t you?”
“Damn it. Fine. But I have one condition.”
“A condition?”
“Never call me that again.”
“Yes, Little Master!”
“Damn it.”
“Oh. Sorry, Granduncle.”
“...Where in the world did the Sword Saint pick up a lunatic like you?”
The Slaughter Saint probably hadn’t known.
Before even a month of their journey had passed, he would ask that question again—but mean something entirely different by it.
“...Where in the world did the Sword Saint pick up a lunatic like this?”
“Grandpa said a stork brought me. My Benefactor said it was ovulation, fertilization, and implantation, but I couldn’t make heads or tails of it.”
“...I really can’t understand.”
“Right? I’d never heard such bizarre words in my life.”
“...It’s my first time, too. Seeing anything this bizarre.”
The Slaughter Saint’s bewildered face rose before Cheongpung’s eyes.
At the same moment, Cheongpung’s feet, now as light as feathers, touched a pool of blood.
No—they barely brushed it.
*Shhk.*
Ghost Illusory Slaughter Step.
The unique footwork technique created by the greatest assassin of all time—so stealthy that no other technique under heaven could match it—unfolded beneath Cheongpung’s feet.
“You were right, Granduncle. This really isn’t easy.”
“...Is that something someone who reached three-tenths mastery in only a month should be saying?”
It was the unique technique of none other than the Slaughter Saint, known as the greatest assassin of all time.
And yet Cheongpung had mastered Ghost Illusory Slaughter Step at a dazzling speed.
For someone else, a month might have been *only* a month. For him, it was a *whole* month.
“I like martial arts. A whole, whole lot.”
“That much I know... This is driving me mad. How is this even possible?”
It was possible.
To Cheongpung, all of it came as naturally as breathing.
He watched with his eyes and moved with his body, and before he knew it, the technique became his.
Not merely copied: it was reborn with Cheongpung’s own character woven into it, a new martial art that belonged to him alone.
*Whoosh.*
Cheongpung moved forward.
His steps were neither fast nor slow. With each one, it seemed that the fragrance of plum blossoms, perceptible only to him, spread through the air.
Dark Fragrance Drift.

The fragrance of Huashan’s plum blossoms spread through the pouring rain. Joined with Ghost Illusory Slaughter Step, which Cheongpung had brought to nine-tenths mastery over the past six months with the Slaughter Saint, it had grown quieter and more elusive still.
So much so that even with both eyes open, no one could clearly make out his presence.
*Shh-shh-shh-shhk!*
“Graaagh!”
*Stab! Slice!*
“Heaven above and earth below; all demons—Guh!”
The fighting all around had spun beyond anyone’s control, yet no one properly noticed Cheongpung slipping past them.
As he crossed the heart of the battlefield, he blended naturally into everything around him.

He was the rain falling ceaselessly over everyone’s heads. He was a Dark Heaven fanatic, drunk on madness and the effects of a Temporary Strength Pill—and he was one of the martial artists and soldiers trying to stop them.
He was a part of this chaotic battlefield, and the battlefield itself.
Moving in only one direction, toward only one person.
*Benefactor.*
Cheongpung saw him.
*Gooooom.*
Space warped as if gripped by an invisible hand. Jin Taekyung was about to unleash an appallingly immense force all at once.
The Blood Lord was charging toward him, while a pitch-black figure lunged from his blind spot as though it had been waiting for this very moment.
*Too late.*
His instincts whispered it to him.
It was a shame, but this wasn’t enough.
Cheongpung had neither the strength to bring down the Blood Lord nor the time.
But—
*He can do it. My Benefactor can.*
That wasn’t a guess. It was certainty.
His faith in Jin Taekyung didn’t waver in the slightest.
So Cheongpung shot forward without hesitation.
Toward the enormous flames erupting in a blinding flash.
Toward the Black Ghost, which had thrown its own body in the way as a shield to counter that unprecedented force.
*Fwoosh.*
Time slowed. Space disappeared.
Just before One Annihilation was unleashed, a flash slipped between his tightly shut eyelids and pierced his retinas like a needle.
But Cheongpung could feel it clearly.
The Black Ghost at the end of his path.
The single line his strike was drawing toward that pitiful being.
And then—
*Shhk.*
The moment he passed the Black Ghost with a cut almost too quiet to hear, a lightning-like shiver surged up his spine.
A shiver that wouldn’t fade, not even in the dreadful heat swallowing the space he had just crossed.
*I did it.*
At the same moment, a colossal fire dragon swallowed the Black Ghost’s body as it tilted helplessly.
No—more precisely, it swallowed the blood-red monster charging from behind it.
*KWA-AAAAA!*
Even as the overwhelming shock wave swept him away, Cheongpung laughed aloud.
He watched the Red Blade shatter beneath the pillar of fire that had finally burst forth.
But he didn’t know.
At that very moment, one person was watching the blue-black flames dye everything around them.
Jin Taekyung’s face had gone colder than ever.
*Cough.*
His skin had gone deathly pale, his eyes growing cloudy.
Yet even as he coughed up a doe of blood, Jin Taekyung forced his heavy eyelids open and watched the wave of fire he had unleashed.
He took in the surest information he could get—something only he could hear.
*Beep! Be-be-beep!*
He’d poured everything he had into that strike.
With a body emptied of strength and senses gone dry, he tried to understand what was happening.
But he couldn’t see or hear.
It wasn’t in any of the countless holographic windows floating before him. It wasn’t among the System warnings sounding without pause in his ears.
The clear chime announcing the enemy’s death never came.
Not even as his legs gave way beneath him, the spear shaft the only thing keeping him upright.
*Splash.*
And as Jin Taekyung’s knees plunged into a pool of blood—
*Drip. Drip.*
From within the wave of fire that had engulfed a radius of dozens of jang, the monster’s charred body rose to its feet.
Thirst.
That was the first thing the Blood Lord felt when he regained consciousness.
*What the hell happened?*
He didn’t know. He couldn’t know.
He remembered nothing.
He couldn’t even recall who he was or what kind of life he’d lived.
Only the instinct to quench this terrible thirst remained, controlling his body.
*Scuff.*
His unsteady footsteps sounded as dry as if he were walking through a desert.
Why?
The Blood Lord wondered blankly.
He’d been sure there was something somewhere around here that could quench his thirst.
He’d been sure of it.
*Why?*
He turned his head and looked around, but he couldn’t see anything. His senses had failed, his retinas burned away, trapping him in pitch-black darkness.
All he could make out was a faint sound.
A strange noise.
Yes, he remembered. Screams and the sound of steel scraping against steel.
And then, from the unknown thing that touched his skin, came a feeling that was familiar—and strangely dear.
*Splash.*
At that moment, forgotten sensations and memories awoke.
Something hot, wet, and sticky.
The Blood Lord remembered what this utterly familiar thing was.
*Blood.*
Something inside the human body. The source of his strength—and the only liquid that could quench his thirst now.
*I’m thirsty.*
Strange. Just thinking it was enough for him to feel the blood splattered across his body seeping into him.
As it did, his senses gradually sharpened.
But—
*More. Give me more.*
This wasn’t nearly enough.
He needed far, far more blood.
“More!”
With the cry already escaping his lips, the Blood Lord swept his hand out with all his strength.
*Grab.*
At last, his fingertips touched someone’s shoulder. At the same time, a voice rang more clearly in his ears, echoing like a distant sound.
“Blood Lord! Your subordinates will protect you—!”
But before the desperate voice could finish, the Blood Lord’s teeth, already grown, sank into the man’s throat.

sentences.text: He was dead.
No—he’d thought he was dead.
Fifteen minutes earlier, the young man who had rushed in front of Jin Taekyung, lost in a Trance and unable to sense the danger, had been certain he was about to die.
But he hadn’t.
A blood-red flash charged with an unprecedented force had struck him, followed by a tremendous impact that battered his entire body.
When he finally opened his eyes, clinging to the thread of consciousness that had briefly been severed, the young man buried beneath a pile of stones—or rather, Cheongpung—muttered to himself:
*This is the most dangerous thing I’ve ever been through...
No, it isn’t.*
If this had happened before—more precisely, if he hadn’t gone through what happened on Mount Song—he might have trembled with fear.

Overwhelmed by the terror of death, something he’d never experienced before, and frozen by the killing intent and madness he’d never felt amid the clear streams and plum blossoms of Lotus Peak, he might have been unable to move.
But—
*I have to move.*
Things were different now.
The child who had wandered through Huashan’s beautiful scenery had entered the martial world and learned how to run.
He’d faced the world’s ugliness and learned what anger felt like.
He’d spent time with good people and come to understand what it meant to do right by others.
So even knowing that countless threats and hardships awaited him, he could rise again.
That was the right path his grandfather had raised him to follow.
It was the chivalry he had learned from watching Jin Taekyung.
*Go.
To my Benefactor.
To them.*
Cheongpung pushed himself to his feet, unsteady.
He shoved aside the stones weighing down his body and endured the pain of bones broken here and there, moving slowly.
And more stealthily than ever before.
“You want me to teach you martial arts?”
Perhaps it was the blood trickling from the large and small wounds etched across his body.
In his wavering vision, a conversation he’d once had with the Slaughter Saint seemed to echo in his ears.
“Do you even know what you’re asking?”
“Uh, I think so.”
“Unbelievable.
The Sword Saint’s Disciple, of all people, wants to become a mere assassin.”
“Huh?”
“You idiot.
I don’t practice martial arts.
I practice the art of killing.
It’s not for someone like you.”
Back then, the Slaughter Saint had shaken his head with a bitter smile.
At least, until he heard Cheongpung’s reply.
“Huh.
I don’t think so.”
“What?”
“My grandfather told me it’s not the tool that matters, but the person holding it.
And there was an assassin I saw a long time ago who didn’t seem like the kind of person who’d hurt someone for no reason.”
“Oh, and he said everyone I cross paths with in this world could become my teacher and Benefactor.”
“Please take care of me, Granduncle!”
Remembering how the Slaughter Saint had silently watched him, then spoken with an expression that grew complicated, Cheongpung let out a quiet breath.
*Hoo.*
His heart, pounding from pain and blood loss, grew calm.
The blood flowing from his wounds gradually stopped, and he erased all trace of his presence.
“It won’t be easy to master even one technique.
You don’t have the time, and the situation won’t allow for it.”
“Wow, so you’re saying yes, right?
You are, aren’t you?”
“Damn it.
Fine.
But I have one condition.”
“A condition?”
“Never call me that again.”
“Yes, Little Master!”
“Damn it.”
“Oh.
Sorry, Granduncle.”
“...Where in the world did the Sword Saint pick up a lunatic like you?”
The Slaughter Saint probably hadn’t known.
Before even a month of their journey had passed, he would ask that question again—but mean something entirely different by it.
“...Where in the world did the Sword Saint pick up a lunatic like this?”
“Grandpa said a stork brought me.
My Benefactor said it was ovulation, fertilization, and implantation, but I couldn’t make heads or tails of it.”
“...I really can’t understand.”
“Right?
I’d never heard such bizarre words in my life.”
“...It’s my first time, too.
Seeing anything this bizarre.”
The Slaughter Saint’s bewildered face rose before Cheongpung’s eyes.
At the same moment, Cheongpung’s feet, now as light as feathers, touched a pool of blood.
No—they barely brushed it.
*Shhk.*
Ghost Illusory Slaughter Step.
The unique footwork technique created by the greatest assassin of all time—so stealthy that no other technique under heaven could match it—unfolded beneath Cheongpung’s feet.
“You were right, Granduncle.
This really isn’t easy.”
“...Is that something someone who reached three-tenths mastery in only a month should be saying?”
It was the unique technique of none other than the Slaughter Saint, known as the greatest assassin of all time.
And yet Cheongpung had mastered Ghost Illusory Slaughter Step at a dazzling speed.
For someone else, a month might have been *only* a month.
For him, it was a *whole* month.
“I like martial arts.
A whole, whole lot.”
“That much I know...
This is driving me mad.
How is this even possible?”
It was possible.
To Cheongpung, all of it came as naturally as breathing.
He watched with his eyes and moved with his body, and before he knew it, the technique became his.
Not merely copied: it was reborn with Cheongpung’s own character woven into it, a new martial art that belonged to him alone.
*Whoosh.*
Cheongpung moved forward.
His steps were neither fast nor slow.
With each one, it seemed that the fragrance of plum blossoms, perceptible only to him, spread through the air.
Dark Fragrance Drift.
The fragrance of Huashan’s plum blossoms spread through the pouring rain.
Joined with Ghost Illusory Slaughter Step, which Cheongpung had brought to nine-tenths mastery over the past six months with the Slaughter Saint, it had grown quieter and more elusive still.
So much so that even with both eyes open, no one could clearly make out his presence.
*Shh-shh-shh-shhk!*
“Graaagh!”
*Stab!
Slice!*
“Heaven above and earth below; all demons—Guh!”
The fighting all around had spun beyond anyone’s control, yet no one properly noticed Cheongpung slipping past them.
As he crossed the heart of the battlefield, he blended naturally into everything around him.
He was the rain falling ceaselessly over everyone’s heads.
He was a Dark Heaven fanatic, drunk on madness and the effects of a Temporary Strength Pill—and he was one of the martial artists and soldiers trying to stop them.
He was a part of this chaotic battlefield, and the battlefield itself.
Moving in only one direction, toward only one person.
*Benefactor.*
Cheongpung saw him.
*Gooooom.*
Space warped as if gripped by an invisible hand.
Jin Taekyung was about to unleash an appallingly immense force all at once.
The Blood Lord was charging toward him, while a pitch-black figure lunged from his blind spot as though it had been waiting for this very moment.
*Too late.*
His instincts whispered it to him.
It was a shame, but this wasn’t enough.
Cheongpung had neither the strength to bring down the Blood Lord nor the time.
But—
*He can do it.
My Benefactor can.*
That wasn’t a guess.
It was certainty.
His faith in Jin Taekyung didn’t waver in the slightest.
So Cheongpung shot forward without hesitation.
Toward the enormous flames erupting in a blinding flash.
Toward the Black Ghost, which had thrown its own body in the way as a shield to counter that unprecedented force.
*Fwoosh.*
Time slowed.
Space disappeared.
Just before One Annihilation was unleashed, a flash slipped between his tightly shut eyelids and pierced his retinas like a needle.
But Cheongpung could feel it clearly.
The Black Ghost at the end of his path.
The single line his strike was drawing toward that pitiful being.
And then—
*Shhk.*
The moment he passed the Black Ghost with a cut almost too quiet to hear, a lightning-like shiver surged up his spine.
A shiver that wouldn’t fade, not even in the dreadful heat swallowing the space he had just crossed.
*I did it.*
At the same moment, a colossal fire dragon swallowed the Black Ghost’s body as it tilted helplessly.
No—more precisely, it swallowed the blood-red monster charging from behind it.
*KWA-AAAAA!*
Even as the overwhelming shock wave swept him away, Cheongpung laughed aloud.
He watched the Red Blade shatter beneath the pillar of fire that had finally burst forth.
But he didn’t know.
At that very moment, one person was watching the blue-black flames dye everything around them.
Jin Taekyung’s face had gone colder than ever.
*Cough.*
His skin had gone deathly pale, his eyes growing cloudy.
Yet even as he coughed up a doe of blood, Jin Taekyung forced his heavy eyelids open and watched the wave of fire he had unleashed.
He took in the surest information he could get—something only he could hear.
*Beep!
Be-be-beep!*
He’d poured everything he had into that strike.
With a body emptied of strength and senses gone dry, he tried to understand what was happening.
But he couldn’t see or hear.
It wasn’t in any of the countless holographic windows floating before him.
It wasn’t among the System warnings sounding without pause in his ears.
The clear chime announcing the enemy’s death never came.
Not even as his legs gave way beneath him, the spear shaft the only thing keeping him upright.
*Splash.*
And as Jin Taekyung’s knees plunged into a pool of blood—
*Drip.
Drip.*
From within the wave of fire that had engulfed a radius of dozens of jang, the monster’s charred body rose to its feet.
Thirst.
That was the first thing the Blood Lord felt when he regained consciousness.
*What the hell happened?*
He didn’t know.
He couldn’t know.
He remembered nothing.
He couldn’t even recall who he was or what kind of life he’d lived.
Only the instinct to quench this terrible thirst remained, controlling his body.
*Scuff.*
His unsteady footsteps sounded as dry as if he were walking through a desert.
Why?
The Blood Lord wondered blankly.
He’d been sure there was something somewhere around here that could quench his thirst.
He’d been sure of it.
*Why?*
He turned his head and looked around, but he couldn’t see anything.
His senses had failed, his retinas burned away, trapping him in pitch-black darkness.
All he could make out was a faint sound.
A strange noise.
Yes, he remembered.
Screams and the sound of steel scraping against steel.
And then, from the unknown thing that touched his skin, came a feeling that was familiar—and strangely dear.
*Splash.*
At that moment, forgotten sensations and memories awoke.
Something hot, wet, and sticky.
The Blood Lord remembered what this utterly familiar thing was.
*Blood.*
Something inside the human body.
The source of his strength—and the only liquid that could quench his thirst now.
*I’m thirsty.*
Strange.
Just thinking it was enough for him to feel the blood splattered across his body seeping into him.
As it did, his senses gradually sharpened.
But—
*More.
Give me more.*
This wasn’t nearly enough.
He needed far, far more blood.
“More!”
With the cry already escaping his lips, the Blood Lord swept his hand out with all his strength.
*Grab.*
At last, his fingertips touched someone’s shoulder.
At the same time, a voice rang more clearly in his ears, echoing like a distant sound.
“Blood Lord!
Your subordinates will protect you—!”
But before the desperate voice could finish, the Blood Lord’s teeth, already grown, sank into the man’s throat.
*Crunch!*
He chewed and swallowed.

To quench his thirst.
Only then did the world around the monster grow bright.

chapters.title: Chapter 1109
paragraphs: The moment fierce flames swept through the battlefield, everyone—ally and enemy alike—thought the Blood Lord was dead.
That was how much power the strike had contained.
Even with his near-immortal regenerative ability, surviving that dreadful, hellish heat had seemed impossible.
But there was one exception.
Jin Taekyung had used even his own life as kindling to summon those flames.
*Splash.*
His knee sank into a pool of blood. Beyond the drifting ashes, the monster that had stopped just short of death began to rise.
Then a single shout burst from Jin Taekyung’s lips, now pale as snow. He wrung it out with every ounce of strength he had left.
“Attack!”
The azure dragon’s roar shook the air on every side, breaking the momentary silence and setting time in motion again.
The first to respond was another Divine Dragon, still hurtling away after being caught in the aftermath of One Annihilation.
Cheongpung’s eyes flew open.
The thrill and elation he’d felt just after cutting off the Black Ghost’s head were gone.
Only overwhelming shock and confusion rushed in to take their place.
*How is this even possible...!*
He couldn’t believe what he was seeing. But he had no choice but to accept it.
Gritting his teeth, Cheongpung twisted around.
*Whoosh.*
His body spun against the howling wind. He thrust out a foot and stepped into empty air.
No—he made it burst.
*Boom!*
Compressed air exploded.
The distance of some twenty jang closed in an instant, bringing the staggering monster sharply into view.
*I’ll kill him. No matter what!*
Cheongpung’s mind was cold as ice.
His instincts were screaming at him. If he didn’t stop that terrible monster now, he might never get another chance.
He had to bring the creature down by any means necessary, before it recovered its original strength.
But another group of monsters awaited his descending sword. They went by a different name: fanatics.
“Stop him!”
“Heaven above and earth below; all demons—!”
*Sh-sh-sh-shhk! Slice!*
Purple Force flowed along Cheongpung’s blade, cutting through flesh and bone without hesitation.
Thirty-Six Plum Blossom Swords.
Huashan’s finest sword technique filled the air. Along the path traced by his blade, the Force of the Zaha Divine Technique blossomed and scattered like petals.
Beautiful, and sorrowful.
And more than anything, desperate.
*Thud! Fwoosh!*
He cut, and cut, and cut again.
They fell, and fell, and fell again.
But—
*They’re not backing down...*
Cheongpung’s face turned pale.
Everything around him was stained red. Blood poured out without pause, washing away the fragrance of his sword technique and obscuring the purple Force.
The defenders who had joined the fight were swinging their weapons with the resolve to die, but even so, the wall of fanatics held firm.
To them, death—the thing every living person feared—was sacred martyrdom.
“The great Lord of Heaven’s power has descended upon this land! We will give our lives to protect His Apostle!”
“Lord of Heaven, lead us!”
The fanatics’ spirits had never been higher than after witnessing the Blood Lord survive.
No—this had gone beyond madness.
To others, his survival was a strange and terrible calamity. To the fanatics, it was a miracle proving their faith had been right all along.
And amid that whirlpool of madness and death, Cheongpung could see the monster clearly.
A monster slowly retreating from the jaws of death, absorbing the blood of friend and foe pouring in from every direction.
*Rustle.*
New flesh began to grow over its charred body.
*Crack.*
Melted bone and muscle regenerated.
*Pop. Pop.*
Its lips, fused together above and below, came apart to reveal sharp white teeth.
A long, blood-red tongue flicked out between them, driven by an unbearable thirst.
“...More. Give me more.”
The moment a voice like scraping metal slipped from the monster’s parched lips, Cheongpung felt the blood in his whole body turn cold.
*Already?*
The sight was bizarre beyond words, and the recovery was far too fast. It was well beyond what he and the other allies had expected.
For a moment, he wondered whether they would be better off falling back, if that could delay the monster’s recovery even a little.
But even in that fleeting moment, the mindless monster was regaining its original strength at an astonishing rate.
“More!”
The Blood Lord’s sudden cry sent a shiver down Cheongpung’s spine.
Because his voice was so much clearer now?
No.
It was the majestic internal energy carried in that cry—something Cheongpung hadn’t been able to feel just moments ago.
*No!*
With that silent scream, Cheongpung thrust his sword forward with all his strength.
*Sh-sh-sh-shhk!*
Force brighter than ever slashed through the air.
The fanatics blocking his way, endlessly chanting their eight-character incantation, were cut to pieces and scattered.
A breakthrough aimed at a single point.
Jeong Hogun and the Embroidered Uniform Guards under his command, now among the defenders, charged in behind him.
“Wipe out the rebels!”
“Long live His Majesty the Emperor!”
They were the Great Nation’s finest troops in every sense, each a martial artist of at least Supreme First Rate, with others at Peak.
They had cast aside the golden armor and helmets bestowed by the Son of Heaven, but their pride and their vows still shone. Every sword point drove in the same direction.
Toward the Blood Lord.
*Fwoooosh! Boom!*
A deafening crash sent a thick spray of blood surging through the air.
A narrow gap began to open among the countless fanatics, whose ranks had seemed like an unbreakable iron wall.
*Slice! Thud-thud-thud!*
Even with Temporary Strength Pills, they could not close the gap in martial enlightenment.
Dozens of Huashan’s finest techniques poured from Cheongpung’s blade, while the Embroidered Uniform Guards, led by Jeong Hogun, drove into the fanatics’ formation like an awl.
Before another enemy could fill the gap.
So they could get one step closer, one moment sooner, to the Blood Lord.
*At this rate, we can do it.*
No—they had to do it.
They all thought so, and they were all prepared to die.
The Kunlun Sect Daoist who, even with a sword buried in his chest, used his last strength to wrap his arms around a fanatic.
The young, nameless soldier behind him, squeezing his eyes shut as he thrust his spear.
The middle-aged Embroidered Uniform Guard, holding in the entrails spilling from his split abdomen as he advanced, clad in pride that shone brighter than his armor.
They all knew it instinctively.
If they let the chance Jin Taekyung had given them slip away, they might never bring that monster down.
If the West Gate fell, they would be slaughtered—and so would the hundreds of thousands of people sheltering in the Inner City.
Their unshakable, desperate resolve shot toward the wall of fanaticism like the spear of someone kneeling behind them.
“Now!”
At Cheongpung’s shout, every ally who had pushed deep into enemy lines squeezed out their remaining strength and lunged forward.
It might be their final charge. None of them would regret it.
*Crack-crack-crack!*
Fountains of blood burst into the air.
Cries of pain spilled from every direction, and the bodies of allies and enemies alike tangled together as they crumpled.
But it was enough.
Countless fanatics still surrounded them. Right now, though, Cheongpung had only one target.
*Crunch. Crunch.*
The monster was chewing something Cheongpung couldn’t identify—and didn’t want to. It suddenly turned to look at him.
It had two arms and two legs like a human, but could no longer be called one. In its red hand hung a corpse with its neck gone.
Dozens more bodies lay at its feet: fanatics dried out like mummies.
“Who are you?”
It looked and sounded genuinely curious.
Cheongpung didn’t know why the monster couldn’t remember him, but one thing was certain.
*He still hasn’t fully recovered.*
Watching his reflection in those blood-red pupils, Cheongpung spat out his answer, his voice more hostile than ever.
“You don’t deserve to hear my name.”
And at that moment—
*Flash.*
Cheongpung’s hand moved faster than sound. Purple light burst from his fingertips.
*Slice!*
Skin split, and blood flew.
The Blood Lord stared at Cheongpung in bewilderment, then blinked as he noticed the deep gash across his chest.
With the pain, forgotten memories began to rise slowly to the surface.
And with them came anger.
He reached out as though in a trance.
But before he could recover his memories, Cheongpung was already moving without hesitation.
*Slice, slice, slice!*
They moved at a speed like streaks of light, their bodies tangling and crossing. Each time they did, blood sprayed into the air.
The Blood Lord’s blood.
*Drip-drip-drip.*
Watching his own blood spatter across the ground, the Blood Lord’s eyes widened.
It wasn’t the pain.
Thirst.
The more blood he lost, the tighter that terrible thirst—briefly quenched—closed around him again.
*Sh-sh-sh-shhk!*
Even as sword strikes rained down like a storm, the Blood Lord looked around, his thirst growing stronger.
*I need it. Blood. I need more.*
But Cheongpung was pouring his last strength into the attack, giving him no time to quench it.
*Crack! Crunch!*
Blood flowed everywhere as the battle went on, but it wasn’t nearly enough. It could only close the wounds appearing across his body, one after another.
But he had remembered something else he’d briefly forgotten.
Other beings that could quench his thirst.
*Right. That’s right.*
The Blood Lord grinned, unable to contain his delight.
He raised both hands toward the sky and cried out eagerly.
“Come! Hurry!”
At that instant—
*Whoosh!*
The purple Force Cheongpung had sent flying grazed the Blood Lord’s arm as he paused for an instant.
No—it cut through both arms.
*Slice!*
Both arms flew high into the air. Pain and thirst surged through him at once.
But even after losing the arms he had barely regenerated, the Blood Lord kept smiling.
He knew what the countless shadows plunging down toward him would do. They blocked even the heavy rain pouring over his head, turning an already dark sky utterly black.
They would quench his thirst.
*Kiiieeet!*
At the bloodcurdling sound that suddenly rang out from the air, Cheongpung instinctively looked up.
He saw them.
No. Everyone saw it clearly.
Countless flying beasts—too many to count—plunged toward the battlefield, their blood-red eyes flashing.
And at the center of them all, at the very end, was one being.
*Flap-flap-flap!*
A wave of monstrous creatures no one could block or evade.
Beyond the thunder of countless wings beating as they poured down and covered the space, the voice of the monster who had finally regained all his strength and memories pierced Cheongpung’s ears.
“I remember your name.”
“And the debt I owe that bastard Mae Jonghak, the Sword Saint.”
At that moment—
*Crack-crack-crack!*
Flesh and bone tore with a sickening sound, and sticky blood stained Cheongpung’s vision red.

Their unshakable, desperate resolve shot toward the wall of fanaticism like the spear of someone kneeling behind them.
“Now!”
At Cheongpung’s shout, every ally who had pushed deep into enemy lines squeezed out their remaining strength and lunged forward.
It might be their final charge.
None of them would regret it.
*Crack-crack-crack!*
Fountains of blood burst into the air.
Cries of pain spilled from every direction, and the bodies of allies and enemies alike tangled together as they crumpled.
But it was enough.
Countless fanatics still surrounded them.
Right now, though, Cheongpung had only one target.
*Crunch.
Crunch.*
The monster was chewing something Cheongpung couldn’t identify—and didn’t want to.
It suddenly turned to look at him.
It had two arms and two legs like a human, but could no longer be called one.
In its red hand hung a corpse with its neck gone.
Dozens more bodies lay at its feet: fanatics dried out like mummies.
“Who are you?”
It looked and sounded genuinely curious.
Cheongpung didn’t know why the monster couldn’t remember him, but one thing was certain.
*He still hasn’t fully recovered.*
Watching his reflection in those blood-red pupils, Cheongpung spat out his answer, his voice more hostile than ever.
“You don’t deserve to hear my name.”
And at that moment—
*Flash.*
Cheongpung’s hand moved faster than sound.
Purple light burst from his fingertips.
*Slice!*
Skin split, and blood flew.
The Blood Lord stared at Cheongpung in bewilderment, then blinked as he noticed the deep gash across his chest.
With the pain, forgotten memories began to rise slowly to the surface.
And with them came anger.
He reached out as though in a trance.
But before he could recover his memories, Cheongpung was already moving without hesitation.
*Slice, slice, slice!*
They moved at a speed like streaks of light, their bodies tangling and crossing.
Each time they did, blood sprayed into the air.
The Blood Lord’s blood.
*Drip-drip-drip.*
Watching his own blood spatter across the ground, the Blood Lord’s eyes widened.
It wasn’t the pain.
Thirst.
The more blood he lost, the tighter that terrible thirst—briefly quenched—closed around him again.
*Sh-sh-sh-shhk!*
Even as sword strikes rained down like a storm, the Blood Lord looked around, his thirst growing stronger.
*I need it.
Blood.
I need more.*
But Cheongpung was pouring his last strength into the attack, giving him no time to quench it.
*Crack!
Crunch!*
Blood flowed everywhere as the battle went on, but it wasn’t nearly enough.
It could only close the wounds appearing across his body, one after another.
But he had remembered something else he’d briefly forgotten.
Other beings that could quench his thirst.
*Right.
That’s right.*
The Blood Lord grinned, unable to contain his delight.
He raised both hands toward the sky and cried out eagerly.
“Come!
Hurry!”
At that instant—
*Whoosh!*
The purple Force Cheongpung had sent flying grazed the Blood Lord’s arm as he paused for an instant.
No—it cut through both arms.
*Slice!*
Both arms flew high into the air.
Pain and thirst surged through him at once.
But even after losing the arms he had barely regenerated, the Blood Lord kept smiling.
He knew what the countless shadows plunging down toward him would do.
They blocked even the heavy rain pouring over his head, turning an already dark sky utterly black.
They would quench his thirst.
*Kiiieeet!*
At the bloodcurdling sound that suddenly rang out from the air, Cheongpung instinctively looked up.
He saw them.
No.
Everyone saw it clearly.
Countless flying beasts—too many to count—plunged toward the battlefield, their blood-red eyes flashing.
And at the center of them all, at the very end, was one being.
*Flap-flap-flap!*
A wave of monstrous creatures no one could block or evade.
Beyond the thunder of countless wings beating as they poured down and covered the space, the voice of the monster who had finally regained all his strength and memories pierced Cheongpung’s ears.
“I remember your name.”
“And the debt I owe that bastard Mae Jonghak, the Sword Saint.”
At that moment—
*Crack-crack-crack!*
Flesh and bone tore with a sickening sound, and sticky blood stained Cheongpung’s vision red.

chapters.title: Chapter 1110
paragraphs: It all began and ended in an instant.
“I remember. Your name.”
The low voice of the monster that had absorbed the life force of countless fiends raining down from the sky rang across the battlefield.
“And the debt I owe that bastard Mae Jonghak, the Sword Saint.”
At last, the monster—the Blood Lord—had awakened with all his strength and memories restored. His red eyes flashed.
Then a blood-red flash, brighter even than the light in his eyes, shot through the air.
*Whoosh!*
Cheongpung had to dodge. If it hit him, he would die.
But he had already spent all his strength. He could only watch helplessly as the Blood Lord’s palm struck the air like lightning, sending a blood-red palm strike hurtling toward him.
Someone else moved, though—guided by careful judgment honed through countless experiences and by an instant’s instinct.
*Crunch!*
A terrible tearing sound sent a chill down Cheongpung’s spine. Flesh and bone ripped away all at once, and the blood within burst out.
*Splatter. Drip-drip.*
Hot, sticky blood washed over his face. Cheongpung blinked, dazed.
Not from unbearable pain, or because he’d seen death looming before him.
Through his blood-red vision, he saw a man looking down at him. Somehow, Cheongpung had ended up sprawled on his side.
“Get... up. Quickly.”
*Cough.*

The man swallowed the blood that surged up whenever he opened his mouth and spoke again, his voice strained but calm. It was hard to believe the palm strike had torn off his arm all the way to the shoulder.
“Leave now. Before it’s too late.”
“B-but—”
Cheongpung’s mind had gone blank at this unexpected turn. He was just starting to stammer out a reply when—
“You fool!”
The fierce shout burst out without warning. Then a growl like a beast’s came from between the man’s bloodied lips.
“Do you still not understand? Can you still not see?”
Blood spilled with every word he ground out. Even so, he did not stop.
Something mattered more to him than the pain threatening to overwhelm his mind. More even than the death he knew was coming.
“None of this is for you! It’s to save everyone—to save the whole world!”

The man roared like a great tiger. He pointed to the Blood Lord, who was approaching even now amid scattering flashes of blood-red light, and to the people throwing themselves at that unprecedented monster without a moment’s hesitation.
*BOOM!*
*Crack! Splaaash!*
Deafening crashes shook the battlefield. Fountains of blood erupted without pause, blotting out the rain.
Cheongpung stared at the horrific hellscape of slaughter. At last, he gritted his teeth and stood.
*Grind.*
A dull pain, and the taste of blood filled his mouth.
But that was nothing compared to what those people were suffering as they were torn apart and broken, even now.
“I’ll... thank you later.”
What more was there to say?
The man smiled faintly and nodded. Watching Cheongpung walk away, he murmured as if to himself, “Please look after him. The Marquis of Shangshan.”
That was all. There would be no later for him, and he knew it.
*Step.*
His footstep felt unusually heavy as he turned. He fixed a calm gaze on the monster approaching through the dense mist of blood and spoke.
“You who dared to plot rebellion and throw the world into chaos: state your identity and surrender peacefully.”
“Criminal? Surrender?”
The Blood Lord’s mouth twisted into a smile. It held mockery—and the anger of a predator whose prey had slipped away before his eyes.
“There are a lot of you idiots who’ve got a death wish.”
*Shhhhh.*
In a matter of moments, the blood-red beams that had swallowed hundreds of lives rose in strands from the Blood Lord’s entire body.
“You should have run. It would only have bought you a little time, but at least you might have had a chance to look back on your life.”
The man gripped the great sword in the one hand he had left and answered.
“I don’t need that chance. I’m not like you.”
And he truly wasn’t.

Not everything he had done in his life had been perfectly just. But he had lived it with true loyalty. He had never blindly submitted to orders, nor had he wavered when powerful men dangled tempting offers before him.
He had proved himself, and in doing so earned the right to stand here—just as the others forming a square around him had, though they looked ready to collapse.
“Let me ask you all: what is our duty?”
At the sudden question from their commander, the roughly three hundred surviving Embroidered Uniform Guards answered as one.
“To protect the Imperial House with an unshakable oath and unwavering loyalty!”
Some voices were young, others old.
The familiar faces of friends and comrades who had shared their lives with them—less than half remained.
Each remembered the oath they had etched into their hearts the day they first received shining golden armor.
“Then what is our obligation?”
They were exhausted in body and mind. Even raising their voices was a struggle now.
That was why they drew on every last bit of strength to answer: so the fear creeping into their hearts would not rule them, and so their oath would not fade even in death.
“To protect all the people—and beyond them, the whole world!”
Their cry shook the air. The sneer on the Blood Lord’s lips began to fade.
*Vroooom.*
The great sword in the man’s hand trembled and shone with a clear light.
Force. Magnificent and radiant, it had long seemed to him a realm he could never reach.
*Did enlightenment finally come when I let go of everything? Or... is Heaven telling me to fight back however I can?*
The question crossed his mind, and he let out a quiet laugh.
He didn’t know where this sudden power had come from. It no longer mattered. He knew what he had to do, and that was enough.
“As a Thousand Captain of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, carrying out His Majesty the Emperor’s exalted will, I give you your orders!”
The man—Jeong Hogun—swallowed the blood surging up his throat and shouted. He leveled his Force, burning like a final rally, at the enemies who had surrounded them and the monster at their center.
“Behead the rebels!”
At that moment—
“Loyalty!”
Their military salute rang out with more force and desperation than ever. Jeong Hogun and the roughly three hundred Embroidered Uniform Guards charged with a roar that caught in their throats.
Straight toward the death looming before them.
Their bodies would perish, but what they did at the end would remain.
They were magnificent.
*Whoosh.*
And it was glorious.
*CRUNCH!*
A massive blood-red flash erupted without warning, staining everything around them. Within it, they fell.
My vision was blurry.
Pains large and small jabbed through my body like sharp awls. Every sound reaching my ears seemed distant, like an echo from beyond a mountain ridge.
*Ah.*
A question suddenly occurred to me.
Where was I? Who was I? And why were my eyelids so heavy?
It was strange. I could’ve sworn I remembered everything just a moment ago.
*I just want to sleep. Peacefully.*
I couldn’t think of anything else. If I could just fall asleep, I felt I would be completely at peace.
A desperate longing to rest somewhere without pain or worry was the only thing ruling my body.
—Rest, huh? That doesn’t sound so bad.
An unfamiliar voice echoed in my mind, but I wasn’t even curious who it belonged to. Maybe I was hearing things as I drifted in and out. Maybe another part of me agreed.
What did it matter, as long as I could fall asleep in peace?
*Right? There’s nothing wrong with taking a little rest.*
The voice answered my question.
—If you put it that way... I’d have to say there are plenty of reasons it could be a problem.
*A problem?*
—You know why better than I do.
*What?*
I was bewildered. I didn’t even remember who I was. How could I know why?
The voice spoke again.
—You can’t feel it, can you? Even now, you’re struggling with everything you have to wake up.
That couldn’t be right. That was nonsense from some clueless idiot.
My vision was blurred and spinning, and pain was gnawing at every part of me. Who wouldn’t want to rest like this? I wanted so badly to fall asleep.
—Are you sure?
Of course.
Or... I thought so.
—Then how are you still conscious? All you have to do is close your eyes and give in to instinct. Everything will be peaceful.
*That’s...*
—Don’t tell me you’ve forgotten how to fall asleep.
I had no answer.
Confusion had crept in and begun to push the drowsiness aside, though I hadn’t even noticed. All I could do was turn a question over in my mind.
*Why? Why am I fighting so hard to hold on?*
This time, the voice gave me no answer.
Instead, fragments of memory fell one by one onto the once-calm surface of my consciousness. And from somewhere deep within me, an unfamiliar current of qi began to rise.
*Whooosh.*
It felt as though a wind were blowing. Clear and refreshing, it pressed down on the pain that had tormented me and rekindled the dying embers of my memory.
My name. Countless faces and voices. As my senses sharpened, the strong smell of blood and someone’s shout reached me too.
My vision slowly cleared, and the echo drew closer.
Amid it all, I finally remembered why I had wanted so badly to rest—and why, despite that, I had refused to let go of consciousness.
As my mind awoke, the pain returned with it.
Was this what it felt like to fall into a pit of fire? To have my body torn into thousands of pieces?
I didn’t know. I couldn’t know.
But I knew one thing: I still had so much left to protect.
—As always, a good decision.
At the moment the unknown voice whispered its last words in my mind—
*Whoooosh.*
The wind sweeping through my body became a wave of qi carrying the fragrance of flowers. It washed over me.
No—it lifted my dying body and mind back to their feet.
And at last, I heard a familiar voice.
“...Benefactor! Benefactor!”
A frantic cry. A face drenched in tears.
I woke with a gasp, and Cheongpung’s voice thundered in my ears.
“The West Gate—the West Gate...!”
The reality I had barely returned to was still cruel.
