He wanted to deny it, to tell himself it couldn’t possibly be true. But it was no use.
Unlike the fire raging in his chest, his mind had gone cold. It faced the reality coming toward him head-on.
*It’s them. It has to be.*
Pa Ryun, the Alliance Leader of the Yangtze River Channel League.
And Tae Gunak, the Alliance Leader of the Green Forest Alliance—Pa Ryun’s equal and lifelong rival.
The two giants who divided the world’s dark-path forces between them had finally reached the battlefield.
And they’d brought an army of thirty thousand.
*...Then that means—*
Unable to finish the thought, Jin Taekyung raised his hazy eyes and looked around.
People leaned against the low walls of the Inner City, gasping for breath amid countless bodies and pools of blood scattered in every direction.
Some of those who had retreated from the three sides other than the East Gate had familiar faces. Others had not appeared at all.
*Why?*
Jin Taekyung wondered in a daze.
Why hadn’t they returned yet?
He already knew the answer. Still, he asked himself again.
*Right. So that’s how it ended.*
A weak laugh escaped him.
He thought of the faces he would never see again.
He felt the presence of tens of thousands of enemies surrounding the Inner City, and of the monster leading them.
KWA-BOOOOM!
With a tremendous crash, the Inner City crumbled.

sentences.text: Boom!
The low sound of air being torn apart rang out, and the whole world seemed to stop.
At least, that was how it felt to the members of the Fire Dragon Pavilion who saw a palm strike, launched at lightning speed, hit Hyuk Mujin in the chest.
And then—
Splatter.
As Hyuk Mujin’s body crumpled, scattering dark-red blood, the world that had stopped began to move again.
“No!”
Taishan’s eyes were bloodshot.
The muscles across his body bulged as if they might burst.
At the unbelievable sight before him, he let out a thunderous roar and charged toward the gate.
He forgot his exhaustion.
He cast aside his fear.
Like an enraged bull, Taishan swung his two-section staff with all his strength and pressed forward.
Whoooosh!
Wham!
Each time the furious wind rose, brains flew and bones shattered like powder.
Fanatics had taken the place of the monsters, frozen like statues at the death of the corpse sorcerer.
They tried to block his path, but none could easily stop Taishan in his rage.
No—more accurately, they couldn’t stop *them*.
KRRRUNCH!
A fierce rush of saber energy tore through the space, and severed limbs flew in every direction.
Amid the swirling spray of blood, Sama Pyo’s eyes—usually so composed—blazed with blue fire.
And someone else plunged into the dozens of fanatics closing in around Sama Pyo, heedless of their fallen comrades.
SHWEEEE!
Song Ilseom’s narrow-bladed sword shot through the air in swift, economical movements, each one utterly cruel.
Even the epithet Soul-Chasing Guest seemed inadequate.
Stab!
Stab-stab!
Song Ilseom stabbed and twisted at every opening.
With the most efficient movements, he dealt his enemies certain pain and death.
Blood burst from a terrible scream and splashed across his face.
Blades rained down indiscriminately from every direction, leaving cuts large and small across his body.
But his tightly pressed lips didn’t tremble.
The blood flowing through Song Ilseom’s veins came from an illustrious family.
But what had made him the Soul-Chasing Guest was blood shed on the battlefield.
He had once left the path of the wandering martial artist, which he’d walked all his life to repay the debt of an earlier generation.
Now he was throwing his life away to repay a comrade’s blood debt.
He gave himself over to pure rage, without a thought for the cost.
And Song Ilseom wasn’t the only one who felt it.
“How dare you...!”
“You bastards are lower than this beggar!”
Sssshing!
Slice!
Ju Hwaran, Gung Gibang, and the thousand defenders who had barely survived gritted their teeth and forced themselves to their feet.
Hope that they could win?
They’d long since erased it from their hearts.
The monsters had stopped moving, but fanatics remained—several times as many.
Worse, tens of thousands of enemy reinforcements had appeared.
But hope wasn’t the only thing that could move people.
In that dark, bottomless despair, they had seen it clearly:
Hyuk Mujin, refusing to lose his dignity until the very last moment before he fell.
*Fire Dragon Pavilion...
No.*
Before an enemy they could not possibly defeat, his spirit had not bent.
*Swift Wind Sword Hyuk Mujin.*
CLANG-CLANG-CLANG!
At last, a thousand blades began to shine again, rippling like a wave.
The defenders clamped their hands over severed arms and slashed-open bellies.
They bit their tongues to suppress their pain and fear, gripped their weapons, and stood.
With all their strength, they shouted what might be their last words—the final proof that they had existed in this world.
“Knife-and-Dagger Hero So Gyuhyeok is here!”
“Swift Blade Shakes the Heavens Mu Cheol is here too!”
“Figures the orthodox faction would have such fancy titles.
I’m Black-Killing Sword Jo Hyeok, you bastards!”
Masters of the orthodox faction, the unorthodox faction, and those who belonged somewhere between the two.
Their roots, their branches, and the fruit they bore were different.
But the great cause they sought to protect was the same.
“Destroy the Demonic Path and restore Heaven.”
Destroy the Demonic Path and set the heavens right.
An old Daoist murmured the four characters they had once shouted until they were spitting blood, back when they fought a hundred thousand followers of the Demonic Path.
He tightened his grip on his sword.
Slice.
A body split into dozens of pieces along a streak of white light and scattered.
The Black Ghost had finally met its true end.
The old Daoist turned away, and Cheongheoja’s voice rang out, carrying the force of his internal energy.
“I miss those days.
The time when you and I were ‘us.’ Don’t you?”
In Cheongheoja’s eyes, steeped in sorrow and anger, a huge figure stood before the ruined gate in the distance.
“Seafaring King Pa Ryun.”
The next moment—
“You haven’t changed, Cheongheoja.”
With a heavy voice that brushed over Hyuk Mujin’s fallen head, the master of the long, vast Yangtze strode out beneath the faint moonlight.
Two more unwelcome guests emerged from behind his imposing frame.
One was a mysterious figure dressed in black from head to toe.
The other, a slight old man standing beside him, had a familiar face.
“It’s been a long time, Cheongheoja.”
At the greeting, Cheongheoja’s gaze turned cold.
“Right.
You were there too.
Green Forest Battle King Tae Gunak.”
“Such a sharp edge to your words.
Last time we met, I believe you called me a fellow Daoist, not ‘you.’”
“Those days will never return.
Not after the irrevocable choices some people made.”
Tae Gunak looked around, his brow furrowing slightly.
“I’m sorry things came to this.
I mean that.”
“You mean that...”
Cheongheoja murmured the words hollowly, then drew up every last bit of his remaining internal energy.
Hummm.
As if sensing that his master’s end was near, the treasured sword that had been with him all his life trembled.
Not far away, Great Sir was still struggling against Black Ghost.
But Cheongheoja’s senses and energy had already focused entirely on the unwelcome guests guarding the gate.
He had to bring down more than the two giants who divided the world’s dark-path forces between them.
There was also the mysterious man in black.
Instinct told Cheongheoja he was no weaker than either of them.
*He must be one of Dark Heaven’s key figures.
But who?*
The question crossed his mind, but Cheongheoja could only smile bitterly.
Worry was ultimately a luxury for those who survived.

All he could do was resolve to meet his end without shame before those remarkable young people, still advancing as they cut down their enemies.

The old Daoist’s eyes flashed, colder than ever.

A quiet voice reached every ear.

Jin Taekyung couldn’t tell what had caused it or why.

chapters.title: Chapter 1121
paragraphs: Regardless of a wall’s height, size, or durability, its mere existence made a huge difference in a siege.
Even the shabbiest wall was still a wall.
Xining’s Inner City had been built with street fighting against outside invaders in mind. Its walls might not compare to those of the Outer City, but they still offered a considerable advantage.
It should have, anyway.
KWA-BOOOOM!
It began and ended in an instant.
All because of one man.
No—one monster.
Rumble.
The Inner City wall crumbled with a roar like a scream, raising a thick cloud of dust. Watching it fall, the Blood Lord laughed wildly.
He prided himself on having gained power beyond human limits. To him, the sight was laughable.
They should have been scattering in every direction, running for their lives. Instead, they’d fled to the Inner City?
“Did you think a pile of rocks like that could stop me?”
With a low mutter, the Blood Lord raised the Red Blade once more.
Shhhhh!
A blood-red flash surged along the blade.
A massive half-moon of Force took shape in an instant, about to tear across the space before him—
“Stop!”
An urgent voice rang out.
But even as someone appeared to stop him, the Blood Lord brought the Red Blade down without hesitation.
WHOOOSH!
The space turned red.
In a flash like a bolt of lightning, the Force crossed dozens of jang and sank into the dust cloud.
No—it swallowed the cloud whole.
Its ferocity could only be called monstrous.
KRRRUNCH!
As the crash and tremor shook heaven and earth, the Blood Lord smiled. Then he turned toward the uninvited guest who had dared to stop him.
“You’re late. You should’ve said something sooner. I might’ve been able to stop just in time.”
The Blood Lord sounded almost casual. The Grand Sorceress’s gaze turned cold.
“What have you done?”
“What does it look like?”
He shrugged and gestured with his chin toward the distant cloud of dust.
“Crushing their last hope. Making sure they won’t even want to resist anymore.”
Her voice trailed off. She stared at the still-smiling Blood Lord, unable to continue. Then she asked calmly about the one thing that mattered most: whether a certain person was still alive.
“So he’s still safe, isn’t he?”
“Safe? Better than fine. Look at me. Can’t you feel this power?”
The Blood Lord spread his arms with the innocent pride of a child showing something off to a parent. A chill settled in the Grand Sorceress’s chest.
He was different.
He had changed.
Everything about him was different from usual.
His pupils were completely blood-red. An unprecedented aura flowed naturally from his grotesque body, as though human and monster had been fused together. But the greatest change lay elsewhere.
Madness.
The Grand Sorceress could sense it now: a bottomless madness whose depth and intensity she could not begin to fathom.
Instinct also told her she must never let him know she had noticed.
“Cut the pointless nonsense. You know better than anyone that isn’t what I meant.”
“That hurts. I didn’t know there was something you cared about more than the well-being of a comrade in the same boat.”
“Since when were we so close?”
“Well, if you put it like that, I have nothing to say. Fine.”
The Blood Lord let out an exaggerated sigh.
“Jin Taekyung is still alive. Probably.”
“Probably?”
“Then let me correct that to *definitely*. There’s no way those old monsters in there couldn’t protect one little brat.”
Even to the Grand Sorceress, it didn’t sound like an unreasonable guess.

Just fifteen minutes earlier, the defenders had retreated from the walls on all three sides except the East Gate and gathered in the Inner City. Among them were the Bow Saint, the Slaughter Saint, and the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang.
They’d all suffered serious injuries while withdrawing to the Inner City, but even so, their wounds shouldn’t have been severe enough to prevent them from keeping Jin Taekyung safe.
As if to prove the Blood Lord right, familiar faces appeared beyond the thinning dust cloud.
And among them was the most important person of all—the one who absolutely could not die.
The Slaughter Saint and the Bow Saint were pale with exhaustion and internal injuries. Jeok Cheongang looked worse than either of them.
But the Grand Sorceress barely saw them now.
She saw only one person.
Jin Taekyung.
The moment she spotted him, she let out the breath she had been holding.
There was no mistaking him. He was drenched in blood from head to toe, but he was alive.
He could barely stand, using a white-glowing spear as a cane while Cheongpung supported him. For the Grand Sorceress, that was enough.
She had Magic—the mysterious power the Lord of Heaven had given her.
Still, Jin Taekyung’s condition looked so grave she could sense his precarious state even from this far away.
*I have to take him to that person. As soon as possible.*
His injuries might be beyond even Magic’s power to heal completely.
The anxious Grand Sorceress was about to recite a teleportation spell silently when—
“What’s the rush?”
The Blood Lord’s low whisper came from behind her. Her eyes widened before she could stop them.
*How?*
If the foundation of martial arts was the accumulation of energy, Magic depended on attunement to it. That made her more sensitive than anyone to its fluctuations.
Yet the Blood Lord had taken a position behind her without her seeing or sensing him. He stood there smiling like a predator with its prey already in its mouth.
“The more I think about it, the more interesting Magic seems. Traveling thousands—tens of thousands—of ri in the blink of an eye... Even saving someone who’s half dead. Am I right?”
His hot breath touched the back of her neck. The Grand Sorceress spoke through clenched teeth.
“I already told you. Cut the pointless nonsense.”
“Nonsense?”
The Blood Lord gave a short laugh and licked his lips with his red tongue.
“Not this time, I’m afraid. I don’t want to let prey I’ve already caught escape like that.”
Realizing what he meant, the Grand Sorceress gritted her teeth.
“Blood Lord, you’ve finally gone mad.”
“That’s strange. I could’ve sworn you always called me a madman.”
“You dare go against that person’s will...?”
After a brief silence, the Blood Lord answered with a bright smile.
At last, he had cast off his mask and shackles. He was freer—and stronger—than ever.
“Why not? Just this once.”
At that moment—
Slice!
A streak of red flashed. The Grand Sorceress’s hazy figure appeared three jang away.
Then—
SPLAAASH!
Her body staggered, spraying blood, before collapsing like a puppet with its strings cut.
Splat.
That was the end.
Her body lay motionless in a pool of blood. Her eyes remained wide open, without a trace of life in them.
“I wasn’t planning to kill her... Oh, well. Can’t be helped.”
The Blood Lord muttered to himself and looked around.
Countless eyes stared at him in the sudden silence. Tens of thousands of fanatics surrounded the Inner City without a gap in their lines, watching the unexpected scene with eyes wide.
This time, even they could not hide their agitation.
The Blood Lord addressed them calmly, choosing the shortest and surest method—one possible only in Dark Heaven.
“By the command of the great Lord of Heaven, I have executed the apostate. From now on, I will command the entire army.”
“Kill every last one of them.”
The order broke the heavy silence.
Rumble!
With a roar that shook heaven and earth, tens of thousands of fanatics charged toward the Inner City.
To punish the wicked heretics who dared oppose the Lord of Heaven—the living god and sole absolute ruler.
The fanatics surged forward like a giant wave. The Blood Lord laughed aloud and began to walk.
He was going to take the life of the one man he had longed to kill.
“Jin Taekyung—!”
The monster’s roar, imbued with an unprecedented aura, rang across the battlefield and swallowed it whole.
The air trembled. Sound was muffled in my ears.
Shouts and screams burst without pause from every direction. The bone-chilling clang of steel engulfed the battlefield.
But through the chaos and my fading senses, I could still feel it:
The warmth radiating from the people fighting countless enemies to protect me.
At the same time, I heard the monster’s roar, full of joy and madness.
*Jin Taekyung.*
Right. That was my name.
The name I had been given at birth.
In two different worlds, I existed as both one person and two.
And maybe today was the last moment I’d been given.
*I have to go.*
I didn’t know where I found the strength.
My organs must have been twisted, my Eight Extraordinary Meridians torn to shreds. With the mere handful of internal energy I had left, I couldn’t do anything.
Even so, I shook off Cheongpung’s support and staggered forward as if in a trance.
Slice!
A stray blade grazed my shoulder.
Blood flowed—blood I hadn’t even known was still there—but I felt no pain as I reached out.
CRACK.
The fanatic’s gleaming eyes widened in pain.
He instinctively tried to wrench his wrist from my grasp with all his strength, but a surge of scorching heat reached him first and engulfed him.
BOOM!
To someone else, it might have felt like flames hot enough to burn them alive. To me, it felt like the warmest thing in the world.
Maybe it was because of who had saved me.
“El...der.”
Squeezing out every last bit of my voice, I grabbed Jeok Cheongang’s shoulder and whispered.
“A path. Please open a path for me.”

chapters.title: Chapter 1122
paragraphs: With the collapsed walls at their backs, the defenders fought more fiercely and more valiantly than ever.
After surviving against impossible odds and retreating to the Inner City, they numbered a little over five thousand.
Compared to the tens of thousands of fanatics blackening the land on every side, they were a mere handful. Yet the last-ditch defenders didn’t give an inch.
No—they couldn’t.
Behind them, beyond the rubble of the fallen walls, countless civilians trembled before the threat of death drawing closer by the second.
But having nowhere left to retreat didn’t mean they could advance.
KRRRUNCH!
Flesh split, revealing white bone. Amid the red mist that swirled over the battlefield at the moment of impact, anguished screams and shouts rang out, muffled and dull.
“Graaaagh!”
“Hold the line! We have to hold—!”
Stab!
An axe blade cleaved through the crown of his head, cutting off the shout.
The man who crumpled had been a Peak master renowned as a hero throughout Qinghai for decades. But in this horrific melee, amid all this death, none of that meant anything.
And he wasn’t the only one.
The Sect Leader of a school. The Family Head of a household surrounded by relatives.
A young man whose downy cheeks hadn’t even lost their softness.
The moment the fanatics’ blind blades swept them up, they fell as nothing more than lumps of meat.
CRUNCH! Stab-stab-stab!
Perhaps the outcome of this desperate final battle had been decided before it even began.
The defenders had long since pushed past the limits of exhaustion.
Surviving this long in today’s battle was proof of their strength. But what lay before them couldn’t be overcome by sheer will.
The energy they had left. Their numbers.
They lacked everything. Desperately.
The dead rolled limply across the ground. Those still alive could only tremble on instinct as they watched the advancing enemy trample over the bodies of their fallen comrades.
Fear and anger gripped them, along with the helplessness of being unable to do anything.
Perhaps that was why, as their bodies and hearts—and the whole world around them—seemed to sink into pitch-black darkness, the flame someone kindled shone all the brighter.
Fwoosh—BOOM!
The air caught fire. Heat like the sun evaporated the rain and swallowed the fanatics whole.
At the heart of the fierce flames surging forward stood a giant of fire, his burning eyes flashing.
“Who dares!”
With a furious roar, Jeok Cheongang, the Fire King, swept his sleeve.
The flames, whipped up by a fierce wind, melted steel and burned the fanatics’ flesh and bones.
“Stand in our way?!”
Jeok Cheongang had always called himself “this old man,” but not this time.
He wasn’t walking alone anymore.
Now, they walked together.

Along the perilous, steep path to the brink of death that Jeok Cheongang had always been forced to walk alone, there was now someone at his side—a man who had become both a part of him and his whole world.
“Don’t retreat! Don’t be afraid!”
Supporting Jin Taekyung as he staggered, Jeok Cheongang burned the enemies rushing in from every direction and shouted with all his might.
Blades he would normally have scoffed at and dodged grazed his body. Every time he summoned his internal energy, pain blazed through his tangled acupoints. None of that mattered to him now.
“Open a path!”
It was a request from Jin Taekyung, his one and only Disciple.
A reckless request. One that might truly be his last.
But the old Master couldn’t refuse his Disciple, already standing at death’s door.
And Jeok Cheongang wasn’t the only one willing to grant it.
Slice!
Dozens of heads flew into the air in a dazzling flash.
Jeok Cheongang swallowed the blood that suddenly surged into his mouth and watched with a faint smile.
“Took you long enough. You’re slow as hell.”
At the familiar reproach, the Slaughter Saint spoke, his face pale as a sheet.
He, too, had suffered serious injuries fighting to hold back the Grand Sorceress and the Black Ghosts during the retreat to the Inner City.
“I couldn’t see the patient, so I went looking. Figured I’d drag him back by the collar.”
“And what do you intend to do?”
SHWICK!
The Slaughter Saint answered by bringing down his small knife.
The strike was ghostly in its speed and precision. The fanatics rushing in to fill the momentary gap crumpled like bundles of straw.
Just as his heart had when he saw Taekyung’s condition.
“Before it’s too late...I’ll take the lead.”
At the Slaughter Saint’s quiet reply, something tightened in Jeok Cheongang’s chest.
Perhaps the man could escape this battlefield right now. He was the greatest assassin of all time.
That was why they called him the Slaughter Saint.
Yet Jeok Cheongang gritted his teeth against the weight pressing down on his heart.
*Before it’s too late.*
That was what he’d said. Clear as day.
Jeok Cheongang knew instinctively that the words hadn’t come from the Slaughter Saint as an assassin, but from the Divine Physician. And that his answer held not a glimmer of hope, but despair.
*He’s going to die.*
A cruel truth too hard to believe, too hard to accept.
Jeok Cheongang stared blankly at Jin Taekyung, limp in his grasp as if unconscious. Then he clenched his fist.
There were no choices left for them now.
All they could do was give everything they had and kindle one last flame—perhaps their final one.
Even now, that flame was slowly growing larger and hotter.
SHWAAAA!
Force suddenly shot out from somewhere and spread across the space.
Unlike the Slaughter Saint’s Force, so keen it seemed it could cut you just by looking at it, this web of Force felt as free as the wind. It wrapped around the enemies.
Calmly. Gently.
Then it struck with enough destructive power to wipe away that fleeting impression.
Slice—SPLAAASH!
A fountain of blood burst into the air.

Among the enemies crumpling to the ground, the Bow Saint appeared. Following the movement of her fingers, the broken bowstaff—split in two amid the fierce battle at the West Gate—moved with blinding speed.
KRRRUNCH!
It had lost its original shape, but her bow had always been made to come apart and serve as a pair of curved swords.
Without a word, the Bow Saint swept through the fanatics like a storm. Close behind her, another familiar face appeared.
“Benefactor!”
Despite his urgent shout, Cheongpung’s sword technique flowed as gracefully as a painter’s brush across white paper.
SHSHSHK!
A handful of purple Force, the color of sunset, sketched out flowers.
The dozens of plum blossoms seemed beautiful—until they touched the fanatics. Then they turned an even deeper red and bloomed in a glorious spray.
“Why’d you have to come along too...?”
Before the Slaughter Saint could stop Cheongpung from plunging deep into enemy lines to join this perilous undertaking, a roar from far away swallowed the battlefield.
If a sound could take the shape of a giant, would it look like this?
The roar was so immense it shook even the eardrums of someone whose hearing had already burst. And there was a desperate, almost spiteful edge to it.
Everyone who turned toward its source stared wide-eyed.
Jeok Cheongang and Cheongpung, injured themselves, supporting Jin Taekyung as they fought off their enemies.
The Slaughter Saint and Bow Saint, realizing that the enemy reinforcements who had finally taken the East Gate had arrived.
And one man walking slowly toward them, an overwhelming aura pouring from him.
No—a monster.
“That’s...”
His words trailed off.
The Blood Lord stared toward the source of the roar, an indescribable look on his face. Then he burst into laughter.
“Pfft—hahahahaha!”
His booming laughter had no place on a battlefield covered in a sea of corpses and blood.
But the Blood Lord didn’t care. He laughed like a madman, bending over and clutching his stomach as if he’d never heard or seen anything funnier in his life.
Then, as if he hadn’t laughed at all, he lifted his head, his expression cold, and looked at the countless people approaching from far away beneath shouts that seemed to pierce the heavens.
They were weaker and more insignificant than any enemy he had faced so far. That only made those damn moths flying into the flame more infuriating.
“What kind of lunatics are these...?”
The Blood Lord meant it. He could think of no other explanation for the absurd sight reflected in his blood-red eyes.
But no matter how he questioned it or thought it over, he couldn’t find an answer.
No—even if the Blood Lord gained the power of true immortality, he could never understand it.
The old, the powerless, the very young—people born to spend their lives being trampled and trembling in fear—were risking their lives to protect someone else. He couldn’t even imagine it.
And yet they were there.
They shouted with set faces and trembling voices, caught between desperate resolve and fear they couldn’t quite shake. They gripped crude bamboo spears and rusty axes with all their strength.
They had spent their lives yielding to fate. Now they defied it to help those who had staked their own fates on protecting them.
Countless civilians, seeking for the first time in their lives to protect someone beyond their own families.
They were here.
Today. Right here.
“How—dare you!”
The monster’s roar, charged with power beyond anything before it, crushed the civilians’ seemingly endless shouts.
With a faint voice only a handful of people could hear, Jin Taekyung forced his eyelids open in his Master’s arms and struggled to speak.
“Shut up already...you fucking bastard.”

chapters.title: Chapter 1123
paragraphs: Hearing that familiar voice tremble with agitation, I let out the breath I’d been holding.
I blinked slowly and swallowed the blood pooled in my mouth.
It was a strange feeling, unlike anything I’d ever experienced.
I felt hazy, as if I were trapped in a dream I could never escape. And yet, at the same time, everything around me came through with perfect clarity.
As for what this unfamiliar sensation was, the System gave me a clear answer, as it always did.
In its uniquely kind and cruel way.
*Beep.*
**System Status Effect:** Final Rally has been applied.
Final rally.
Like sunlight blazing just before sunset, it was the last flame to burn at the darkening edge of a life.
*So this is what it feels like.*
The thought came to me suddenly.
I thought of the final moments of those I’d brought down with my own two hands—and those I’d desperately tried to hold on to, only to lose them anyway.
All the countless emotions I’d glimpsed in them.
At last, I felt as though I could understand them all.
I understood something else, too. Unlike them, who had waited for death as it slowly drew near, I was the kind of fool who had no choice but to run toward it.
*Ding.*

**System** Final Rally is an act of divine mercy, an expression of human will, and a candle by which you may reflect on the life you have lived. Though its flame burns only briefly, that moment of light will shine so brightly that even death may be forgotten.
This time, it wasn’t the cold, harsh warning tone.
A familiar, clear chime rang in my ears, rousing my body and mind from their endless plunge into darkness.
Just as the System had said, it was a light bright enough to make me forget even death.
**System** All pain you feel is greatly reduced for the duration of Final Rally.
My body stopped trembling under the pain and death closing in by the second.
**System Qi Sense** temporarily increases greatly.
A spark caught in the ashes of my cooling mind.
Fwoosh.
Sudden warmth seeped into my back, and the spark swelled into a flame.
**System** Scorching Yang Qi cradles your exhausted body and heals some of your Internal Injuries.
Two flames could not coexist.
Sooner or later, they would collide and destroy each other.
But if they came from the same root, they were one flame to begin with.
Just like the person who, despite suffering severe Internal Injuries of his own, had shared his qi with me without hesitation.
“What are you waiting for?”
His face was as pale as paper. Wounds large and small covered his body, and his frame trembled.
But Jeok Cheongang was smiling at me.
He was trying to hold back both his joy that his Disciple had regained a little strength and his sorrow at what that meant.
“Come on. Let’s go. Together.”
At that moment—
*Ding.*
**System** A sudden Quest, A Candle in the Wind, or a Flame, has been generated! Death awaits you. You cannot refuse this Quest! **Time Limit:** 9 minutes, 59 seconds
Time began to flow again. I gripped White Flame tightly and took a step forward.
Into the nightmare that wasn’t over yet.
No—toward a reality worse than any nightmare.
*I’ll change it. I have to.*
If this had been my fight alone, I might have given up already.
I might have leaned my exhausted body against a pile of corpses, looked back on the time I’d left behind, and waited for death to slowly descend.
But—
SHWICK!
I wasn’t alone anymore.
KWA-BOOOOM!
Dazzling light-flames swallowed the enemies whole.
Amid the reddish, overheated earth and the shimmering haze that warped the air, a giant of fire roared.
At the same time, the Slaughter Saint, the Bow Saint, Cheongpung, and the last of the devoted defenders advanced.
Countless civilians followed behind them like a wave, no longer shouting out of desperation but calling a name none of us had expected.
“Charge! Charge! Protect the Marquis of Shangshan!”
The great shout shook the battlefield and reached my ears. A jolt like lightning shot up my spine.
They said they would protect me.
Me, of all people.
Those people with neither a scrap of internal energy nor a proper weapon, gripping sickles and pickaxes in their hands.
They were risking their lives for me—the man who hadn’t even managed to protect his own people.
*Right. In the end, I couldn’t protect you.*
The beloved faces I would never see again flashed through my mind, and I shot toward the fanatics.
SHWIIK!
My toes. My waist. My shoulder. My arms and wrists.
My body followed movements etched into instinct through countless repetitions and real battles, splitting the raging wind and rain.
Slice!
A single, cool cutting sound crossed the air.
At the same time, more than ten pairs of eyes flew wide open.
The fanatics stared at me in disbelief, clutching their slit throats as they crumpled to the ground.
White Flame’s spearhead, trailing a faint heat, was slower and weaker than it had ever been. But for some reason, the enemies waiting in its path couldn’t react in time.
Neither could those surging forward to fill the gaps left by their dead comrades.
Stab! Crack!
I stabbed through everything in my way, pulled my spear free, and twisted it.
My vision was still hazy, but my senses were sharper than ever.
So were the faces and voices that flickered past, one by one, through the thickening mist of blood.
“I’ll join you. Just make sure the danger pay is generous.”
A pair of fierce eyes, and the willow-leaf saber he always kept close.
But despite his rough appearance, Song Ilseom had always been a reliable comrade and a good person to me.
He complained about the danger and the extra pay on every mission, yet he always fought in the most dangerous places.
He’d left behind the path he’d walked his whole life to protect someone. I was sure he’d kept that vow until his final moments.
*He must have. The Song Ilseom I knew would have.*
There was more to a person than what you saw.
That was true of a wandering martial artist others might have seen as nothing but rough and uncouth. It was true, too, of the two unorthodox faction members I’d unexpectedly formed ties with.
*Am I too late?*
That day in Gansu, when a battle like this one had raged, Sama Pyo had returned from staying with his father through his final moments and asked me that question.
I’d answered without hesitation.
No. You came right on time.
I’d meant it. There hadn’t been a trace of a lie in my answer.
Even if he lost his way while wrestling with his choices and took a long detour, Sama Pyo was the sort of person who would find his way back to the right path in the end.
No.
*He was that kind of friend.*
The words echoed endlessly somewhere deep inside me, and I moved as if entranced.
SHWICK!
Like Song Ilseom, I rolled through a pool of blood to evade blades flying at me from every direction.
Slice!
Like Sama Pyo, I ended my enemies’ lives by the cruelest, surest means.
KRRRUNCH!
Like someone else who wasn’t here, I swept through everything in my way with an overwhelming aura as immense as Taishan.
*Taishan believes in Pavilion Master! Likes him second best in the world, after Lord!*
I pressed forward.
Voices rang like hallucinations amid flying blood and screams.
Familiar faces appeared, one after another, over the enemies collapsing like bundles of straw.
“Would you like to take a walk?”
The memories rose like mist and passed like wind.
The Fire Courtyard of the Yongbong Escort Bureau, shrouded in darkness, and the full moon, unusually bright and large that night.
“Great Hero Jin.”
Her lively voice and light, dancing steps, buoyed by drink.
“Do you think...I can do it?”
And the tears in her eyes that none of it could hide.
“Can I really do it?”
I remembered it all vividly.
Every bit of it.
How I’d made a pointless fuss about the brightness of the moon, then fallen silent at her unexpected question.
Even the moment I’d looked into her tear-filled eyes and spoken.
“It’s all right if you can’t do it well. You don’t have to force yourself.”
That night, I hadn’t been looking at the moon.
“Wouldn’t that be enough, Young Lady Ju?”
I’d been staring blankly at her eyes, brighter than the full moon and curved like a crescent.
I’d never imagined a day like today would come—or that pitch-black Force would come rushing toward me as it was now.
WHOOOOOSH!
“Get out of the way!”
When had I gotten this far?
Jeok Cheongang’s urgent shout rang out behind me, deep in enemy lines, and a terrible whooshing sound swallowed the noise around us.
But I didn’t flinch.
More precisely, I didn’t have even that much reason left.
I only faced the two streams of energy darkening my already hazy vision. They were so murky they hardly seemed alive at all.
Not with my eyes, but with my senses.
No—with my heart.
And in the gap between moments slowed to a crawl, I thrust out my spear.
SHWICK!
White Flame’s spearhead, wreathed in a faint blaze, cut through the air.
It pierced space, the darkness beyond it, and a single point.
Fwoosh!
The two streams of Force, which had seemed ready to swallow everything without a trace, scattered helplessly. I felt the air tremble all around me.
Destruction? A clash?
No.
The only word for what had just happened was *shattering*.
It was so inexplicable that even I, the one who’d done it, couldn’t understand it.
So perfectly shattered that it enraged even the dead who had just fired Force at me.
—JIN. TAE. KYUNG!
The last two Black Ghosts cried out in unison and charged.
A ghostly horse leaped across the dozen or so jang of open air in an instant, casting its shadow over me. With its blood-red eyes flashing, the now-enlarged Force came crashing down.
KWA-BOOOOOOM!
The rushing blast was violent enough to shake even my already-burst eardrums.
But I wasn’t the only one in its path.
KWAANG! RUMBLE!
In the blink of an eye, four streaks of light tangled in midair and swelled.
The compressed air exploded, and the earth overturned beneath the tremendous force.
At the heart of it were two superhumans who had rushed to save me.
Stab! Crack!
The Slaughter Saint’s short knife and ox-hair needles, and the two curved swords clenched in the Bow Saint’s hands, pierced and sliced through the Black Ghosts at lightning speed.
The two Saints gritted their teeth, faces ashen, wringing out what little strength they had left. The Black Ghosts, meanwhile, refused to fall.
They recovered from mortal wounds and even severed limbs, rising again after dozens of deaths.
Wooooong.
The air trembled.
Countless overlapping spells bolstered the Black Ghosts’ ability to heal and gave them still greater strength and speed.
Enough to face two of the Three Saints, who had fought more fiercely than anyone and were now pushed to their absolute limits.
“Go! Hurry!”
The Slaughter Saint’s urgent shout pierced my ears. The Bow Saint’s tired, lowered gaze touched my cheek, as if telling me to prove I was the one who’d been chosen.
Or that this wasn’t where I was supposed to die.
*Right. I can’t fall here.*
I staggered forward, leaving them behind.
Following Jeok Cheongang and Cheongpung as they opened a path, I cut down the enemies looming through my dreamlike haze, again and again.
I thought of a promise to one person that could never be kept now.
Of the moment I hadn’t been able to bring myself to tell someone who had become my greatest memory in this world to run away.
“I’m Hyuk Mujin, Captain of the Gatekeepers of the great Jin Family of Taiyuan. State your identity and purpose for visiting... What? A pleasure house?”
“Third Young Master, I may be a low-ranking Captain, but let me say one thing.”
We’d met as enemies who couldn’t seem to shake each other.
“A scouting squad? Why me, Third Young Master...?”
“I’ll follow your orders. Captain—no, Captain, sir.”
Before long, the two of us had fallen into step.
“Now, now, Captain. What’s there to worry about when you’ve got me?”
“Your heart! Your right arm! Trust Hyuk Mujin!”
“...Even so, isn’t your little toe a bit much?”
Then we’d become inseparable.
So close that, at some point, being apart no longer felt right.
When I couldn’t see him, I missed him. When he was away, I worried about him.
My most trusted friend and subordinate.
That guy—Hyuk Mujin—had died.
In the end, I hadn’t even seen where he’d died or who had killed him.
*Even if some miracle saved him, I’ll never see him again.*
The last promise I’d made to him would never be fulfilled.
I would die before it could be.
Because I’d have to leave behind the people I’d wanted to protect—or the people waiting somewhere for me, desperate for my return—and set off down a long road from which there was no coming back.
I gritted my teeth and let out the breath I’d been holding.
I swung my spear, rekindling the dying flame without pause.
Trampling the corpses piling up with each step and the blood spurting into the air, I moved as one with the people protecting me.
Toward the last, the only path left for the living and the dead alike.
Toward the blood-red eyes I could sense clearly even through my hazy vision.
KRRRUNCH!
The fanatics’ flesh and bones broke apart beneath the spearhead I brought down on instinct.
Beyond that fierce storm of blood stood a monster steeped in blood and madness.
“You should be running for your life, yet you’ve come to me of your own accord. I hardly know how to thank you.”
The Blood Lord, at last standing before me again, smiled broadly.
More precisely, he smiled at Jeok Cheongang and Cheongpung, both exhausted beyond measure, and at me standing between them.
“Now, it’s time for you to die.”
Maybe he was right.
But—
*Beep.*

Not yet.

sentences.text: Hearing that familiar voice tremble with agitation, I let out the breath I’d been holding.
I blinked slowly and swallowed the blood pooled in my mouth.
It was a strange feeling, unlike anything I’d ever experienced.
I felt hazy, as if I were trapped in a dream I could never escape.
And yet, at the same time, everything around me came through with perfect clarity.
As for what this unfamiliar sensation was, the System gave me a clear answer, as it always did.
In its uniquely kind and cruel way.
*Beep.*
**System Status Effect:** Final Rally has been applied.
Final rally.
Like sunlight blazing just before sunset, it was the last flame to burn at the darkening edge of a life.
*So this is what it feels like.*
The thought came to me suddenly.
I thought of the final moments of those I’d brought down with my own two hands—and those I’d desperately tried to hold on to, only to lose them anyway.
All the countless emotions I’d glimpsed in them.
At last, I felt as though I could understand them all.
I understood something else, too.
Unlike them, who had waited for death as it slowly drew near, I was the kind of fool who had no choice but to run toward it.
*Ding.*
**System** Final Rally is an act of divine mercy, an expression of human will, and a candle by which you may reflect on the life you have lived.
Though its flame burns only briefly, that moment of light will shine so brightly that even death may be forgotten.
This time, it wasn’t the cold, harsh warning tone.
A familiar, clear chime rang in my ears, rousing my body and mind from their endless plunge into darkness.
Just as the System had said, it was a light bright enough to make me forget even death.
**System** All pain you feel is greatly reduced for the duration of Final Rally.
My body stopped trembling under the pain and death closing in by the second.
**System Qi Sense** temporarily increases greatly.
A spark caught in the ashes of my cooling mind.
Fwoosh.
Sudden warmth seeped into my back, and the spark swelled into a flame.
**System** Scorching Yang Qi cradles your exhausted body and heals some of your Internal Injuries.
Two flames could not coexist.
Sooner or later, they would collide and destroy each other.
But if they came from the same root, they were one flame to begin with.
Just like the person who, despite suffering severe Internal Injuries of his own, had shared his qi with me without hesitation.
“What are you waiting for?”
His face was as pale as paper.
Wounds large and small covered his body, and his frame trembled.
But Jeok Cheongang was smiling at me.
He was trying to hold back both his joy that his Disciple had regained a little strength and his sorrow at what that meant.
“Come on.
Let’s go.
Together.”
At that moment—
*Ding.*
**System** A sudden Quest, A Candle in the Wind, or a Flame, has been generated!
Death awaits you.
You cannot refuse this Quest! **Time Limit:** 9 minutes, 59 seconds
Time began to flow again.
I gripped White Flame tightly and took a step forward.
Into the nightmare that wasn’t over yet.
No—toward a reality worse than any nightmare.
*I’ll change it.
I have to.*
If this had been my fight alone, I might have given up already.
I might have leaned my exhausted body against a pile of corpses, looked back on the time I’d left behind, and waited for death to slowly descend.
But—
SHWICK!
I wasn’t alone anymore.
KWA-BOOOOM!
Dazzling light-flames swallowed the enemies whole.
Amid the reddish, overheated earth and the shimmering haze that warped the air, a giant of fire roared.
At the same time, the Slaughter Saint, the Bow Saint, Cheongpung, and the last of the devoted defenders advanced.
Countless civilians followed behind them like a wave, no longer shouting out of desperation but calling a name none of us had expected.
“Charge!
Charge!
Protect the Marquis of Shangshan!”
The great shout shook the battlefield and reached my ears.
A jolt like lightning shot up my spine.
They said they would protect me.
Me, of all people.
Those people with neither a scrap of internal energy nor a proper weapon, gripping sickles and pickaxes in their hands.
They were risking their lives for me—the man who hadn’t even managed to protect his own people.
*Right.
In the end, I couldn’t protect you.*
The beloved faces I would never see again flashed through my mind, and I shot toward the fanatics.
SHWIIK!
My toes.
My waist.
My shoulder.
My arms and wrists.
My body followed movements etched into instinct through countless repetitions and real battles, splitting the raging wind and rain.
Slice!
A single, cool cutting sound crossed the air.
At the same time, more than ten pairs of eyes flew wide open.
The fanatics stared at me in disbelief, clutching their slit throats as they crumpled to the ground.
White Flame’s spearhead, trailing a faint heat, was slower and weaker than it had ever been.
But for some reason, the enemies waiting in its path couldn’t react in time.
Neither could those surging forward to fill the gaps left by their dead comrades.
Stab!
Crack!
I stabbed through everything in my way, pulled my spear free, and twisted it.
My vision was still hazy, but my senses were sharper than ever.
So were the faces and voices that flickered past, one by one, through the thickening mist of blood.
“I’ll join you.
Just make sure the danger pay is generous.”
A pair of fierce eyes, and the willow-leaf saber he always kept close.
But despite his rough appearance, Song Ilseom had always been a reliable comrade and a good person to me.
He complained about the danger and the extra pay on every mission, yet he always fought in the most dangerous places.
He’d left behind the path he’d walked his whole life to protect someone.
I was sure he’d kept that vow until his final moments.
*He must have.
The Song Ilseom I knew would have.*
There was more to a person than what you saw.
That was true of a wandering martial artist others might have seen as nothing but rough and uncouth.
It was true, too, of the two unorthodox faction members I’d unexpectedly formed ties with.
*Am I too late?*
That day in Gansu, when a battle like this one had raged, Sama Pyo had returned from staying with his father through his final moments and asked me that question.
I’d answered without hesitation.
No.
You came right on time.
I’d meant it.
There hadn’t been a trace of a lie in my answer.
Even if he lost his way while wrestling with his choices and took a long detour, Sama Pyo was the sort of person who would find his way back to the right path in the end.
No.
*He was that kind of friend.*
The words echoed endlessly somewhere deep inside me, and I moved as if entranced.
SHWICK!
Like Song Ilseom, I rolled through a pool of blood to evade blades flying at me from every direction.
Slice!
Like Sama Pyo, I ended my enemies’ lives by the cruelest, surest means.
KRRRUNCH!
Like someone else who wasn’t here, I swept through everything in my way with an overwhelming aura as immense as Taishan.
*Taishan believes in Pavilion Master!
Likes him second best in the world, after Lord!*
I pressed forward.
Voices rang like hallucinations amid flying blood and screams.
Familiar faces appeared, one after another, over the enemies collapsing like bundles of straw.
“Would you like to take a walk?”
The memories rose like mist and passed like wind.
The Fire Courtyard of the Yongbong Escort Bureau, shrouded in darkness, and the full moon, unusually bright and large that night.
“Great Hero Jin.”
Her lively voice and light, dancing steps, buoyed by drink.
“Do you think...I can do it?”
And the tears in her eyes that none of it could hide.
“Can I really do it?”
I remembered it all vividly.
Every bit of it.
How I’d made a pointless fuss about the brightness of the moon, then fallen silent at her unexpected question.
Even the moment I’d looked into her tear-filled eyes and spoken.
“It’s all right if you can’t do it well.
You don’t have to force yourself.”
That night, I hadn’t been looking at the moon.
“Wouldn’t that be enough, Young Lady Ju?”
I’d been staring blankly at her eyes, brighter than the full moon and curved like a crescent.
I’d never imagined a day like today would come—or that pitch-black Force would come rushing toward me as it was now.
WHOOOOOSH!
“Get out of the way!”
When had I gotten this far?
Jeok Cheongang’s urgent shout rang out behind me, deep in enemy lines, and a terrible whooshing sound swallowed the noise around us.
But I didn’t flinch.
More precisely, I didn’t have even that much reason left.
I only faced the two streams of energy darkening my already hazy vision.
They were so murky they hardly seemed alive at all.
Not with my eyes, but with my senses.
No—with my heart.
And in the gap between moments slowed to a crawl, I thrust out my spear.
SHWICK!
White Flame’s spearhead, wreathed in a faint blaze, cut through the air.
It pierced space, the darkness beyond it, and a single point.
Fwoosh!
The two streams of Force, which had seemed ready to swallow everything without a trace, scattered helplessly.
I felt the air tremble all around me.
Destruction?
A clash?
No.
The only word for what had just happened was *shattering*.
It was so inexplicable that even I, the one who’d done it, couldn’t understand it.
So perfectly shattered that it enraged even the dead who had just fired Force at me.
—JIN.
TAE.
KYUNG!
The last two Black Ghosts cried out in unison and charged.
A ghostly horse leaped across the dozen or so jang of open air in an instant, casting its shadow over me.
With its blood-red eyes flashing, the now-enlarged Force came crashing down.
KWA-BOOOOOOM!
The rushing blast was violent enough to shake even my already-burst eardrums.
But I wasn’t the only one in its path.
KWAANG!
RUMBLE!
In the blink of an eye, four streaks of light tangled in midair and swelled.
The compressed air exploded, and the earth overturned beneath the tremendous force.
At the heart of it were two superhumans who had rushed to save me.
Stab!
Crack!
The Slaughter Saint’s short knife and ox-hair needles, and the two curved swords clenched in the Bow Saint’s hands, pierced and sliced through the Black Ghosts at lightning speed.
The two Saints gritted their teeth, faces ashen, wringing out what little strength they had left.
The Black Ghosts, meanwhile, refused to fall.
They recovered from mortal wounds and even severed limbs, rising again after dozens of deaths.
Wooooong.
The air trembled.
Countless overlapping spells bolstered the Black Ghosts’ ability to heal and gave them still greater strength and speed.
Enough to face two of the Three Saints, who had fought more fiercely than anyone and were now pushed to their absolute limits.
“Go!
Hurry!”
The Slaughter Saint’s urgent shout pierced my ears.

Or that this wasn’t where I was supposed to die.
*Right.

State your identity and purpose for visiting...
What?
A pleasure house?”
“Third Young Master, I may be a low-ranking Captain, but let me say one thing.”
We’d met as enemies who couldn’t seem to shake each other.
“A scouting squad?
Why me, Third Young Master...?”
“I’ll follow your orders.
Captain—no, Captain, sir.”
Before long, the two of us had fallen into step.
“Now, now, Captain.
What’s there to worry about when you’ve got me?”

Your right arm!

Then we’d become inseparable.

paragraphs: *Beep.*
**System Time Limit:** 5 minutes, 00 seconds
The second hand of a clock granted to only one person on this vast battlefield began to move.
*Flash.*
Space split apart.
It was erased, shattered.
And at its center, four figures hurtled toward one another with all their might.
More precisely, one monster and the three humans standing against it.
Among them was Jin Taekyung.
SHWAAK!
A horrifyingly low whistle of air pierced his ears.
A strike that seemed capable of splitting a mountain, faster than sound itself.
The Red Blade came down at an angle, swift and fierce in equal measure.
Could Jin Taekyung have followed that movement even in his usual condition?
Even if he had, he wouldn’t have dared meet the enormous Force coiling around the blade head-on.
But his senses, honed sharper than ever at the edge of death, were guiding his still-warm body toward a path of survival.
*Rustle.*
The wind stopped. Time slowed.
In Jin Taekyung’s eyes, hazy as a clouded sky, the blood-red blade and its blazing Force passed barely an inch from his face.
*Slice!*
Following the strike’s path, the ground split like tofu mere inches from him.
The wind pressure whipped around like a blade and raked his body, but Jin Taekyung had already forgotten pain. As if entranced, he thrust out his spear.
SHWAAK!
The spearhead pierced straight through space.
At the same time, Jeok Cheongang’s Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist and Cheongpung’s sword cleaved through the wind.
FWOOSH, SHWISH-SHWISH-SHWISH!
Two streams of flame surged forward as one, while sunset-violet Force scattered like flower petals.
Their renown might differ, but each of the three Supreme Peak masters could make the entire Murim tremble at the sound of his name. Together, they launched a perfect combined attack.
But waiting for them was a monster that had already far surpassed the limits of humanity.
HWAASH!
Enormous qi boiled up in an instant.
At the same time, the Blood Lord’s hands, now free of the hilt, struck through space like a bolt of lightning.
KWA-BOOOOM!
Two palms, faster than sound itself.
With a roar as if the sky had split, a blood-red flash erupted around the Blood Lord and swept in every direction.
An overwhelming, destructive force that made no distinction between friend and foe.
RUMBLE, RUMBLE...!
A deep reverberation spread through the devastated space.
It swept past the fanatics’ corpses, scattered in countless chunks of flesh, and reached the three men staggering as they steadied themselves.
“They survived that?”
The Blood Lord muttered despite himself.
He had put tremendous power into that strike—poured a third of his strength into a single attack.
Enough to erase every living thing within a radius of over ten jang and turn the area into a hellscape where only death remained.
Of course, the outcome wasn’t entirely beyond what he’d expected.
No matter how grievously wounded and bloodied they were, a beast was still a beast.
Especially when even the weakest beast among them was called the Huashan Divine Dragon.
No—perhaps this was for the best.
If he’d killed them all with that last strike, he might have been left feeling empty.
“No. Not like this. Not so easily.”
The Blood Lord let out a low laugh and took a step forward.
*Rustle.*
Something felt wrong.
He raised his hand to see what it was, and his gaze turned cold.
Blood.
Beads welled up from a shallow split in his skin—too slight to even call a wound—and ran across his palm.
The very hand that had just met someone’s attack head-on.
“This is...”
The Blood Lord trailed off and slowly lifted his head.
And saw him.
One man, covered in blood from head to toe, struggling to catch his breath.
His face was so pale he could have collapsed at any moment, yet his eyes still held a flame that hadn’t died out.
*Jin Taekyung.*
The Blood Lord ran his red tongue over his lips.
How had this happened?
He’d been sure he had blocked the attack.
None of their strikes could have broken the Palm Force gathered in his hands.
And yet—
“Yes. This is how it should be. You ought to manage at least this much.”
The Blood Lord murmured softly, almost to himself.
The light that had dimmed in his eyes flared to life, and his wavering lips curled into a gentle smile.
At this moment, he was truly enjoying himself.
Carelessness? Fear of what might happen?
He’d felt none of that from the start.
He had simply been certain.
Certain that he could hunt the prey before him, whether it was a powerless rabbit or a beast hiding its fangs.
Though it had been only a single exchange, the Blood Lord had realized once again just how immense the power within him was at this moment.
And how boundless.
*Squelch.*
As the monster stepped forward, the pool of blood at his feet, spread out like a small lake, swirled and rushed toward him.
SHWAAAAA!
The Blood Lord greedily swallowed the blood. Intoxicated by the strength surging through him anew, the monster shot through space like a flash of light.
*Drip.*
A single drop of blood fell behind him.
The Blood Lord’s confidence was no arrogance.
He moved faster than anyone else on the battlefield, and the immense blood-red Force bursting from his Red Blade was enough to make anyone who saw it think of the word *unprecedented*.
At least at this moment.
He was the strongest predator on this vast battlefield, an absolute being no one could oppose.

With even the two giants among the Three Saints pinned down by the enemies’ fierce counterattack, he was powerful enough to crush the three Supreme Peak masters—each already seriously injured—in an instant.
Jin Taekyung knew that better than anyone. Which was why he couldn’t understand what was happening.
SHWEEEE!
Why—
KRRRCH!
Why was that terrifying Force, powerful enough to split a mountain—
SHWAAK!
Why was the Blood Lord’s movement, seemingly faster than wind, sound, even light—
WHOOOOSH!
Missing him by a hair every time, every single moment?
Why couldn’t it touch him?
“You—!”
Jin Taekyung didn’t hear the monster’s voice echoing through the blade-sharp wind.
No. More precisely, he couldn’t hear it.
Amid the flashes that continually washed across his hazy vision, he simply kept moving as if entranced.
*Slice!*
He brought his advancing foot back to where it had been and ducked his head. The blood-red Force passed overhead.
A nearly flawless dodge, without a moment’s hesitation.
Jin Taekyung himself didn’t know how he had evaded such a swift, ferocious strike. He didn’t know why he’d moved that way, either.
He just felt he had to.
It all seemed perfectly natural.
Like the sun rising in the east each morning, or water flowing downhill.
Like a duel whose every move had been carefully arranged in advance.
But that was true only for Jin Taekyung.
*Rustle, SHWEEEE!*
The Red Blade was descending toward the crown of his head when it abruptly changed direction.
KWAANG!
With a single deafening crash, Cheongpung, who had rushed in to attack from the blind spot, dropped to one knee and spat up blood.
Above him, the Red Blade had wiped away the path of the Thirty-Six Plum Blossom Swords in an instant. It crashed down like lightning and bore upon his sword with the weight of ten thousand geun.
CRACK.
The violet Force faded rapidly, and hairline fractures spread across the blade like a spiderweb.
As Cheongpung swallowed blood and summoned all his strength, the Blood Lord’s dark-red light poured down on him.
“You dare, you little—!”
The monster’s earlier delight had turned to anger.
Why? How?
With martial prowess this immense, and Jin Taekyung clearly dying, why couldn’t he finish this simple fight whose outcome was so certain?
And even when victory was all but decided, why did that damned brat before him keep resisting to the end?
Just as he had on that day at Mount Song, when he’d inflicted a humiliation that was like a brand upon the Blood Lord.
“Fine. I’ll kill you first.”
The Blood Lord spat out the words. The blood-red Force swelled and dug into Cheongpung’s blade.
Then—
HWAASH!
Heat swept in from behind him. The Blood Lord released the hilt without hesitation and thrust out a fist.
KWA-BOOOOM!
Two fists collided in midair.
White light-flames and blood-red Force charged at each other, each trying to devour the other.
But the difference in their power was already clear. Through the thick heat haze, the Blood Lord bared his teeth at Jeok Cheongang.
“Get lost, old man.”
*BOOM!*
Blood-red Force swallowed the flames. With an explosion, Jeok Cheongang was sent flying helplessly and rolled across the ground.
Right where someone had been standing just moments before.
*...What?*
The realization came in an instant.
An alarm rang in the Blood Lord’s mind, and a current of air crossed the space between them.
*Fwoosh.*
A whistle of air so low and faint it raised goose bumps.
In time slowed to a crawl, the Blood Lord turned. Jin Taekyung filled his blood-red eyes, thrusting out his spear with a hazy gaze.
The Blood Lord couldn’t even get out the word *How?*
Nor could he think how he, overwhelmingly powerful as he was, had lost track of the presence of a bloodied wretch sinking deeper into death with every passing moment.
Jin Taekyung was no different.
*Now.*
It was as if someone else, someone he didn’t know, were whispering in his ear.
His vision was clouded white, and he couldn’t see a thing.
Time was running out. A horrible weariness—and an even stronger feeling of death—was seeping into his body.
*Shhk.*
Jin Taekyung thrust out his spear smoothly.
The shouts and screams of friend and foe, ringing out without pause even now. The cold clang of steel. The sound of a trumpet, now drawing close.
Even the palm the Blood Lord thrust out on instinct.
Nothing could stop him.
Leaving it all behind, as if it had been decided from the beginning, Jin Taekyung let the flames deep inside his body flow toward a single point.
*Pshk.*
The spearhead, carrying a faint heat, pierced the palm wrapped in Force and drove on through.
Past that very hand, whose wound, for some reason, still hadn’t healed.
KRRRCH!
The monster’s eyes flew wide, bulging as they filled with shock.

He’d been sure he had blocked the attack.
None of their strikes could have broken the Palm Force gathered in his hands.
And yet—
“Yes.
This is how it should be.
You ought to manage at least this much.”
The Blood Lord murmured softly, almost to himself.
The light that had dimmed in his eyes flared to life, and his wavering lips curled into a gentle smile.
At this moment, he was truly enjoying himself.
Carelessness?
Fear of what might happen?
He’d felt none of that from the start.
He had simply been certain.
Certain that he could hunt the prey before him, whether it was a powerless rabbit or a beast hiding its fangs.
Though it had been only a single exchange, the Blood Lord had realized once again just how immense the power within him was at this moment.
And how boundless.
*Squelch.*
As the monster stepped forward, the pool of blood at his feet, spread out like a small lake, swirled and rushed toward him.
SHWAAAAA!
The Blood Lord greedily swallowed the blood.
Intoxicated by the strength surging through him anew, the monster shot through space like a flash of light.
*Drip.*
A single drop of blood fell behind him.
The Blood Lord’s confidence was no arrogance.
He moved faster than anyone else on the battlefield, and the immense blood-red Force bursting from his Red Blade was enough to make anyone who saw it think of the word *unprecedented*.
At least at this moment.
He was the strongest predator on this vast battlefield, an absolute being no one could oppose.

With even the two giants among the Three Saints pinned down by the enemies’ fierce counterattack, he was powerful enough to crush the three Supreme Peak masters—each already seriously injured—in an instant.
Jin Taekyung knew that better than anyone.
Which was why he couldn’t understand what was happening.
SHWEEEE!
Why—
KRRRCH!
Why was that terrifying Force, powerful enough to split a mountain—
SHWAAK!
Why was the Blood Lord’s movement, seemingly faster than wind, sound, even light—
WHOOOOSH!
Missing him by a hair every time, every single moment?
Why couldn’t it touch him?
“You—!”
Jin Taekyung didn’t hear the monster’s voice echoing through the blade-sharp wind.
No.
More precisely, he couldn’t hear it.
Amid the flashes that continually washed across his hazy vision, he simply kept moving as if entranced.
*Slice!*
He brought his advancing foot back to where it had been and ducked his head.
The blood-red Force passed overhead.
A nearly flawless dodge, without a moment’s hesitation.
Jin Taekyung himself didn’t know how he had evaded such a swift, ferocious strike.
He didn’t know why he’d moved that way, either.
He just felt he had to.
It all seemed perfectly natural.
Like the sun rising in the east each morning, or water flowing downhill.
Like a duel whose every move had been carefully arranged in advance.
But that was true only for Jin Taekyung.
*Rustle, SHWEEEE!*
The Red Blade was descending toward the crown of his head when it abruptly changed direction.
KWAANG!
With a single deafening crash, Cheongpung, who had rushed in to attack from the blind spot, dropped to one knee and spat up blood.
Above him, the Red Blade had wiped away the path of the Thirty-Six Plum Blossom Swords in an instant.
It crashed down like lightning and bore upon his sword with the weight of ten thousand geun.
CRACK.
The violet Force faded rapidly, and hairline fractures spread across the blade like a spiderweb.
As Cheongpung swallowed blood and summoned all his strength, the Blood Lord’s dark-red light poured down on him.
“You dare, you little—!”
The monster’s earlier delight had turned to anger.
Why?
How?
With martial prowess this immense, and Jin Taekyung clearly dying, why couldn’t he finish this simple fight whose outcome was so certain?
And even when victory was all but decided, why did that damned brat before him keep resisting to the end?
Just as he had on that day at Mount Song, when he’d inflicted a humiliation that was like a brand upon the Blood Lord.
“Fine.
I’ll kill you first.”
The Blood Lord spat out the words.
The blood-red Force swelled and dug into Cheongpung’s blade.
Then—
HWAASH!
Heat swept in from behind him.
The Blood Lord released the hilt without hesitation and thrust out a fist.
KWA-BOOOOM!
Two fists collided in midair.
White light-flames and blood-red Force charged at each other, each trying to devour the other.
But the difference in their power was already clear.
Through the thick heat haze, the Blood Lord bared his teeth at Jeok Cheongang.
“Get lost, old man.”
*BOOM!*
Blood-red Force swallowed the flames.
With an explosion, Jeok Cheongang was sent flying helplessly and rolled across the ground.
Right where someone had been standing just moments before.
*...What?*
The realization came in an instant.
An alarm rang in the Blood Lord’s mind, and a current of air crossed the space between them.
*Fwoosh.*
A whistle of air so low and faint it raised goose bumps.
In time slowed to a crawl, the Blood Lord turned.
Jin Taekyung filled his blood-red eyes, thrusting out his spear with a hazy gaze.
The Blood Lord couldn’t even get out the word *How?*
Nor could he think how he, overwhelmingly powerful as he was, had lost track of the presence of a bloodied wretch sinking deeper into death with every passing moment.
Jin Taekyung was no different.
*Now.*
It was as if someone else, someone he didn’t know, were whispering in his ear.
His vision was clouded white, and he couldn’t see a thing.
Time was running out.
A horrible weariness—and an even stronger feeling of death—was seeping into his body.
*Shhk.*
Jin Taekyung thrust out his spear smoothly.
The shouts and screams of friend and foe, ringing out without pause even now.
The cold clang of steel.
The sound of a trumpet, now drawing close.
Even the palm the Blood Lord thrust out on instinct.
Nothing could stop him.
Leaving it all behind, as if it had been decided from the beginning, Jin Taekyung let the flames deep inside his body flow toward a single point.
*Pshk.*
The spearhead, carrying a faint heat, pierced the palm wrapped in Force and drove on through.
Past that very hand, whose wound, for some reason, still hadn’t healed.
KRRRCH!
The monster’s eyes flew wide, bulging as they filled with shock.

chapters.title: Chapter 1125
paragraphs: KRRRCH!
At the ghastly sound of flesh tearing, the Blood Lord felt as though the world had stopped.
*Ah.*
Hot. Distant.
His vision wavered. The noise around him seemed impossibly far away.
Everything felt so unfamiliar that he wondered if all that had happened until now had been a dream.
If not for the terrible heat scorching his flesh and bones, he might truly have believed it.
No.
If not for the face he could see beyond the acrid smoke and shimmering haze of the flames.
*Cough.*
Fresh blood spilled past his lips.
Through pain so fierce it turned his vision white, the Blood Lord coughed up blood mixed with bits of his innards and looked at the young man before him.
The reckless young moth, now joined to him by a single spear.
He parted his blood-soaked lips.
“How?”
It was a short question, but there was much behind the genuine confusion in his eyes. Jin Taekyung answered.
“I don’t know either.”
“What?”
“I just... knew. It felt natural.”
His voice astonishingly calm, Jin Taekyung went on.
“Every move you’d make. And what I had to do.”
“That’s all.”
The Blood Lord’s eyes widened before he even realized it.
Because of the pain burning through him?
No.
The accursed spearhead had pierced his palm and driven deep into his body, spreading heat through him. Compared to the shock he felt now, that was nothing.
*He knew? Everything I’d do?*
A moment ago, he would have scoffed at such absurd words.
His power had grown beyond its limits, and the gulf between them was so vast that even the word *possibility* had become meaningless.
But—
*He isn’t lying. He isn’t boasting.*
The moment their eyes met, the Blood Lord understood instinctively.
A truth unbearably cruel to him.
And the fact that he had been trying desperately to deny it.
“So there was no point in asking in the first place.”
“Yeah.”
Jin Taekyung gave a small nod, then added faintly,
“At least in that moment, I was stronger than you.”
Hearing his enemy say what he could no longer deny sent a shiver down the Blood Lord’s spine.
Countless emotions swept through him, overwhelming even the pain.
Bitter defeat. Fear of something he could not comprehend. And something entirely at odds with both.
Deep relief and joy.
With his whole body, he knew he had made the right choice.
*Lord of Heaven, my revered master. Are you watching? Can you hear me?*
The Blood Lord looked up. He whispered toward his own heaven, hidden behind the unceasing rain and dark clouds.
*My choice was never wrong.*
The truth was, anxiety had been stirring in a corner of his heart.
Unwavering loyalty was not the only reason he had decided to eliminate Jin Taekyung.
He’d been disappointed. Resentful.
His master seemed to spare no thought for the servants who gave their lives in his service.
And, absurdly, he’d been jealous of Jin Taekyung, who received something close to affection from that same master.
So he’d wanted to kill him.
He’d told himself he was removing an obstacle that kept standing in Dark Heaven’s way, hiding his reasons behind the word *loyalty*.
But now he no longer had to.
Here, today, Jin Taekyung had proved for himself why he had to die.
And die he would.
“Blazing Flame Divine Dragon Jin Taekyung. I’ll admit it. You deserve to be called a Divine Dragon.”
The Blood Lord whispered the words to Jin Taekyung without a trace of falsehood.
If anything, *Divine Dragon* seemed inadequate.
Even at death’s door, Jin Taekyung had fallen into a Trance and drawn closer to a higher enlightenment. Remembering it sent a chill through the Blood Lord.
“Yes, you were right. In that moment, you were terrifyingly strong. Strong enough that even I couldn’t stop you.”
He didn’t know what profound enlightenment Jin Taekyung had gained.
He didn’t know how he could fight so fiercely with his life hanging by a thread.
Or how a spearhead carrying no more than a handful of qi had broken through his formidable Force.
But—
“None of that matters.”
By then, the Blood Lord was smiling.
Wearing a bright smile no defeated man could have worn, he grasped the spearhead buried deep inside him.
The spearhead of White Flame, lodged a handspan from his heart.
*Squish. Crack.*
Blood burst out with a ghastly sound of tearing flesh.
The Blood Lord pulled the spearhead free with a hand wrapped in dense Palm Force and muttered,
“I thought I was dead. In that moment, I truly did.”
Jin Taekyung’s final attack, thrust with all his strength, had been a strike the Blood Lord could not have stopped.
If Jin Taekyung’s internal energy hadn’t run dry at just that moment—
If the spearhead hadn’t lost power and veered off course because of it—the Blood Lord would have died.
But he hadn’t.
*This is Heaven’s will.*
Joy welled up from deep within him.
The heavens above had chosen him, not Jin Taekyung.
*Not that paltry heaven you believe in. This is the will of the true Heaven I serve!*
At that moment, a lightning-like thrill made him forget his pain. The Blood Lord pulled his pierced hand free and twisted the spear shaft.
SHWIK—KRRRCH!
The shaft spun violently, its force impossible to resist.
White Flame snapped through the cloth its owner had tied tightly around it so he would not lose his beloved weapon. Then it tore free of Jin Taekyung’s grasp, leaving his hand covered in blood.
*Splatter.*
Unable to withstand the force, Jin Taekyung was driven backward. He fell, unable even to keep himself upright.
The Blood Lord stepped toward him without hesitation.
Or rather, he tried to.
Before he could, another Divine Dragon—one raised on the slopes of Huashan, not beside a pond—charged in with a roar.
“No!”
SHWAAAAK!
Sunset spread through the darkness. Force bloomed along the sword’s cracked blade and scattered into thirty-six petals.
The strike was beautiful enough to draw gasps from anyone who saw it.
But the desperation behind it was greater than ever, making it all the more heartbreaking.
FWOOM!
The blood-red Force that filled the space was strong enough to cut down not just the petals, but an entire forest.
KWA-BOOOOM!
The earth shook with a deafening crash.
Beyond a cloud of dust that even the pounding rain could not settle, a figure staggered upright and stood before the fallen Jin Taekyung.
Not one figure, but two.
“Where do you think you’re going? *Cough.*”
Jeok Cheongang and Cheongpung stood in his way again, both covered in blood. The Blood Lord’s red eyes darkened.
“Mount Beimang.”
He raised the spear that now belonged to him at an angle and added,
“Of course, you’re the ones going there.”
*Hummm.*
The spearhead, parted from its master, let out a sorrowful hum.
*Shhhhh.*
I stared blankly at the dark sky stretching beyond the endless rain.
*This is Heaven’s will.*
The Blood Lord’s voice still echoed in my ears.
*Not that paltry heaven you believe in. This is the will of the true Heaven I serve!*
Remembering the joy in those blood-red eyes, I muttered to myself,
*Yeah. Maybe it is.*
I’d done everything I could.
No—all of us had fought with everything we had.
Until there was nothing left to give.
Until I couldn’t even feel regret or anger.
But...
*I never followed the will of Heaven.*
Quietly, desperately, I struggled.
*Squish.*
With my crushed, broken hand, I gripped a clod of dark red earth mixed with blood as hard as I could and pushed myself up.
I had to. There was no other choice.
For the people even now collapsing, their blood scattering around them.
They were the paltry heaven the Blood Lord had mocked.
*BOOM!*
A fierce crack split the air.
Through my blurred vision, I saw Jeok Cheongang stagger and drop to one knee. Cheongpung was flung away like a cannonball and rolled across the ground.
And the monster, having torn down every obstacle in his way, came toward me.
*Splash.*
One step, then another.
His blood-red gaze grew clearer as the distance closed. I put every bit of strength I had into getting up.
Like a baby whose earliest movements I couldn’t remember, I rolled onto my front, planted my hands and knees on the ground, and somehow hauled my swaying body to its feet.
By then, the Blood Lord was close enough that his eyes seemed to burn red as the sun. The moment I met them—
*Inventory open. Summon.*
From the boundless storehouse granted to me alone in this vast world, I drew a finely sharpened dagger and thrust it forward.
At the same time, a low, mocking laugh reached my ears.
“As expected.”
*Crack.*
I felt no pain, but the sound told me enough.
The Blood Lord had caught my wrist in a flash and crushed it beyond any hope of recovery.
But he wasn’t the only one who could predict his opponent.
*Slip. Tap.*
Ignoring the pain erased by my final rally, I kicked the dagger’s hilt with my toe as it fell from my grasp.
*Thud.*
With a cool, tearing sound, the dagger sank deep into flesh.
The Blood Lord’s eyes flew wide. He looked down at the blade buried in his shin and licked his lips.
“Impressive. Truly impressive. But that is why...”
Without a moment’s hesitation, he whipped his remaining leg like a lash.
“I can never let you live.”
KRRRCH!
White bone burst through mangled flesh.
Having crippled one of my arms and both my legs, the Blood Lord shot out a hand like lightning and seized my throat.
*Crack.*
Bones shifted, and my vision darkened.
As I gasped for breath, his low voice reached my ears.
“We’ve been bound by a long, ill-fated connection, Blazing Flame Divine Dragon Jin Taekyung.”
At that moment—
*FWOOSH.*
Like a last candle burning as a life flashed before it, my vision turned white even as it fell into pitch-black darkness.
No.
Perhaps the color was deeper and redder than sunset.
*Slash.*
