chapters.title: Chapter 1126
paragraphs: It was a low, faint sound—one no one would have noticed under ordinary circumstances.
Nothing beside the ceaseless roar of battle shaking heaven and earth.
Just the sound of wind brushing past somewhere.
But to someone else, it struck like a sudden storm, an unstoppable bolt of lightning.
*Shhk.*
The cold slicing sound reached the Blood Lord’s ears a moment late. His lips parted before he knew it.
The joy that had filled his eyes moments ago gave way to confusion. In his blood-red pupils, a fine line appeared across his arm.
Before he could make sense of it, blood welled through his skin and raced along the line.
*PSSSHHH!*
A fountain of blood shot into the air. The Blood Lord could only stare, eyes wide, as his arm fell away in a spray of crimson.
Beside the severed arm collapsed the man who had barely escaped death.
*Splatter!*
The moment Jin Taekyung’s already-crippled body crumpled to the ground, time began to move again.
Yet even with the man he had wanted so desperately to kill lying at his feet, the Blood Lord couldn’t move.
And he wasn’t the only one who had stopped.
Taekyung’s master, reaching a trembling hand toward his disciple, who lay in a deep pool of blood facing death.
The Bow Saint and the Slaughter Saint, who had finally shaken off countless enemies, including the two Black Ghosts, and were racing toward him with not an instant to spare.
Cheongpung, driving the blade of his sword—now only a handspan long—deep into the ground to force himself upright.
They all felt it. At the same time, they saw it.
Beyond the curtain of wind and rain, someone’s figure wavered into view.
*Shhhhh.*
Through the endless rain walked a black-clad figure. At a movement of his fingertips, an ancient silver blade swept down.
*Shhhk.*
In that instant, the world split apart.
The rain and wind.
The air and qi within them.
And the darkness.
*SHWAAK!*
The dazzling flash that filled their eyes was deeper than sunset and as brilliant as dawn.
Just like that day a year ago, burned into the Blood Lord’s mind like a brand.
*This is...*
In a moment so brief it seemed time had been cut into slivers, the Blood Lord froze, eyes wide. Someone’s presence flashed through his mind.
A name that could not—and must not—appear here today.
A man without peer when it came to the sword, known as the Number One Sword Under Heaven.
A man whose realm had reached the heavens, known as the Sword Saint.
“Mae Jonghak—!”
The name burst from the Blood Lord’s lips like a scream.
*FWOOSH!*
Within the swelling flash, dozens of strands of purple Force bloomed.
*Tap.*
Beneath their dazzling petals, a hand suddenly reached out and touched the Blood Lord’s foot.
No—
*KRAK!*
It seized the monster’s ankle with all its strength as he tried to turn away.
Just like that day when Mount Song was stained with blood.
In the monster’s widened, blood-red eyes, a young man’s faintly smiling face was reflected.
And the purple flash that had finally reached him.
*KWA-BOOOOM!*
Being unable to feel pain is both a curse and a reason for despair.
Pain is proof that you’re alive and breathing.
For a living person to feel none means death is near.
But that is only one side of it.
For someone who has watched death draw close and accepted it deep in their heart, the absence of pain might be one last blessing instead.
No—it must be.
At least right now, Jin Taekyung was more grateful than ever that he couldn’t feel pain.
Both his legs were crushed. One arm was shattered. Yet he could still move, and that made him so happy he could have cried.
*KRAK!*
Where had that strength come from?
Even Taekyung didn’t know.

He had reached out as if bewitched, as though something were controlling him. Somehow, the strength in the only one of his four limbs that wasn’t broken had been enough to stop the monster in his tracks.
*I got... him.*
Taekyung smiled.
Through his blurred vision, he raised the corners of his mouth at the Blood Lord staring down at him.
And then—
*KWA-BOOOOM!*
A tremendous roar battered his ears. A dreadful explosion of power shook everything around him.
Yet inside, he was as calm as a deserted lakeshore.
*This is enough.*
The flash swallowed his vision as he murmured to himself.
Yes. It was enough.
He had done all he could. He had no regrets.
No—he couldn’t allow himself even one.

If any regret remained, he wouldn’t be able to leave in peace. He would call out the names of the family and friends he wanted to see, blame himself for failing to see things through, and bawl like a child.
But now it was all right.
Mae Jonghak had come.
With the Martial God—the heavens—gone, the Sword Saint Mae Jonghak was the highest star in the sky and the greatest under heaven in this era.
Taekyung had an inkling of how Mae Jonghak could have appeared here when he should have been protecting the Central Plains as Alliance Leader. He let the thought go.
He was simply grateful for the hope that this unexpected savior could defeat the monster and save everyone who remained.
*Thank goodness. Really.*
With that hollow thought swallowed deep in his heart, Taekyung’s eyelids began to close.
*CRACK!*
Amid the fading roar and flash, a hand shot out like lightning and seized his throat.
*Drip. Drip.*
Something hot and sticky fell onto his forehead.
Above him, the monster’s blood-red eyes still burned.
“How dare... *cough*... the likes of you...”
The Blood Lord growled like a wounded beast.
He had to swallow mouthfuls of blood just to speak. Wounds deep enough to expose bone covered his body. Yet he was still alive.
He lifted his dying prey like a trophy and bared his bloodstained teeth again.
“Did you think you could defeat me? Me, who inherited the Lord of Heaven’s mighty power?”
Just then, a faint voice escaped Taekyung’s lips, which were turning white under the grip around his throat.
“Yeah. You son of a bitch.”
“...What?”
“I think he can.”
Taekyung smiled faintly at the Blood Lord, who stared at him in silence. At those blood-red pupils, now trembling ever so slightly.
And he understood. Anger wasn’t the only thing behind that tremor.
“You’re scared, aren’t you? Of what’s happening.”
“Yeah. Even a bastard like you has to be scared. That’s why you’re pulling this cheap hostage stunt.”
*Grind.*
The Blood Lord gritted his teeth without realizing it.
A cheap hostage stunt?
Bullshit.
It had to be bullshit.
So why couldn’t he answer? Why did his grip loosen instead?
Taekyung’s mocking voice reached his ears.
“Look around. Then you’ll know whether you’re the hunter right now—or the prey.”
The Blood Lord didn’t answer. He didn’t look around, either.
He couldn’t bring himself to.
He didn’t want to admit that five Supreme Peak masters, led by the Sword Saint, had surrounded him. Or that he had seized Taekyung to hold them back, if only for a moment, and buy himself time.
*At this rate... I’ll die.*
He could feel it against his skin. He knew it instinctively.
That cruel truth, impossible to believe and unbearable to accept, pierced him to the core.
*Why?*
He couldn’t understand how the power bestowed on him by his great master had left him in an instant.
Gone. All of it.
The healing that might as well have been immortality. The qi that had surged endlessly from blood.
Only the strength left over after that power vanished kept him standing.
*But I will not die.*
The Blood Lord bit his lip, trembling with shame.
He thought of the last hope he had left—the final hammer blow that would end this terrible, immense battle.
“Watch closely. See who survives here today.”
He spat the words at Taekyung, who was still smiling.
*Bwoooooo!*
A powerful trumpet call shook the battlefield. At last, the hope he had waited for appeared.
*Rrrrrumble!*
Countless footsteps shook the earth. Enormous flags waved high, as though they might pierce the sky.
Tens of thousands of troops in all manner of dress marched beneath them. Everyone could clearly see the words on the two flags flying overhead.
Yangtze River Channel League.
And Green Forest Alliance.
A wave of unseen shock swept across the battlefield.
“Ah. Ahhh...”
The suicide squad and civilians, who had fought the invaders with everything they had, froze like statues.
“Lord of Heaven!”

The Dark Heaven fanatics, who had held the battle at a stalemate despite a counterattack backed by overwhelming numbers, began chanting the eight-character invocation praising the Lord of Heaven as if entranced.
The Blood Lord watched with joy in his eyes.
“In heaven and on earth, all demons bow...!”
A shiver ran down his spine. He turned to Taekyung, eager to see the despair on his face as soon as possible—and for as long as possible.
Then he realized something was wrong.
His last hope might have been despair all along.
“A meeting when the Yellow River runs clear.”
“What... did you say?”
“Someone sent me a letter once. Said she’d wait for the Yellow River to run clear. That we’d meet again then.”
Taekyung remembered the letter Wolhwa had sent while he was staying in Gansu.
A single line he had long since forgotten.
Hoping that someday we can meet when the Yellow River runs clear, Wolhwa.
Wearing his brightest smile yet, Taekyung lifted a trembling hand and pointed east.
“Looks like this is the moment.”
More precisely, he pointed to another enormous flag slowly rising behind the two at the head of the army.
Through rain falling hard enough to clear the Yellow River, three characters came into view.
Murim Alliance.
The Blood Lord stood frozen, eyes wide.
Taekyung made his final move.
*KRAK!*
The Blood Lord couldn’t stop Taekyung’s teeth from sinking into his neck like a beast’s.
Through the overwhelming pain, the world slowly tilted.
*Splatter.*
The monster, stripped of all the power he had been granted, finally crashed into the pool of blood.

chapters.title: Chapter 1127
paragraphs: It all began in an instant—and ended in one.
But a moment that flashed past like lightning could feel like ten years to someone caught inside it.
*KWA-DRRRK!*
With a grisly sound of flesh tearing, the Blood Lord’s body shuddered.
Hot. Distant.
That was all. That was everything.
*How?*
The Blood Lord couldn’t understand.
Why hadn’t the palm strike he’d thrown on instinct brought his opponent down before those beastlike teeth sank into his neck?
Why was the Murim Alliance’s banner flying above those damn bandits?
And as he felt his body, no longer under his control, being pushed helplessly backward, he muttered to himself:
*Well, it doesn’t matter anymore.*
*Splatter.*
Sticky blood sprayed. Time, which had stopped, began to move again.
Lying in a pool of blood as broad as a pond, the Blood Lord looked up at the sky filling his vision.
*Was it always this dark?*
In truth, he already knew the answer.
The world was unchanged. Only he had changed.
The monster’s pupils were still as red as blood, but even now, his fading gaze could no longer make out light from shadow.
A world gone entirely black.
Beyond it, all the Blood Lord could feel was the rain pouring down without pause and the chill of blood soaking his body.
No. That wasn’t all.
Someone’s voice echoed in his ears.
“You... still listening, you son of a bitch?”
Jin Taekyung.
It was him.
He spat out the flesh and blood filling his mouth and smiled, though he was panting as if he might collapse at any moment. Even forcing out one syllable at a time looked like a struggle.
“I can hear it. Clear as day.”
The Blood Lord couldn’t answer.
He could only swallow the bloody phlegm rising in his throat and listen to the roar shaking heaven and earth.
—Destroy the Demonic Path and restore Heaven!
Destroy demons and set Heaven right.
It was the old Murim Alliance’s banner, the vow it had upheld to the very end—and the hoof that had trampled its invaders.
Just as it was doing now.
*KWA-DRRRRCK!*
He couldn’t see.
But he could picture it from the sound alone.
The fanatics wavering at this unexpected turn. The forest of countless spears and blades closing over them.
The undying will and desperate sense of duty carried by every one of those weapons.
The Blood Lord barely managed to force out the word.
He wanted to ask Jin Taekyung. All of them.
What were they fighting so desperately for?
What could they hold so dear that they would give their lives to protect it?
Jin Taekyung answered that short question, laden with meaning, in two even shorter words.
“Fuck off.”
“So you don’t want to tell me.”
“I’m sick of it. You’re hardly the first idiot like this I’ve met. I’ve gone out of my way to explain it before, and none of you understood a damn thing.”
“I see. So that’s how it was.”
The Blood Lord managed a weak nod. Jin Taekyung watched him, then asked abruptly, “What about you?”
“What?”
“What the hell were *you* doing all this for?”
The Blood Lord fell silent for a moment. His own silence startled him.
Was it the exhaustion weighing down his eyelids?
Or the sense of death drawing closer with every passing second?
“...I don’t know.”
He should have said that everything he’d done was for the Lord of Heaven. That he would do anything for his great master, and would swear loyalty even if he died here and became a ghost.
But the faithful servant’s lips gave a different answer.
“I don’t... know anymore. Anything.”
With that faint murmur, the Blood Lord looked up at the sky.
Where was the heaven he had trusted so completely?
Would his master, somewhere impossibly far away, feel even a trace of grief when he heard that his most faithful servant had died?
*Of course not.*
A faint smile touched the Blood Lord’s lips.
Yes.
He had tried to deny it, but he already knew the answer.
The Lord of Heaven hadn’t wavered when the four Demon Lords and the Demon Empress died one after another. Nor when word came that countless followers had been wiped out.
Not for a single moment.
It was almost as if he’d wanted it to happen.
*Then did you want this lowly servant to die, too?*
The Blood Lord reached a trembling hand toward the sky.
Too far. He couldn’t touch it.
Just like the distance between him and the Lord of Heaven. No matter how hard he’d tried, they had never grown any closer.
*Ah.*
The Blood Lord swallowed a groan.
He had believed in and revered the Lord of Heaven. But the light pouring down from that heaven had always shone on one person alone.
On the owner of those blazing eyes, who could no longer lift a finger yet still watched him die without looking away.
*Jin Taekyung.*
At that moment—
*Shhk!*
The fingers that had been reaching desperately through empty air curled like hooks and plunged downward.
The monster’s final strike carried anger and hatred he no longer knew whom to direct at, and one last duty that now seemed futile.
Just as it was about to pierce Jin Taekyung between the eyes—
*KRAK!*
A hand caked in dried blood blocked it.
The bones in the monster’s fingers shattered, joint by joint, and his flesh and blood burned.
*Hiss.*
A haze rose with the smell of scorching flesh.
Beyond it, the old master who had returned to his Disciple’s side parted his lips.
“How dare you lay a hand on him?”
Through heat that penetrated even his dulled senses, the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, looked down at the monster trembling in pain.
And he wasn’t alone.
The Bow Saint and the Slaughter Saint. Sword Saint Mae Jonghak and Cheongpung. Others, too, who had rushed over covered in blood.
They surrounded the monster like reapers, like iron towers.
They blotted out the sky that had been his whole world and became a broad, sturdy roof sheltering someone else from the rain.
That was why Jin Taekyung could laugh aloud.
He remembered the monster’s joyful cry just moments ago.
“See them?”
He spoke emphatically to the monster, its blood-red eyes wide open.
“Those faces you’re looking at? That’s the paltry heaven I believed in.”
What could the monster say?
What more could he do?
He blinked helplessly, swallowed the blood spilling over his lips, and forced out a few last words.
“Rejoice... all you want. This will be the last time.”
As his vision darkened to pitch-black, Jin Taekyung’s voice reached him, faint and distant.
“I was planning to.”
A bitter smile touched Jin Taekyung’s lips. The monster breathed his last, and that breath dispersed into the air.
*Ding.*
A clear chime rang out like the bell of an ancient cathedral, announcing that everything was over.
It carried boundless joy—and even greater sorrow.
There’s a saying: animals leave their hides behind when they die, and people leave their names.
But a monster that’s neither animal nor human can leave behind a massive amount of EXP.
*Ding. Ding. Ding.*
The familiar clear chime rang nonstop in my ears.
If everyone could hear it instead of just me, I bet it would’ve carried for hundreds of ri.
*That bastard sure knew how to make an exit.*
The Blood Lord’s end was miserable and shabby, but the System’s payouts were lavish.
How many times had I leveled up in that brief instant?
Three? More?
I wasn’t sure.
All I knew was that several Quests had been completed the moment the Blood Lord died, and I’d turned off notifications after my third Level Up.
*Any other time, I’d have passed out from happiness.*
No, I definitely would have. Leveling up had become a once-in-a-blue-moon event. Doing it several times in a row was nothing short of a miracle.
But none of it meant anything to me now.
The chimes that should have sounded like heaven were just irritating noise. Even having my crushed flesh and broken bones heal offered only a little comfort.
One small, final comfort: I could pat someone’s trembling shoulder.
“Quit bawling. Your dick’ll fall off.”
Cheongpung didn’t stop crying at my attempt to comfort him. He just spoke through his sobs.
He said he was sorry. And thanked me, too.
But my farewell to Cheongpung—surely our last—was brief.
Unlike him, I still had so many last faces left to see.
And once I’d seen them all, my own final moment would be waiting.
**System** Time Limit: 5 minutes 35 seconds
I gazed calmly at the hourglass of the final rally, still hanging in the air.
Truthfully, I’d already guessed. Ever since I’d launched One Annihilation at the Blood Lord.
There was a limit to how much a Level Up could heal, and the injuries I’d suffered from One Annihilation’s backlash went beyond it.
Now that what was called innate qi—or original true qi—had been damaged, my fate was like a boat that had crossed a river with no way back.
*The System warned me, and I accepted it.*
That was all.
I’d taken the step I had to take, even knowing death might be waiting for me.
I had been prepared for this. If anything, I was grateful for the way things had turned out.
Without the healing from those Level Ups, without the extra time it had given me in the final rally, I wouldn’t even have been able to say goodbye.
*If that’s what happened, then it was enough.*
The Blood Lord was dead. Dark Heaven’s army had crumbled. And I’d been given a few precious extra minutes.
Now I was smiling at faces I’d thought I’d never see again.
As if this were an ordinary, peaceful day, with no enemy to defeat and no one dear to me in need of protection.
Just like this moment.
Yeah.
I was ready to leave.
I had to be.

Nor when word came that countless followers had been wiped out.
Not for a single moment.
It was almost as if he’d wanted it to happen.
*Then did you want this lowly servant to die, too?*
The Blood Lord reached a trembling hand toward the sky.
Too far.
He couldn’t touch it.
Just like the distance between him and the Lord of Heaven.
No matter how hard he’d tried, they had never grown any closer.
*Ah.*
The Blood Lord swallowed a groan.
He had believed in and revered the Lord of Heaven.
But the light pouring down from that heaven had always shone on one person alone.
On the owner of those blazing eyes, who could no longer lift a finger yet still watched him die without looking away.
*Jin Taekyung.*
At that moment—
*Shhk!*
The fingers that had been reaching desperately through empty air curled like hooks and plunged downward.
The monster’s final strike carried anger and hatred he no longer knew whom to direct at, and one last duty that now seemed futile.
Just as it was about to pierce Jin Taekyung between the eyes—
*KRAK!*
A hand caked in dried blood blocked it.
The bones in the monster’s fingers shattered, joint by joint, and his flesh and blood burned.
*Hiss.*
A haze rose with the smell of scorching flesh.
Beyond it, the old master who had returned to his Disciple’s side parted his lips.
“How dare you lay a hand on him?”
Through heat that penetrated even his dulled senses, the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, looked down at the monster trembling in pain.
And he wasn’t alone.
The Bow Saint and the Slaughter Saint.
Sword Saint Mae Jonghak and Cheongpung.
Others, too, who had rushed over covered in blood.
They surrounded the monster like reapers, like iron towers.
They blotted out the sky that had been his whole world and became a broad, sturdy roof sheltering someone else from the rain.
That was why Jin Taekyung could laugh aloud.
He remembered the monster’s joyful cry just moments ago.
“See them?”
He spoke emphatically to the monster, its blood-red eyes wide open.
“Those faces you’re looking at?
That’s the paltry heaven I believed in.”
What could the monster say?
What more could he do?
He blinked helplessly, swallowed the blood spilling over his lips, and forced out a few last words.
“Rejoice... all you want.
This will be the last time.”
As his vision darkened to pitch-black, Jin Taekyung’s voice reached him, faint and distant.
“I was planning to.”
A bitter smile touched Jin Taekyung’s lips.
The monster breathed his last, and that breath dispersed into the air.
*Ding.*
A clear chime rang out like the bell of an ancient cathedral, announcing that everything was over.
It carried boundless joy—and even greater sorrow.
There’s a saying: animals leave their hides behind when they die, and people leave their names.
But a monster that’s neither animal nor human can leave behind a massive amount of EXP.
*Ding.
Ding.
Ding.*
The familiar clear chime rang nonstop in my ears.
If everyone could hear it instead of just me, I bet it would’ve carried for hundreds of ri.
*That bastard sure knew how to make an exit.*
The Blood Lord’s end was miserable and shabby, but the System’s payouts were lavish.
How many times had I leveled up in that brief instant?
Three?
More?
I wasn’t sure.
All I knew was that several Quests had been completed the moment the Blood Lord died, and I’d turned off notifications after my third Level Up.
*Any other time, I’d have passed out from happiness.*
No, I definitely would have.
Leveling up had become a once-in-a-blue-moon event.
Doing it several times in a row was nothing short of a miracle.
But none of it meant anything to me now.
The chimes that should have sounded like heaven were just irritating noise.
Even having my crushed flesh and broken bones heal offered only a little comfort.
One small, final comfort: I could pat someone’s trembling shoulder.
“Quit bawling.
Your dick’ll fall off.”
Cheongpung didn’t stop crying at my attempt to comfort him.
He just spoke through his sobs.
He said he was sorry.
And thanked me, too.
But my farewell to Cheongpung—surely our last—was brief.
Unlike him, I still had so many last faces left to see.
And once I’d seen them all, my own final moment would be waiting.
**System** Time Limit: 5 minutes 35 seconds
I gazed calmly at the hourglass of the final rally, still hanging in the air.
Truthfully, I’d already guessed.
Ever since I’d launched One Annihilation at the Blood Lord.
There was a limit to how much a Level Up could heal, and the injuries I’d suffered from One Annihilation’s backlash went beyond it.
Now that what was called innate qi—or original true qi—had been damaged, my fate was like a boat that had crossed a river with no way back.
*The System warned me, and I accepted it.*
That was all.
I’d taken the step I had to take, even knowing death might be waiting for me.
I had been prepared for this.
If anything, I was grateful for the way things had turned out.
Without the healing from those Level Ups, without the extra time it had given me in the final rally, I wouldn’t even have been able to say goodbye.
*If that’s what happened, then it was enough.*
The Blood Lord was dead.
Dark Heaven’s army had crumbled.
And I’d been given a few precious extra minutes.
Now I was smiling at faces I’d thought I’d never see again.
As if this were an ordinary, peaceful day, with no enemy to defeat and no one dear to me in need of protection.
Just like this moment.
Yeah.
I was ready to leave.
I had to be.

chapters.title: Chapter 1128
paragraphs: If I’d let myself think for just a little longer, I might have started crying without meaning to.
I knew better than anyone that I wasn’t ready to leave yet.
But the time I’d thought was endless was inching toward its end even now, and I forced the corners of my mouth upward.
For my sake.
And for the sake of those who would remain and remember my final moments for a long time.
“Oh, you’re here?”
Personally, I thought it was a very convincing performance.
A smiling face. A calm voice.
But the Fire Dragon Pavilion members, reunited with me at last, weren’t foolish enough to miss what my condition and the heavy air around us meant.
“...Pavilion Master.”
There was nothing more to say.
Sama Pyo stared at me blankly, then bit his lip. Song Ilseom quietly closed his eyes, and tears clouded Taishan’s eyes, each as big as a calf’s.
And Ju Hwaran—
*Squish. Squish.*
She staggered across a lake-like pool of blood and buried her trembling face against my shoulder.
That was all.
There were no more words, but it was enough for me.
*They’re all alive.*
My ominous hunches were never wrong, but this time was the exception.
Seeing them safe, I felt my stiff smile soften.
*Thank goodness. Really... thank goodness.*
The smile on my lips wasn’t an act anymore.
Gung Gibang and Cheongheoja appeared after the Fire Dragon Pavilion members.
Even the face of that wild-haired weirdo who gave me a headache every time I saw him made my heart swell with relief.
No—maybe it wasn’t Great Sir himself I was so glad to see, but the person on his back.
“Don’t worry. He suffered a serious internal injury, but the Seafaring King got the stagnant blood out in time. His life isn’t in danger.”
At the voice that suddenly reached my ears, I gave a small nod instead of answering.
Hyuk Mujin was unconscious and covered in blood from head to toe, but I could trust those words a hundred times over.
They came from none other than a man worthy of being called the greatest under heaven in this age.
“Swift Wind Sword Hyuk Mujin fought magnificently. He never gave an inch. He stood his ground with pride.”
Sword Saint Mae Jonghak added quietly, “Just like you.”
Hearing the sincerity in his voice, I parted my blood-crusted lips.
“Yes. I’m sure he did.”
I looked at Hyuk Mujin and smiled faintly.
“He’s my right arm, after all.”
Mae Jonghak had been watching me with a grave expression. Then he smiled along with me.
“So that’s how it is.”
“But he probably doesn’t know.”
“Why not?”
“I was always giving him a hard time. Told him he wasn’t nearly good enough to be my right arm.”
If there’d been even the slimmest chance I could recover, Mae Jonghak would have answered without hesitation.
*Tell him yourself later.*
*He’ll be happy to hear it.*
But like the Slaughter Saint and Bow Saint, who stood with their jaws clenched, he knew I didn’t have much time left.
“When he wakes, I’ll tell him exactly what you said. I won’t leave out a single word.”
“He’s so starved for praise that you can exaggerate all you like. For example...”
A conversation I’d had with Hyuk Mujin a long time ago came to mind, and I let out a quiet laugh.
“He has what it takes to become the Alliance Leader. Yeah. That’d make him faint with joy.”
“The next Alliance Leader, you say? I must reflect on this. My successor was right in front of me, and I failed to recognize him.”
“I’ll let it slide this time. You saved everyone, after all.”
“No. That’s not right.”
*Tap.*
Mae Jonghak placed a hand on my shoulder, his voice firm.
“It wasn’t me who saved everyone. It was you. And they saved themselves, too.”
“Look. Listen. See who they’re fighting for—and whose name they’re shouting.”
At that moment—
*Fwoooosh.*
Warm qi flowed from the fingers resting on my shoulder and seeped into me.
Like the sunset, it roused my fading consciousness. I saw the fanatics crumbling even now and heard our allies’ shouts sweeping over them like a wave.
A roar that swallowed the fierce wind, the rain, and even the eight-character maxim.
“Fight back! For the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon, Jin Taekyung!”
Banners soared so high they seemed to pierce the sky, whipping wildly in the wind.
A forest of glittering steel covered the city and advanced, raising red flowers as it went.
Murim warriors, government troops, and commoners.
Three forces that mixed about as well as water and oil had come together as one, driving through the invaders.
All of them shouting my name.
Their desperate will and resolve drowned out even the fanatics’ madness.
I trembled before I knew it.
A lightning-like shiver ran up my spine, and Mae Jonghak’s voice reached my ears.

“A month ago, when I went to persuade the Seafaring King, he told me that ships couldn’t sail on a stormy night. The sails and oars would break, and without a single glimmer of light, you wouldn’t even know which way was forward or back.”
The age of war had come at last.
The sun of peace that had shone over the land for more than fifty years had disappeared. Night had fallen with the dark clouds of Dark Heaven, deep and black as pitch.
Deep enough to shake even the two giants of the dark path, who had once fought the Hundred Thousand Demonic Disciples led by the Heavenly Demon.
“The Green Forest Battle King said much the same thing. Both of them feared Dark Heaven’s power, and spies planted in their ranks long ago had urged them to submit in order to survive.”
But what I saw now was the exact opposite.
*KRA-DRRRK!*
Two streaks of red and blue Force flashed so fiercely I could make them out even from here.
At the heart of those vast energies, cutting down fanatics without mercy, were two Supreme Peak masters who ruled the mountains and rivers of the land.
“Yes, I managed to persuade them in the end. And it was easier than I expected.”
“How?”
“It was just like the Great Faction War. All they needed was someone they could believe in and move forward beside. A single ray of light.”
I didn’t know that distant past.
And yet I could guess what light had shone through the darkness of the Great Faction War.
That was probably why my eyes widened without my meaning to.
The brilliant light that had illuminated that age of war had vanished long ago.
“...No way.”
I looked at Mae Jonghak, smiling faintly, and asked as if groaning.
“Has the Martial God returned?”
His answer sent something hot surging up from deep in my chest.
“No. But you were here.”

“One who goes ahead of everyone else to light the way. Someone who can bring everyone together because he isn’t bound by status or formality. That’s why you are the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon and Prince Shangshan—but before either of those, you’re a human being.”
His voice carried across the battlefield as though he were reciting a poem.
Countless feet trampled through the pools of blood left by the invaders, and dazzling spears and blades lit the darkness.
The darkness was fading. So was the flame inside me.
But the shouting didn’t stop.
Everyone in Xining was still calling my name at the top of their lungs.
As if mourning my death, just around the corner.
“Thank you. And I’m sorry. For coming too late. For failing to protect you.”
Mae Jonghak said much the same thing as Cheongpung had, crying just as he had. Then he had no choice but to turn away from me.
He was the Alliance Leader.
He had a duty to end this damn battle even a moment sooner and save as many lives as he could.
No.
Maybe he was also giving someone space.
Someone who stood a few steps behind me, frozen in body and spirit, watching it all in silence.
“What’s so amusing?”
His voice was so cold it seemed at odds with his title, the Fire King.
But I knew better than anyone that Jeok Cheongang’s anger was aimed at himself.
And I knew that smiling was the only thing I could do for him, when he must have been bleeding tears inside.
“What, I’m not even allowed to smile when I feel like it?”
“I can tell you’re forcing it.”
“...Is it that obvious?”
“Yeah. Look at the state you’re in.”
“I can’t see myself. Why don’t you bring me a mirror?”
“Do you need one? You’re covered in blood from head to toe, grinning like some evil spirit.”
“Like you’re in any position to talk.”
Jeok Cheongang and I fell silent.
Then, as if we’d planned it, we smiled at the same time.
We both knew it was the only way we could comfort each other, even a little.
Of course, we could see in each other’s eyes that neither smile was real.
“I can definitely tell you’re forcing that smile.”
“It isn’t easy.”
“No. It isn’t. Looking back, nothing ever was.”
I murmured weakly and looked at Jeok Cheongang.
The translucent hologram window stayed in the corner of my vision, no matter which way I turned my head.
**System Time Limit:** 59 seconds
“Old Master.”
“Speak.”
“Do you think there really is an afterlife?”
“There must be. No—there definitely is.”
“How do you know?”
“Hong Dao said so. The great Abbot of Shaolin Temple said it, so you’d better believe him without arguing.”
“Come on. You always write him off as some damn monk.”
“This time, I intend to believe him.”
“Why?”
“...There has to be an afterlife for us to meet again.”
**System Time Limit:** 30 seconds
“I don’t mind if it’s a long time before we meet. Come as late as you can.”
“It’ll take quite a while regardless. There are a lot of bastards I need to kill.”
“Now that you mention it, you’re right. That gives me an idea.”
“What is it?”
“Once you’ve killed those motherfuckers, I’ll be waiting in the afterlife to kill them again.”
“No.”
“What? Why not?”
“Just beat them until they’re about to die. Then we can kill them together one more time.”
“Wow. Are you a genius?”
“I suppose I was close to a natural disaster.”
**System Time Limit:** 15 seconds
“By the way, Old Master.”
“Hmm?”
“I think I’m getting sleepy.”
“...Yeah. You must be exhausted.”
“I’m sorry, but could I ask you for a favor?”
“I’ll grant it. Anything.”
“I have family. They aren’t here, so I don’t think I’ll get to see them now.”
**System Time Limit:** 10 seconds
“If you happen to meet them someday—though I know that probably won’t happen—could you tell them how I’m doing?”
“What must this old man do to reach the realm of immortals where you stayed?”
“I’m not sure. Ascend to immortality? I don’t really know.”
“Understood. I’ll find a way, whatever it takes. But you must grant this old man one favor in return.”
“Tell me.”
**System Time Limit:** 5 seconds
I blinked weakly.
Through my blurring vision, I could see Jeok Cheongang crying like a child.
“Please... can’t you stay alive?”
As darkness closed in, I answered.
“I’m sorry, Master.”
**System Time Limit:** 1 second
And then the entire world around me closed.

chapters.title: Chapter 1129
paragraphs: Looking back, I think I’d wondered about death since I was very young.
Not that I was particularly precocious.
I was just curious.
Why was the amusement park I’d been promised a trip to if I got a perfect score on my spelling test burning on TV?
Why was there a white bouquet on the desk of the classmate I’d played with just yesterday?
It didn’t take long for me to learn the truth.
Death, destruction, grief, and anger.
Hunters and monsters. Gates left all over the world. A war that still hadn’t ended.
That was simply the age we lived in.
An age of chaos, with truths too vast and terrible for anyone to hold back spilling out without end.
I soon understood why my parents had changed the TV channel with grim faces, and what the white bouquet on my friend’s desk meant.
But my kindergarten teacher’s description of my friend’s absence as a “long journey” left me with even more questions.
I understood that she’d been trying to be kind. Still, one thought led to another.
Why do people die?
Where do they go when they die?
If they really do go on a journey, is there a world beyond death?
Even after many years, no one could answer those questions for me.
Of course they couldn’t.
The departed don’t speak.
So I wanted to find the answer from someone who had died, but wasn’t dead anymore.
“Hey, Golgoli.”
“A mere human like you dares call me by such a vulgar name? Can’t you see this radiant crown?”
“Want me to make it so you can’t see anything at all?”
“...Why did you call me? Get to the point.”
Deep down, I’d believed Bones—or rather, the Skeleton King—could answer the question I’d carried for so long.
But faith has a way of being betrayed.
“The afterlife? I don’t know why you’re asking me.”
“Does that mean—”
“That’s right. I don’t know a thing. I can’t remember my life before I died, so why would I know any more about what came after? I just woke up in the dark and found myself like this.”
It was ironic.
Even an undead being who had already crossed death’s threshold and been reborn didn’t know what lay beyond it.
In the end, I gave up looking for an answer.
Or rather, I put it off.
I’d find out someday.
Whether I wanted to or not, death would wait in the shadows for its moment, then swallow everything whole.
Just like now.
*Ssshhh.*
Everything blurred and drifted away.
The sky that had only just begun to clear. The faces looking down at me.
Their cries, and the shouts still rising from the battlefield.
The past I’d struggled through. The fleeting moments I’d let slip away.
All of it.
*Ah.*
With no voice left to escape my lips, I sank weakly.
Into pitch-black darkness.
Into the swamp of death, tugging hard at my soul.
And in a gap in time that felt like eternity, I heard a voice echo as if in a hallucination.
“Open your eyes.”
At that moment—
*Whoosh!*
A beam of light appeared from nowhere, somehow, tearing through the darkness and illuminating the world.
A new world, where everything had changed.
I blinked blankly.
Then I took in the sight before me and wondered:
*Where am I?*
The gray-white space stretched on without end. Even “vast” felt too small a word for it.
The horizon far in the distance was hazy. When I looked up, I saw a ceiling that seemed higher and more distant than the sky.
It felt as though I’d been shut inside a gigantic box.
Strangely, though, I wasn’t afraid.
For all its emptiness, the infinite space inspired an awe I couldn’t explain just by looking at it.
Yes.
The answer to the question I’d carried for so long was here.
Though it looked nothing like I’d imagined.
“Hmm. I suppose so.”
A voice came from behind me without any hint of someone’s presence. I instinctively twisted away and retreated, fixing my gaze on the uninvited guest standing only a few steps away.
“...You’re—”
I had no time to marvel at the fact that I could speak.
The unexpected visitor—an old man—was far more shocking.
He, on the other hand, sounded perfectly calm.
“Do you know who I am?”
I nodded and tried to answer evenly.
“The Grim Reaper?”
“Uh, no?”
After a brief silence, the old man shook his head.
“Think whatever you like. It isn’t important.”
“It’s pretty important to me.”
“Why? Worried you’ll be dragged to hell?”
“Honestly, yes.”
“You must have sinned a lot.”
“...Who knows?”
I gave the old man, whoever he was, a bitter smile.
I’d sometimes wondered whether every enemy I’d defeated had really deserved to die like that.
Whether the mountain of corpses and river of blood I’d made with my own hands could be weighed against all the lives saved because of me.
*Maybe I deserve to go to hell more than anyone.*
That was when he spoke.
“You’re worrying over nothing. It’s not so easy to end up in hell.”
The old man’s sunken gaze settled on me.
As if he could see right through my thoughts.
“And the people you miss won’t be there, either.”
“Isn’t that what worries you most? That you might die and still never see them again?”
For a moment, I couldn’t speak. I stared at him, frozen like a statue, then barely managed to force out the words.
“Wait. Is this, by any chance—”
“Ah, forgive me. I didn’t mean to let that slip.”
His answer all but confirmed my guess.
As I struggled to find the words, the old man shrugged.
“Well, there it is.”
“I knew something was off. So it really was true.”
“It happens more often than you’d think. When the thing you thought couldn’t happen does. It’s easier if you think of it as just one of those cases.”
There was nothing simple or comforting about that. Yet, for some reason, I found it surprisingly easy to accept.
Even who owned that voice, the one that had sounded like a hallucination just before I opened my eyes in this strange place.
“You’re quick on the uptake. Good.”
I took another look at the old man, who now read my thoughts as naturally as breathing.
A robe without a speck of dust on it. A beard long enough to reach the floor.
And something about him that felt oddly familiar.
“Have we... met before?”
The old man seemed to ponder the question for a while before answering.
“We may have. Or we may not.”
“Excuse me?”
“That’s the best answer I can give. I have my own circumstances to consider. I’ve already gone quite far out of my way to help you.”
“You helped me? How?”
“Find the answer to that question yourself. You don’t have as much time as you think, so... let’s get started.”
I wanted to ask what on earth he was talking about, and what he meant by *begin*.
But the instant his figure blurred, every tangled thought in my head vanished.
*Pop.*
I hadn’t seen him move. I hadn’t even sensed it.
He was so fast he left no afterimage.
By the time I turned, he had crossed the few steps between us and taken position behind me. His fist blotted out my vision.
*Thud!*
My vision swam, and strength left my legs.
I’d never seen an attack so fast and precise.
I had no reason to fight anymore. Even so, I forced my buckling legs to hold and reached out on instinct.
*Whoosh—BOOM!*
Indigo flames engulfed the gray-white space.
Before I could even think about why I had internal energy here, the old man’s calm voice rang out from beyond the scorching heat.
“The Flame Divine Palm. An excellent martial art.”
“...How do you know that?”
“Didn’t I tell you? Keep it simple and accept it.”
*Whoosh.*
The flames parted as he answered.
Without even forming Palm Force, the old man waved a hand and blew away the heat of the Flame Divine Palm as if snuffing out a candle. Then he signaled to me with his eyes.
“Go on. Struggle all you like. Try the Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist—or better yet, the Blazing Flame Divine Spear.”
“Ah, but not One Annihilation. For your sake, not mine.”
Was this what it felt like to be haunted by a ghost?
I could only stare at the ghost—or rather, the old man—in a daze, unable to speak.
Of course, he didn’t even allow me that moment.
*Slash!*
When had he moved? How?
He’d been standing amid the dying flames, but now he was in my blind spot. Invisible qi carried on the edge of his hand swept smoothly across my chest.
So sharp that a beat later, the flesh it sliced through—like tofu—let out a scream.
*Splurt!*
Blood sprayed into the air. At the same time, a distant pain I’d thought I’d never feel again came surging back.
So did the fear I’d briefly forgotten.
*At this rate... I’ll die.*
It was bizarre.
I’d already died once, yet here I was thinking about dying again.
But I had no time to question it.
Against a power that seemed capable of erasing not just my body but my soul, I had to struggle with everything I had.
“Good. That’s right. Looks like you’re finally starting to understand the situation.”
The old man nodded, seeing straight through my thoughts. A curse escaped before I could stop it.
“You crazy old bastard.”
“High praise. Thank you.”
“What... the hell are you?”
“Who knows? I might be your grandfather.”
The old man smiled faintly for the first time. While I stood speechless at the unexpected family insult, he reached toward me.
No—he held something out.
A spear that had suddenly appeared in midair.
“Take it. Even if you’re going to die, you should at least get to fight back properly once, shouldn’t you?”
I gritted my teeth.
Then I caught the shaft as the spear flew slowly toward me and spat out the words.
“You’re dead.”
The old man replied, “May you be reborn in paradise.”
At that moment—
*Shhhk!*
A dazzling flash of light streaked across the vast gray-white space.

chapters.title: Chapter 1130
paragraphs: Light doesn’t exist only to illuminate.
Sometimes it erases everything and lets you forget.
Just like the beam flying toward Jin Taekyung now, filling his vision with white.
Whoooooosh!
As the flash swelled, Jin Taekyung’s gaze sank low.
He cleared every stray thought and question from his mind.
No—he had no choice.
The beam had split into dozens, and each one writhed as if alive, aiming for a vital point on his body.
*It’s no feint.*
Every one of those solid beams held terrifying destructive power unlike anything he’d ever experienced.
But Jin Taekyung chose to advance, not retreat.
Fwoosh—BOOM!
Flames streamed from the foot he drove forward. Keeping low, he shot through the rain of light, narrowly slipping past each beam. The old man watched him and nodded.
“The Flamefire Path. You certainly know how to fight.”
Jin Taekyung answered the praise in his own way.
Ssshh.
As the distance between them vanished, his spear surged toward the old man. Afterimages engulfed it, rippling like a wave.
Like the tail of a colossal dragon.
Whoooosh!
Indigo flames rose along the spearhead. As with the old man’s move moments earlier, they split into dozens in an instant and surged forward, blanketing the space.
KWA-BOOM!
If a hell of boiling sulfurous fire existed, would it look like this?
Yet even before that lava-like heat, the old man’s calm eyes did not waver.
Nor did his hands as he brought them together to meet the spearhead amid that life-or-death crisis.
Crack!
For an instant, Jin Taekyung’s eyes flew wide.
The trembling spearhead was reflected in Jin Taekyung’s eyes between the old man’s palms, pressed together as if in prayer.
The question escaped before he knew it.
The old man, who had blown away every flame coming at him simply by bringing his palms together, looked puzzled.
“Hm? I just grabbed it.”
“Anyway, try something hotter this time. This is making me pleasantly drowsy. Not bad.”
Jin Taekyung felt his vision swim.

The old man was already a madman for stopping his full-power strike with Empty-Hand Seizes the Blade. And now he was treating several jiazi of Scorching Yang Qi—hot enough to melt steel—as if it were hot spring water.
*What kind of old man is this?*
Even the Blood Lord, the strongest opponent he’d faced until now, hadn’t been this powerful.
Not even close.
The Blood Lord had used blood to gain healing that bordered on Regeneration and a seemingly endless supply of internal energy. But even that terrifying power had its limits.
The old man was different. His very nature, his level, was different from the Blood Lord’s.
Jin Taekyung sensed no particular killing intent in eyes as still as a secluded lake. Yet merely facing the old man made his whole body freeze.
It was like standing before an enormous wall he could never climb, no matter how hard he struggled.
And the old man saw straight into that passing thought.
“Your head’s full of stray thoughts. You must still have some life left in you. In that case...”
At that moment—
CRASH!
The spearhead in the old man’s grasp shattered. His palm glided forward and touched Jin Taekyung’s chest.
BOOM!
An explosion rang out from deep within his body.
Jin Taekyung dropped to one knee as pain bleached his vision white. Even through the ringing in his ears, the old man’s whisper came through with startling clarity.
“I’ll clear those stray thoughts away for you again.”
Jin Taekyung had no time to answer, let alone recover from the pain.
More precisely, the old man didn’t give him any.
Whoosh!
A massive force descended toward the crown of his head with a heavy rush of air.
The energy wave was so terrifying it made him forget even the pain. Jin Taekyung rolled to the side without time to think.
KWA-BOOM!
A roar like the sky splitting apart shook the space, followed by a shock wave that swept in every direction.
Jin Taekyung felt himself thrown far away, as if weightless. Behind him, the old man appeared, having crossed more than ten jang in an instant.
“Good judgment. If you hadn’t used Narye tagon, it would’ve ended there.”
Normally, Jin Taekyung would have told an enemy to shut the hell up, no matter who it was.
Not this time.
Every part of him knew that against this old man, even a single deep breath—or the smallest stray thought—was a luxury he couldn’t afford.
“You only just figured out something that simple?”
...and that as long as this mysterious old man could read his mind, he would never escape this damned situation.
“Oh, that’s quite an insight. So what will you do now?”
Meeting the old man’s interested gaze, Jin Taekyung used what remained of his spear as a cane and pushed himself upright.
Slowly. Carefully.
By the time he stood on both feet, he had found his answer.
Ssshh.
His eyes closed.
The thought that he was doing something insane, and the fear of what might happen, lasted only a moment. His trembling eyelids grew still, shutting out everything his eyes had shown him.
By giving up that one thing, Jin Taekyung gained something new.
The thread of enlightenment he hadn’t managed to follow to its end during the fierce battle against Dark Heaven.
And the only way through the situation he faced now.
At the sight of him, the old man smiled faintly once more.
“Yes. That’s how it should be.”
At that moment—
Pop.
As if on cue, the young man and the old man shot toward each other.
Fwoosh—BOOM!
Jin Taekyung thrust out the Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist as if entranced.
Heat that seemed capable of melting even a thousand-year-old boulder swept through the gray-white space. But he already knew.
He could feel it.
The old man was no longer there.
He was moving faster than sound, slipping into Jin Taekyung’s blind spot.
BOOM!
Jin Taekyung twisted like lightning. A powerful palm strike slammed through the air where his head had been a moment earlier.
“Much better.”
In the darkness behind his closed eyes, Jin Taekyung swallowed a breath as he barely evaded the attacks closing in from every direction.
Was it his imagination?
The old man’s voice, once clearer than anything else, now sounded fainter and farther away than an echo.
“The fact that you can still hear me means you’re not there yet.”
He was right. Maybe.
It was nothing new. It had always been this way.
He hadn’t been strong enough to protect everyone. The guilt and anxiety had brought nightmares night after night.
He had wavered like a candle in the wind, then guttered out.
“But that is greed. Humans cannot become perfect.”
Jin Taekyung knew that, too.
But even if what he wanted went beyond desire into greed, he didn’t care.
He only wanted to save someone, and to live himself.
To live alongside the people he cherished in a more peaceful world.
“Everyone dreams of that. Reality is cruel, though.”
Despite his calm voice, the old man pressed him without pause.
A foot that snapped like a whip, a hand slicing diagonally downward, a palm extending smoothly—each was a sword or spear.
There was no fierce killing intent in any of those moves, yet each brimmed with enough qi to seemingly obliterate not just his body, but his soul.
“Who knows? Perhaps entering perfect rest just like this would be a good thing for you.”
At those words, Jin Taekyung’s retreating steps stopped as though nailed to the ground.
KWA-BOOM!
Two fists collided in midair.
The old man was so wrinkled that Jin Taekyung couldn’t begin to guess his age, and his fist held a force almost impossible to withstand. Jin Taekyung braced himself, though his feet slowly slid back.
“What do you mean by that?”
The question came through clenched teeth. The old man answered calmly.
“What do you think I mean?”
“...You can’t mean—”
“Good. You seem to know already. There’s no time left, so let’s settle this now.”
Just as Jin Taekyung was about to ask what he meant, the old man’s fist gathered more force and shoved him away.
KWA-BOOM!
Jin Taekyung shot backward like a cannonball.
He barely regained his balance in midair. The moment he landed, he felt the space around him hum.
Hmmm.
He couldn’t see it. But he could picture it.
Far away, a formless sword pointed straight at him. The old man held it in his hands—a sword made not of metal, but entirely of qi.
“Try to dodge it. If you can’t... then this is as far as you go.”
Jin Taekyung could no longer ask what that meant.

He couldn’t even bring himself to open his eyes. If he lost his tenuous hold on this new sensation for even an instant, or let the slightest stray thought intrude, he felt certain his body would be cut to pieces.
And that judgment was right.
Gooooong.
The gray-white space trembled as the old man slowly raised both hands.
At the same time, a faint beam of light flowed into some corner of Jin Taekyung’s pitch-black vision.
*What is this?*
A sensation he had never felt before.
Or rather, it had come to him only very rarely after he combined three forms of internal energy, lingering briefly before fading.
Reason had no place in it. It belonged to instinct.
It was a realm where the body moved before the mind gave an order—no, somewhere beyond even that.
It was taking hold of Jin Taekyung’s mind, touching on the sixth sense.
At last, he stared straight at the invisible sword slashing down from the old man’s fingertips.
Sssshing!
At the instant a sound like the whole world splitting apart rang out—
Whoooosh.
Jin Taekyung saw it.
A single beam of light, brightening his vision as dark as the deep night.
And, as if entranced, he stepped forward.
Shhk!

“Anyway, try something hotter this time.
This is making me pleasantly drowsy.
Not bad.”
Jin Taekyung felt his vision swim.
The old man was already a madman for stopping his full-power strike with Empty-Hand Seizes the Blade.
And now he was treating several jiazi of Scorching Yang Qi—hot enough to melt steel—as if it were hot spring water.
*What kind of old man is this?*
Even the Blood Lord, the strongest opponent he’d faced until now, hadn’t been this powerful.
Not even close.
The Blood Lord had used blood to gain healing that bordered on Regeneration and a seemingly endless supply of internal energy.
But even that terrifying power had its limits.
The old man was different.
His very nature, his level, was different from the Blood Lord’s.
Jin Taekyung sensed no particular killing intent in eyes as still as a secluded lake.
Yet merely facing the old man made his whole body freeze.
It was like standing before an enormous wall he could never climb, no matter how hard he struggled.
And the old man saw straight into that passing thought.
“Your head’s full of stray thoughts.
You must still have some life left in you.
In that case...”
At that moment—
CRASH!
The spearhead in the old man’s grasp shattered.
His palm glided forward and touched Jin Taekyung’s chest.
BOOM!
An explosion rang out from deep within his body.
Jin Taekyung dropped to one knee as pain bleached his vision white.
Even through the ringing in his ears, the old man’s whisper came through with startling clarity.
“I’ll clear those stray thoughts away for you again.”
Jin Taekyung had no time to answer, let alone recover from the pain.
More precisely, the old man didn’t give him any.
Whoosh!
A massive force descended toward the crown of his head with a heavy rush of air.
The energy wave was so terrifying it made him forget even the pain.
Jin Taekyung rolled to the side without time to think.
KWA-BOOM!
A roar like the sky splitting apart shook the space, followed by a shock wave that swept in every direction.
Jin Taekyung felt himself thrown far away, as if weightless.
Behind him, the old man appeared, having crossed more than ten jang in an instant.
“Good judgment.
If you hadn’t used Narye tagon, it would’ve ended there.”
Normally, Jin Taekyung would have told an enemy to shut the hell up, no matter who it was.
Not this time.
Every part of him knew that against this old man, even a single deep breath—or the smallest stray thought—was a luxury he couldn’t afford.
“You only just figured out something that simple?”
...and that as long as this mysterious old man could read his mind, he would never escape this damned situation.
“Oh, that’s quite an insight.
So what will you do now?”
Meeting the old man’s interested gaze, Jin Taekyung used what remained of his spear as a cane and pushed himself upright.
Slowly.
Carefully.
By the time he stood on both feet, he had found his answer.
Ssshh.
His eyes closed.
The thought that he was doing something insane, and the fear of what might happen, lasted only a moment.
His trembling eyelids grew still, shutting out everything his eyes had shown him.
By giving up that one thing, Jin Taekyung gained something new.
The thread of enlightenment he hadn’t managed to follow to its end during the fierce battle against Dark Heaven.
And the only way through the situation he faced now.
At the sight of him, the old man smiled faintly once more.
“Yes.
That’s how it should be.”
At that moment—
Pop.
As if on cue, the young man and the old man shot toward each other.
Fwoosh—BOOM!
Jin Taekyung thrust out the Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist as if entranced.
Heat that seemed capable of melting even a thousand-year-old boulder swept through the gray-white space.
But he already knew.
He could feel it.
The old man was no longer there.
He was moving faster than sound, slipping into Jin Taekyung’s blind spot.
BOOM!
Jin Taekyung twisted like lightning.
A powerful palm strike slammed through the air where his head had been a moment earlier.
“Much better.”
In the darkness behind his closed eyes, Jin Taekyung swallowed a breath as he barely evaded the attacks closing in from every direction.
Was it his imagination?
The old man’s voice, once clearer than anything else, now sounded fainter and farther away than an echo.
“The fact that you can still hear me means you’re not there yet.”
He was right.
Maybe.
It was nothing new.
It had always been this way.
He hadn’t been strong enough to protect everyone.
The guilt and anxiety had brought nightmares night after night.
He had wavered like a candle in the wind, then guttered out.
“But that is greed.
Humans cannot become perfect.”
Jin Taekyung knew that, too.
But even if what he wanted went beyond desire into greed, he didn’t care.
He only wanted to save someone, and to live himself.
To live alongside the people he cherished in a more peaceful world.
“Everyone dreams of that.
Reality is cruel, though.”
Despite his calm voice, the old man pressed him without pause.
A foot that snapped like a whip, a hand slicing diagonally downward, a palm extending smoothly—each was a sword or spear.
There was no fierce killing intent in any of those moves, yet each brimmed with enough qi to seemingly obliterate not just his body, but his soul.
“Who knows?
Perhaps entering perfect rest just like this would be a good thing for you.”
At those words, Jin Taekyung’s retreating steps stopped as though nailed to the ground.
KWA-BOOM!
Two fists collided in midair.
The old man was so wrinkled that Jin Taekyung couldn’t begin to guess his age, and his fist held a force almost impossible to withstand.
Jin Taekyung braced himself, though his feet slowly slid back.
“What do you mean by that?”
The question came through clenched teeth.
The old man answered calmly.
“What do you think I mean?”
“...You can’t mean—”
“Good.
You seem to know already.
There’s no time left, so let’s settle this now.”
Just as Jin Taekyung was about to ask what he meant, the old man’s fist gathered more force and shoved him away.
KWA-BOOM!
Jin Taekyung shot backward like a cannonball.
He barely regained his balance in midair.
The moment he landed, he felt the space around him hum.
Hmmm.
He couldn’t see it.
But he could picture it.
Far away, a formless sword pointed straight at him.
The old man held it in his hands—a sword made not of metal, but entirely of qi.
“Try to dodge it.
If you can’t... then this is as far as you go.”
Jin Taekyung could no longer ask what that meant.
He couldn’t even bring himself to open his eyes.
If he lost his tenuous hold on this new sensation for even an instant, or let the slightest stray thought intrude, he felt certain his body would be cut to pieces.
And that judgment was right.
Gooooong.
The gray-white space trembled as the old man slowly raised both hands.
At the same time, a faint beam of light flowed into some corner of Jin Taekyung’s pitch-black vision.
*What is this?*
A sensation he had never felt before.
Or rather, it had come to him only very rarely after he combined three forms of internal energy, lingering briefly before fading.
Reason had no place in it.
It belonged to instinct.
It was a realm where the body moved before the mind gave an order—no, somewhere beyond even that.
It was taking hold of Jin Taekyung’s mind, touching on the sixth sense.
At last, he stared straight at the invisible sword slashing down from the old man’s fingertips.
Sssshing!
At the instant a sound like the whole world splitting apart rang out—
Whoooosh.
Jin Taekyung saw it.
A single beam of light, brightening his vision as dark as the deep night.
And, as if entranced, he stepped forward.
Shhk!

paragraphs: In time brought to a standstill, amid a silence that seemed to last forever, I slowly opened my eyes.
It was a strange feeling.
My mind was hazy, as though lost in thick fog, yet I could see more clearly than ever. Clearly enough to wonder if all of this was a dream.
But the low voice that reached my ears a moment later reminded me that this was no illusion.
“Did you see it?”
I looked up at the old man, dazed.
Then, recalling the formless qi that had flown across the space moments ago, cleaving it in two and missing me by no more than a thread, I parted my lips.
“Yes. I saw it.”
Everything felt natural. The respect that had crept into my voice, and the way the old man accepted it as if it were only right.
“What did you see?”
“A ray of light. A line.”
The old man stroked his snow-white beard, which hung down to his knees.
“How could that be? It must have been formless.”
“It had a form. For that moment, at least.”
“Even with your eyes closed?”
“I didn’t see it with my eyes.”
“You saw it, but didn’t see it. Then what was it?”
“That...”
I faltered.
Not because I didn’t know the answer, but because the thought that had flashed through my mind sounded absurd even to me.
My silence was as good as an answer, though. The old man’s unfathomable gaze was already looking into my heart.
“People often have the truth right before their eyes and still pass it by because they cannot believe it. What a pity.”
Step.
One step was all it took for the old man to close the distance between us. He whispered:
“You saw what cannot be seen, and dodged what could not be dodged. Why can’t you believe you did it?”
“Sit cross-legged.”
Still hazy as though in a dream, I sat as he instructed, almost without knowing what I was doing.
Then I heard his voice again—not in my ears, but inside my head.
—Clear your mind like a stream. Hold your focus and let yourself follow the flow.
A thought came to me. I’d heard something like this before, somewhere.
But it was gone in an instant as my awareness sank deeper.
Fwoooosh.
Light and darkness flickered without end before my eyes, leaving me disoriented.
Amid that overwhelming confusion, I forgot everything.
Where I was. Who I was.
Yet the voice coming from somewhere remained astonishingly clear.
—Remember what you saw. How it felt in that moment.
I took a slow, deep breath.
Then I spoke the name of the thing with no shape, color, or scent in my mind.
*Qi.*
Everywhere and nowhere.
The source and seed of all things in the world.
Yes.
For a brief moment, I had seen it clearly—through a new realm beyond the senses.
And the owner of the voice echoing deep within my soul was someone who had already set foot in that realm.
—I’ll ask again. What did you see it with?
Right. I still hadn’t answered the old man’s question.
This time, though, I could answer without hesitation. That other eye hidden within me—the one even I hadn’t believed in—
*My heart. No...*
The Mind’s Eye.
The moment those two words came to me and were branded into my mind—
—Good judgment, as always.
Flash!
At the sound of the old man’s low voice, the light and darkness that had kept flickering before my eyes scattered.
Or rather, everything around me did.
“Ah.”
I let out the breath I’d been holding and looked around.
Crack. Crack.
Why was this happening? How was it possible?
The vast, endless gray-white space was shaking.
Cracks spread in every direction like a pane of glass about to shatter, and the figure of the man standing beyond it twisted along with the shifting space.
“Don’t be alarmed. The time we were granted is simply coming to an end.”
His voice was calm, at odds with the impossible sight before me. I stared at him as though entranced.
Then, recalling a fragment of a memory I’d long forgotten, I finally spoke.
“I’ve met you before. I’m sure of it.”
The old man smiled faintly.
“Is that what you think?”
Neither a yes nor a no.
But now I was certain. The gray-white space and the old man might look different from how they had then, but neither had changed at the heart of it.
I knew whose voice had come to me now and then like an auditory hallucination ever since my Bone Transformation.
“You’re...”
I could barely force the word out as I looked at the old man smiling silently before me.
No.
*The Helper.*
The one who had first taught me to circulate my qi when I’d only just stepped into the unknown world of Murim.
The mysterious being I’d taken for part of the tutorial System, and forgotten for so long because of it.
“...Who on earth are you?”
Was this what it felt like to have lightning strike the top of your head?
Faced at last with a truth this immense, I trembled as the shock washed over me like a tidal wave.
At the same time, I knew it instinctively. The old man would never answer, and even this brief meeting was drawing to a close.
“No need to answer. I already know.”
Grgrgrk.
The space contorted. I could no longer make out the old man’s face, but I shouted toward him.
“Then what—what happens now?”
“Who knows? I don’t know what lies ahead, either. For now, we have no choice but to return to our respective places.”
“What does that—”
“Jin Taekyung.”
His voice was low. Cutting me off, he spoke.
“Do your best. Only then can you save everyone—and yourself.”
“Now it’s time to go. To the place where you belong.”
My eyes widened as I understood what he meant.
Whoooosh.
The world in my sight rushed past as I was drawn away. Something glimmering touched my hand, and the old man’s final words rang through my head like a voice I was only imagining.
—Take it. This is the last gift this old man can give you.
I instinctively clenched my hand around it.
As my consciousness faded, I heard a sound from somewhere. A clear bell chime I’d been certain I would never hear again.
Ding.
A brilliant light came rushing from far away and filled my vision.
Left alone, the old man gazed in silence at the empty place for a long while.
To the person who had just vanished, it must have looked as though the entire gray-white space was disappearing. But the old man knew better.
This space would last forever. Jin Taekyung had only been a guest passing through.
And the old man would once again have to wait, with no telling when that wait might end.
“When will I be able to finish this?”
He murmured to himself. After so long alone, talking to himself had become a habit.
“No. Will it ever end at all?”
A bitter smile touched his wrinkled lips as he looked around.
Gray-white space stretched endlessly in every direction. Cold and pale, it was his only home—and a vast prison with neither bars nor an exit.
The emptiness that thought brought lasted only a moment. His gaze soon grew calm again.
After all, no one had forced him to become a prisoner here. He had chosen it himself.
“Yes. So that’s enough.”
He murmured the words as though renewing a promise to himself, then started walking.
Then, suddenly, he stopped and turned to look back along the way he’d come.
Or, more precisely, at the place where the guest who had visited after so long had stayed.
“Jin Taekyung.”
The name left his lips, and he wondered if Taekyung could do it. If the choice he had made had truly been the right one.
And if he’d made the wrong choice, how terrible and cruel would the future ahead be?
But all those worries were meaningless.
The old man had already made his choice, and thanks to his help, Jin Taekyung had been given another chance.
“I suppose I’ll have to put my faith in you.”
The words would never reach Taekyung. The old man began walking again, slowly crossing the endless gray-white space as he always had.
The Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, was crying.
He held his Disciple’s lifeless body and sobbed quietly. Nothing around him mattered anymore—not the shouts and clash of steel that still rang out, nor the people watching him.
The Master who had lost his only Disciple did not hold back his tears.
He couldn’t.
Two years.
Only two years out of a life that had lasted more than a hundred. Yet his time with Jin Taekyung had shone brighter than any other.
Taekyung had been the only light to find him when he was at his darkest.
And now Jin Taekyung—his Disciple—was dead.
Despite his Master’s plea for him to live, he had gone somewhere far away.
*I’m sorry, Master.*
That final voice wouldn’t leave his ears.
The corners of Taekyung’s mouth, raised with effort into a smile for his grieving Master. His half-closed, empty eyes. Even now, the sight seared into Jeok Cheongang’s heart like a brand.
Grief overwhelmed him until he could make sense of nothing. Tears kept filling his eyes, hiding what he needed to see.
Plip.
A tear rolled down the Master’s cheek and fell onto the back of his dead Disciple’s hand.
Sss.
The surface of the blood rippled with a sudden tremor, and the finger submerged in it moved.
