chapters.title: Chapter 1132
paragraphs: No one there had dared to imagine it.
That the body of someone already dead would move.
Perhaps that was why even the few who saw his fingers twitch failed to realize what it meant.
They put it down to the grieving Master’s touch as he held his Disciple’s body and sobbed, the lingering vibrations of the battlefield—or simply their imagination.
An illusion born of the desperate wish that the young hero who had met such a noble end might come back to life, even now.
The Master, sunk in grief, thought no differently.
Thump.
At first, he thought he’d imagined the sound.
But when a vibration traveled through the Disciple he held so tightly, Jeok Cheongang could only blink in a daze.
*How?*
It couldn’t be. It was impossible.
Yet contrary to what Jeok Cheongang’s instincts told him, the vibration, once begun, did not stop.
It grew louder and clearer.
Like a war drum beating out the order to charge.
Thump. Thump-thump.
In an instant, Jeok Cheongang hurriedly pressed his ear to his Disciple’s chest. His eyes flew wide.
There was no mistaking it. He wasn’t hearing things.
The heart that had stopped was beating again. An extinguished ember had caught fire once more.
And just as Jeok Cheongang shuddered at the impossible truth—
Fwoosh!
A scorching wind surged up around one person’s body.
No—
A tremendous wave of qi, powerful enough to envelop a radius of a dozen or so *jang*.
Rrrrmmm.
The space trembled in tiny shivers, like a living creature.
Everyone still nearby stared, eyes wide.
They watched dark blue heat waver like a mirage around the young man slowly rising at its center.
An exclamation thick with emotion escaped Jeok Cheongang’s lips.
Most people were simply overwhelmed by the mysterious sight. But he knew all too well what it meant.
So did the two other giants who had remained to witness it, unlike Sword Saint Mae Jonghak, who had gone to bring the long battle to an end.
“...Am I seeing this right?”
The Slaughter Saint sounded unable to believe it. The Bow Saint answered in a voice that trembled, unlike her usual one.
“I think so. No, I’m sure of it.”
Watching the young man rise out of his Master’s arms, she murmured as if to herself.
“Bone Transformation.”
At that moment—
Ssshh!
The heat that had surged like waves and the dark blue streaks of light gathered with sudden force.
Toward the body, still warm.
To rekindle the faint ember within.
People had feared fire since ancient times.
A campfire burning in the mountains at night could give them strength, but greater heat could bring disaster.
So they saw fire as a force of destruction, overlooking the power to purify hidden behind it.
And now, the heat surrounding one person’s body was unquestionably a purifying flame.
Flicker.
Though trapped in a state of consciousness where he couldn’t tell dream from reality, Jin Taekyung could feel it clearly.
The heat surging from deep within him.
The agony of his whole body burning, and at the same time, the cool relief of his wounds being washed clean.
Kwoooosh!
A wave of fire overflowed in every direction. The terrible heat seemed ready to melt even his already-healed body in an instant.
Yet for some reason, Jin Taekyung felt not a trace of fear.
Of course he didn’t.
He understood it instinctively.
That immense heat wasn’t only sweeping through his body, melting every limb and bone. It was also peeling back a layer to reveal the unknown power hidden within him.
But that wasn’t the only reason Jin Taekyung could calmly accept his transformation.
Ding. Ding. Ding.
Beyond his hazy sight and senses, chimes rang out one after another.
They were clearer than ever—the chimes he’d thought he would never hear again. Words swept past his eyes like the wind, tickling his retinas.
New enlightenment and achievements tied to it. Increases in Qi Sense and martial arts...
Unable to bear the weight of the words pouring down without end, Jin Taekyung closed his eyes.
He focused entirely on the landscape of his mind and sank deep beneath the surface.
The next moment, he found himself standing somewhere new.
*Where is this?*
He had seen it only once, yet it was familiar.
How could he forget?
Far below lay endless land and sea. Clouds filled the sky as far as he could see. It was a beautiful sight.
*The peak. It’s the same peak as before.*
When he had brought together the Heavenly Power Demon’s demonic qi, the Thunderbolt Saber King’s lightning qi, and his own Scorching Yang Qi, Jin Taekyung had finally conquered this lofty peak.
He had stepped into a new realm: the Summit of Martial Achievement.
*But that was all.*
He had claimed the peak that touched the clouds, but no matter how far he reached, he couldn’t touch the sky beyond them.
That realm hadn’t been open to him then.
He hadn’t yet earned the right—the enlightenment—to glimpse it, even for a moment.
Yes. That was how it *had* been.
Until today, when the old man had given him another insight.
*Climbing higher was never the only answer.*
He had simply taken that answer for granted.
But now he knew.
Raising the peak beneath his feet wasn’t the only way to glimpse the sky beyond these thick clouds.
*There’s more than one answer.*
Why hadn’t he realized it?
He had always gone beyond anything he’d imagined possible. So why had he set limits on his thinking?
Jin Taekyung suddenly remembered a conversation he’d forgotten.
When he was a novice martial artist, still stuck at Second Rate, he had asked Jin Wikyung how on earth he could reach the First Rate realm. His brother had answered with a single word: *faith.*
“What does that... mean?”
“Exactly what it sounds like. Believe in yourself.”
“What does believing have to do with advancing realms?”
“Martial arts begin with belief.”
Only then had he understood.
Now he understood.
The person who had believed in Jin Taekyung least wasn’t anyone else. It was Jin Taekyung himself.
Even after he’d far surpassed Jin Wikyung’s martial prowess, even after he’d earned the right—he had always been that way.
*But not anymore.*
He decided to try believing, just a little.
In the old man’s words: Don’t set limits for yourself.
In the potential he had yet to discover.
*If I want to see it, I can.*
At the very top of the peak, Jin Taekyung lifted his head as if spellbound.
He looked at the clouds streaming across his path, blocking the view in his mind.
Not with his eyes, but with his heart.
With the Mind’s Eye.
And the next moment—
Fwoosh!
The clouds scattered as if by magic. Light flooded his vision, turning it white, and pain shot through him as though his retinas were burning.
Was this what it felt like to be thrown into a vast pit of fire?
Or would dozens, hundreds of bolts of lightning striking down at once hurt like this?
But Jin Taekyung held on to the thread of his fading consciousness with all his might.
Fighting the pain that threatened to turn his mind to mush, he endured the unprecedented heat pouring down with the light.
Even that was enough to make his body and every memory in his head feel as though they were burning away.
Who he was.
Where he was.
Yet he did not forget the one thing that mattered: why he was enduring this terrible pain.
*I have to go back. No matter what.*
He had left something precious behind.
He had failed to protect what he needed to protect, and there was still something he had to do.
That alone was reason enough to endure.
If he could return, he could bear this agony, each second stretching into ten years.
Even the terrible heat that had seeped deep into his body and flowed through it like lava.
But widening his own limits did not mean every boundary had disappeared.
Kiiiiing.
This was a limit he could not overcome by will. A boundary he truly lacked the qualifications to cross.
And the moment Jin Taekyung realized it—
Ssshhh.
Thick clouds once again hid the light. The immense heat still flowing inside him spread through his body, passing through hundreds of acupoints rather than his Lower or Middle Dantian.
There it was absorbed, melting into him as though it had been part of his body from the start.
As though it were replenishing the natural strength of his body, damaged beyond recovery, and giving him still greater vitality and power.
*Ah.*
In that instant, Jin Taekyung understood.
His endurance had not been in vain.
The old man’s words—that it was time for each of them to return to their own places—could finally come true.
And his hunch was right.
Ding.
A clear chime rang out beyond the depths of his consciousness, and Jin Taekyung—
No.
I opened my eyes.
This time, I didn’t need anyone’s help.
As the dark blue radiance that had blazed for half a day slowly faded, a suffocating silence fell over everything.
The allies who had finally won this horrific bloodbath, and the fanatics who had survived by sheer luck and been captured—
No one dared speak.
It was as if even the dead were watching the figure slowly descend through the fading heat.
But unlike those frozen in place, forgetting even how to breathe, the old Master reached out with a trembling hand to catch his Disciple.
His body was warm now, like a campfire.
A thought struck Jeok Cheongang.
What if none of this were real?
If it were a spring dream unfolding in the mind of an old man who had already gone mad, what would he do?
He couldn’t bring himself to speak.
If this truly was a dream, he would rather never wake.
But someone knew what Jeok Cheongang did not.
That all of this was undeniably real.
“I kept my promise.”
Half-raised eyelids. A languid voice.
The Disciple smiled at the Master staring at him in a daze, then added:
“Master.”

chapters.title: Chapter 1133
paragraphs: The moment a small but unmistakable voice slipped between someone’s lips, the countless people surrounding him all widened their eyes at once, as if they’d agreed to do it together.
What should they call this?
Survival?
Or resurrection?
No one knew the answer.
All they knew was that something hot surged up from deep within their chests.
A choked roar rose beyond the Inner City, powerful enough to shake heaven and earth.
The rain that had poured down without end had long since stopped, but their cries didn’t let up.
Some wept. Some laughed. Others raised their weapons high and roared as if the battle still raged.
Exhausted as they were, they rejoiced with all their hearts.
The brutal bloodbath that had seemed as if it would never end was over.
And yet, alongside their joy, they felt a grief too deep for words.
They saw the empty places left by comrades who had stood shoulder to shoulder and fought back to back with them only several *shichen* ago.
Finally, they shuddered at the sight before their eyes: a young hero awakening amid a blue-black radiance, a miracle beyond belief.
His Master watched his Disciple with an expression of disbelief, then parted his trembling lips and spoke.
“Yeah. I believed in you.”
Despite his answer, his eyes were soaked with tears.
At the sight of Jeok Cheongang, Jin Taekyung said nothing. He only managed a faint smile.
Whether his Master had believed in him or not—what did it matter?
What mattered was the feeling in his Master’s tears, and that he had kept his promise.
*I’m back. Really.*
Perhaps it was because his mind was exhausted beyond its limits.
His consciousness was hazy, as if he’d sunk deep into sleep, but Jin Taekyung knew that everything around him was real.
The sky slowly clearing.
The familiar faces surrounding him now, laughing and crying, though he’d thought he would never see them again.
And—
Among the countless holographic windows floating in the air, the words that stood out largest and clearest.
**System** Innate qi has been restored! Status abnormality, Final Rally, has been lifted! The sudden Quest, A Candle in the Wind, or a Flame, has been successfully completed!
Would he become a candle, its flame dying helplessly away?
Or a blaze that devoured his enemies?
At that crossroads, Jin Taekyung had chosen the latter, and the dying ember inside him had finally been reignited.
The ember called innate qi.
And the second Bone Transformation that followed was nothing short of a miracle—one no one present could have expected.
Not even the peerless giant known as the Sword Saint.
“You make a lot of noise in your sleep. More than I ever imagined.”
At Mae Jonghak’s joking remark as he came over, Jin Taekyung let out a quiet snort of laughter.
“I almost woke up halfway through. It was so noisy around me.”
“Is it still?”
“Yes.”
Jin Taekyung glanced at his allies, who were still cheering, and added:
“But... it sounds good.”
It sounds good.
At Jin Taekyung’s brief comment, Mae Jonghak watched him in silence, then gave a small nod.
“Yes. I think so too.”
No one needed to ask about the battle’s outcome, or explain it.
The proof was all around them: countless allies surrounding them, and a handful of fanatics on their knees, bound from head to toe.
*The battle is over.*
At those few words, something hot surged up from one corner of Jin Taekyung’s chest.
Perhaps this was only a victory for today.
Today’s victory might be erased by a defeat tomorrow, whenever that day came.
But... for now, this was enough.
Enough that this horrific hellscape had come to an end.
Enough that they had defeated the enormous Dark Heaven army that had stood in their way like a mountain, along with the powerful enemies who led it.
*The Blood Lord. And the Grand Sorceress.*
Jin Taekyung lifted his head and looked northeast.
He didn’t know how many more enemies lurked beyond the vast desert outside Qinghai.
But the deaths of the Blood Lord and the Grand Sorceress on this battlefield were undoubtedly a major gain for the allies.
He couldn’t be certain, but as far as he could tell, those two had been the Lord of Heaven’s last hunting dogs.
*But... what is this feeling?*
A sudden sense of déjà vu made Jin Taekyung’s eyelids flutter.
Why?
He felt as if he’d forgotten something.
Something very important—something he couldn’t afford to overlook.
But it didn’t take him long to realize what that feeling was.
Whoooosh!
The next moment, Jin Taekyung’s eyes flew wide as he saw a dozen or so shadows shoot up into the distant sky.
*Those are...!*
They were none other than strange birds.
They flew across the sky with their wings spread wide, white bone joints exposed and blood-red eyes flashing.
Like messengers rushing to deliver urgent news to someone.
“No!”
The shout burst from him on instinct.
But before he could do anything, the birds, already far away, shot west at a speed far beyond anything they’d managed while alive.
They left one name flashing through Jin Taekyung’s mind like a bolt of lightning.
“...Ma Sanbao?”
He’d forgotten about him for a moment.
No—that wasn’t quite right. He hadn’t had even a moment to think about him.
The powerful corpse sorcerer who carried on the Maoshan Sect’s legacy had been hidden from sight by the shadows of the two monsters, the Blood Lord and the Grand Sorceress.
At the same time, the Blood Lord’s final words before he met his end rang through Jin Taekyung’s mind like an auditory hallucination.
*Celebrate to your heart’s content. This will be your last laugh.*
He hadn’t understood it then.
He’d thought those words were nothing more than the tired bluster of a defeated general.
But now, the chill running down Jin Taekyung’s spine foretold another crisis.
*Could it be?*
The tangled threads of information in his mind began to unravel one by one.
Ma Sanbao had never appeared on the battlefield, despite being an undeniably powerful asset—even if he was no match for the Blood Lord or the Grand Sorceress.
The Sword Saint and the Murim Alliance’s elite had traveled thousands of *li* to Qinghai without even telling their own allies the truth.
And then there were the strange birds that had watched everything unfold before flying west.
*Wait. If they’re heading west...*
No doubt about it.
Mount Kunlun.
That place, already in Dark Heaven’s grasp, had to be the birds’ destination.
At the same time, Jin Taekyung recalled one of the questions he still hadn’t answered.
Why had Dark Heaven’s enormous army, which had occupied Mount Kunlun before he and the reinforcements even set foot in Qinghai, remained so immovable?
Had the Blood Lord really made all these moves just to catch him and every other big fish in a single sweep of the net?
*No. That wasn’t all the Blood Lord was after from the start. It was just... they needed time, too.*
Perhaps it was because his mind was already exhausted beyond its limits.
Or perhaps because he’d finally grasped the shape of the foreboding he’d felt.
His face had turned as pale as paper as he looked at the people surrounding him. Without realizing it, Jin Taekyung let out the breath he’d been holding.
Along with two bitter words that had lingered on the tip of his tongue.
“...Moving Formation.”
That was the answer Jin Taekyung had found.
It was one of the main reasons Dark Heaven’s powerful army had hunkered down on Mount Kunlun—and the Blood Lord’s last move, prepared in case things went wrong.
And Ma Sanbao, the hidden blade, would move as soon as he heard this news.
Through the Moving Formation newly inscribed somewhere on Mount Kunlun, he would pierce the allies’ most vital point.
The very place called the Central Plains.
“We have to move. Right now. If we don’t, the Central Plains—”
Jin Taekyung’s voice trembled as he groaned.
His breath came hard, and his heart pounded.
Faces passed one after another through his wavering vision. Perhaps they shouldn’t have come here today at all.
Especially the man who had been known as the Sword Saint for decades, and was now the Alliance Leader.
But—
“Yes. We have to move.”
That was as far as Jin Taekyung could go.
Tap.
A hand suddenly touched the back of his neck.
In the same instant, Mae Jonghak struck him with a Pressure-Point Strike, swift as lightning. In an even voice, he continued:
“But this time, you’re going to rest.”
Jin Taekyung answered.
Or tried to.
No. Absolutely not. He couldn’t rest now.
But despite his desperate resolve, his lips wouldn’t move. Exhaustion and sleep washed over him, pressing down on his eyelids with the weight of ten thousand *geun*.
*Ah.*
As his vision went dark in an instant, Jin Taekyung let go of consciousness, a voice ringing in his ears like an auditory hallucination.
“You’ve done well, my friend.”
Qinghai is vast.
But the wings of the strange birds, granted boundless vigor by death, were swift enough to make the distance between Xining and Mount Kunlun—more than several hundred *li*—seem insignificant.
And the shocking news brought by these exceptional messengers, unlike any seen before or since, reached Mount Kunlun’s highest peak in less than a *shichen*.
No—
It reached a certain corpse sorcerer who carried on the Maoshan Sect’s legacy.
“...So that’s what happened.”
Ma Sanbao muttered to himself as he stared east, his gaze sinking deep.
The news was impossible to believe, but he had no choice.
More than a dozen strange birds had already relayed everything they’d seen and heard in vivid detail.
The outcome of a bloody battle that had raged without a break for half a day—and the presence of people he’d thought could never appear in Qinghai.
*I owe the Blood Lord an apology. I thought he was just a man crazed by blood.*
Ma Sanbao let out a quiet snort of laughter.
More than anyone, the Blood Lord had obsessed over Jin Taekyung. Yet by keeping one last move in reserve, he hadn’t forgotten his most basic loyalty to the master who held his leash.
A final sword stroke that would lay waste to the Central Plains, now all but undefended.
And Ma Sanbao was willing to play that part.
“It’s about time I left this wretched mountain.”
Ma Sanbao rose from the grand chair and addressed his waiting subordinates.
“Let’s go. To the Central Plains.”

But before he could do anything, the birds, already far away, shot west at a speed far beyond anything they’d managed while alive.
They left one name flashing through Jin Taekyung’s mind like a bolt of lightning.
“...Ma Sanbao?”
He’d forgotten about him for a moment.
No—that wasn’t quite right.
He hadn’t had even a moment to think about him.
The powerful corpse sorcerer who carried on the Maoshan Sect’s legacy had been hidden from sight by the shadows of the two monsters, the Blood Lord and the Grand Sorceress.
At the same time, the Blood Lord’s final words before he met his end rang through Jin Taekyung’s mind like an auditory hallucination.
*Celebrate to your heart’s content.
This will be your last laugh.*
He hadn’t understood it then.
He’d thought those words were nothing more than the tired bluster of a defeated general.
But now, the chill running down Jin Taekyung’s spine foretold another crisis.
*Could it be?*
The tangled threads of information in his mind began to unravel one by one.
Ma Sanbao had never appeared on the battlefield, despite being an undeniably powerful asset—even if he was no match for the Blood Lord or the Grand Sorceress.
The Sword Saint and the Murim Alliance’s elite had traveled thousands of *li* to Qinghai without even telling their own allies the truth.
And then there were the strange birds that had watched everything unfold before flying west.
*Wait.
If they’re heading west...*
No doubt about it.
Mount Kunlun.
That place, already in Dark Heaven’s grasp, had to be the birds’ destination.
At the same time, Jin Taekyung recalled one of the questions he still hadn’t answered.
Why had Dark Heaven’s enormous army, which had occupied Mount Kunlun before he and the reinforcements even set foot in Qinghai, remained so immovable?
Had the Blood Lord really made all these moves just to catch him and every other big fish in a single sweep of the net?
*No.
That wasn’t all the Blood Lord was after from the start.
It was just... they needed time, too.*
Perhaps it was because his mind was already exhausted beyond its limits.
Or perhaps because he’d finally grasped the shape of the foreboding he’d felt.
His face had turned as pale as paper as he looked at the people surrounding him.
Without realizing it, Jin Taekyung let out the breath he’d been holding.
Along with two bitter words that had lingered on the tip of his tongue.
“...Moving Formation.”
That was the answer Jin Taekyung had found.
It was one of the main reasons Dark Heaven’s powerful army had hunkered down on Mount Kunlun—and the Blood Lord’s last move, prepared in case things went wrong.
And Ma Sanbao, the hidden blade, would move as soon as he heard this news.
Through the Moving Formation newly inscribed somewhere on Mount Kunlun, he would pierce the allies’ most vital point.
The very place called the Central Plains.
“We have to move.
Right now.
If we don’t, the Central Plains—”
Jin Taekyung’s voice trembled as he groaned.
His breath came hard, and his heart pounded.
Faces passed one after another through his wavering vision.
Perhaps they shouldn’t have come here today at all.
Especially the man who had been known as the Sword Saint for decades, and was now the Alliance Leader.
But—
“Yes.
We have to move.”
That was as far as Jin Taekyung could go.
Tap.
A hand suddenly touched the back of his neck.
In the same instant, Mae Jonghak struck him with a Pressure-Point Strike, swift as lightning.
In an even voice, he continued:
“But this time, you’re going to rest.”
Jin Taekyung answered.
Or tried to.
No.
Absolutely not.
He couldn’t rest now.
But despite his desperate resolve, his lips wouldn’t move.
Exhaustion and sleep washed over him, pressing down on his eyelids with the weight of ten thousand *geun*.
*Ah.*
As his vision went dark in an instant, Jin Taekyung let go of consciousness, a voice ringing in his ears like an auditory hallucination.
“You’ve done well, my friend.”
Qinghai is vast.
But the wings of the strange birds, granted boundless vigor by death, were swift enough to make the distance between Xining and Mount Kunlun—more than several hundred *li*—seem insignificant.
And the shocking news brought by these exceptional messengers, unlike any seen before or since, reached Mount Kunlun’s highest peak in less than a *shichen*.
No—
It reached a certain corpse sorcerer who carried on the Maoshan Sect’s legacy.
“...So that’s what happened.”
Ma Sanbao muttered to himself as he stared east, his gaze sinking deep.
The news was impossible to believe, but he had no choice.
More than a dozen strange birds had already relayed everything they’d seen and heard in vivid detail.
The outcome of a bloody battle that had raged without a break for half a day—and the presence of people he’d thought could never appear in Qinghai.
*I owe the Blood Lord an apology.
I thought he was just a man crazed by blood.*
Ma Sanbao let out a quiet snort of laughter.
More than anyone, the Blood Lord had obsessed over Jin Taekyung.
Yet by keeping one last move in reserve, he hadn’t forgotten his most basic loyalty to the master who held his leash.
A final sword stroke that would lay waste to the Central Plains, now all but undefended.
And Ma Sanbao was willing to play that part.
“It’s about time I left this wretched mountain.”
Ma Sanbao rose from the grand chair and addressed his waiting subordinates.
“Let’s go.
To the Central Plains.”

chapters.title: Chapter 1134
paragraphs: The air on Mount Kunlun was heavy and cold that day.
Mist lay thick over the towering peaks. The creatures large and small that had once shared this beautiful wilderness with humans had long since vanished.
Only blood-red eyes glimmered through the dense mist, accompanied by eerie cries.
“Grrr.”
A savage growl came from between yellowed teeth.
The mountain lord that had ruled Mount Kunlun only a month ago lowered its body, now larger than it had been in life, to greet its master.
Around it, thousands of human demons surrounded Taiqing Hall—the very symbol of the Kunlun Sect—without leaving a single gap.
“Everyone has gathered, as you commanded.”
The report came from one of the hundred or so figures wrapped head to toe in jet-black robes. Ma Sanbao asked eagerly, “How many in all?”
“About five thousand. Three thousand of them are monsters.”
A smile touched Ma Sanbao’s lips.
“Then Mount Kunlun’s spiritual creatures must be extinct.”
Anyone familiar with the state of Murim who heard their purpose and conversation might have scoffed at such an absurd claim.
Five thousand was no small number, but even the Hundred Thousand Demonic Disciples, who had once blanketed the world in darkness, had failed to take the Central Plains.
Ma Sanbao had good reason to smile, though.
*It’s enough. More than enough.*
Ma Sanbao swept his sunken gaze over the subordinates packed in all around him.
The monsters’ blood-red eyes flashed without pause. The fanatics moved only at his command, little more than soulless puppets.
Fully prepared and waiting for Ma Sanbao’s orders, they deserved to be called a Demon Army. Comparing them to the mere Demonic Cult, now a ghost of the past, would be an insult.
But the greatest source of his confidence was the hundred or so corpse sorcerers before him, including the man in black.
None could compare to Ma Sanbao himself, but each was a true monster capable of leading an army so long as there were corpses to use.
He regarded them with satisfaction, then spoke.
“We’ll split the army in two and move out.”
“Forgive me, but has the plan changed?”
Ma Sanbao nodded at the black-clad man’s cautious question.
Under the original plan, they would have split into seven groups and spread chaos across the land. But circumstances had changed.
Sword Saint Mae Jonghak had appeared in Qinghai with no fewer than ten thousand elite troops from the Murim Alliance.
*Who would’ve thought the Alliance Leader himself would bring reinforcements?*

Ma Sanbao had stayed behind in case something like this happened. Even so, Mae Jonghak’s arrival had surprised him as much as the Green Forest Alliance and the Yangtze River Channel League’s betrayal.
But the fact that Alliance Leader Mae Jonghak had left the Murim Alliance meant he must have left at least a minimal defense in Henan.
*Of course, with its main force gone, it’ll be nowhere near enough. Still, to prepare for any eventuality, we’d be wise not to spread ourselves too thin.*

This was an opportunity Ma Sanbao had won with great difficulty—perhaps even a stroke of heavenly fortune. Given what the corpse sorcerers could do, his caution might be excessive. But he wanted the safest, surest course.
He meant to hold a place second only to one and above ten thousand in the world remade under the Lord of Heaven’s rule. He had no intention of meeting a miserable end like the Blood Lord.
After careful thought, he had narrowed his targets to two places.
“Henan and Shanxi.”
At his superior’s voice, which broke the brief silence, the black-clad man bowed deeply.
“As you command. An excellent decision.”
With the Jin Family of Taiyuan away, Shanxi Province was all but an ownerless mountain. Henan, meanwhile, had to be taken for both its symbolic importance to Murim and its strategic location.
With Mae Jonghak gone, this was the perfect chance to seize it.
Henan and Shanxi also shared a border. Should anything go wrong, the two forces could support each other.
“If I give you two thousand troops and half the sorcerers, can you take Shanxi Province within seven days and nights?”
Shanxi Province had grown stronger by the day since the Jin Family of Taiyuan united it.
The black-clad man answered without hesitation. His force might number a *mere* two thousand now, but with *dozens* of corpse sorcerers, it would multiply without end.
“Four days will suffice.”
“And if I include Hebei?”
“Give me ten days. I’ll return leading an army of a hundred thousand.”
Ma Sanbao’s smile deepened at the ready answer.
“I’ll remember that promise.”
At that very moment—
Sssaaaa.
Faint strands of light began to rise from the ground.
The Moving Formation the Grand Sorceress had installed during her stay on Mount Kunlun—no, the Magic Formation—was activating under the hands of the sorcerers who had remained with Ma Sanbao.
Vroooom.
Two enormous circles of light spread outward, growing by the second until they enveloped everyone.
Ma Sanbao felt a mysterious surge of energy from every direction and trembled with elation.
*I’ll end it all in one stroke. With my own two hands.*
No one who knew him could deny that his confidence was justified.
He was the most powerful corpse sorcerer to carry on the Maoshan Sect’s legacy. As a martial artist, he was also a Supreme Peak master who could stand shoulder to shoulder with the Ten Kings.
With the Three Saints, Jin Taekyung, and Jeok Cheongang all absent, nothing in the Central Plains’ Murim frightened him.
*Sword Saint, you of all people shouldn’t have left.*
Whatever defenses they had prepared, this force could cut through the heart of the Central Plains in an instant.
By the time word of its arrival reached the enemy, the army would number tens of thousands rather than thousands.
An immortal army whose ranks would fill again no matter how many times its soldiers were killed.
*Today, the course of history changes.*
The world would remember forever that Ma Sanbao had been there for the first step of a grand new history that would endure a thousand years.
Fwoosh!
A brilliant flash washed his vision white. Smiling, Ma Sanbao closed his eyes and yielded to the mysterious force pulling his spirit and body toward a distant place.
He imagined the great strides he would take, one after another, and the mighty trail they would carve across the world.
Paht.
The change was instantaneous.
The air and wind around him were different now. Instinctively, Ma Sanbao knew the Grand Sorceress’s Magic Formation had carried him and some three thousand of his subordinates to the promised place.
*At last, it begins.*
Thrilled to be taking that great first step, Ma Sanbao opened his eyes.
Or rather, he tried to.
Crunch—splat!
A gruesome sound of flesh being torn rang out, and something hot and sticky covered his face before he could open them.
The smell of blood seeped deep into his nostrils, all too familiar.
It felt as though the world had stopped. Ma Sanbao struggled to lift his trembling eyelids.
Then he saw clearly what else he had failed to realize.
Thump. Splatter.
In some nameless, remote mountain valley where even the moonlight didn’t reach, large and small figures crumpled like bundles of straw without so much as a dying cry.
Ma Sanbao could neither move nor stop it. The survivors around him were no different.
All they could do was stare blankly at the deaths of fully two thousand of their comrades, felled before they could take their first step in Henan.
Their bodies had become one with rocks and trees rather than falling to blades or spears. They lay dead in hideous, unnatural shapes.
“What... What in the world...”
Just then, an unexpected answer reached Ma Sanbao’s ears as he muttered in a dazed voice, as if under a spell.
“What do you think? Exactly what you’re looking at.”
A calm voice sounded from the darkness.
Ma Sanbao whipped his head toward it like lightning and stared.
How long had that man been there?
Several dozen *jang* away, a middle-aged man stood atop a hill that ringed the basin like a wall. He looked down over the fear and confusion below.
No—he was looking at Ma Sanbao.
“Good to meet you. I mean that. I was so worried you wouldn’t come that I could hardly stand it.”
The man slowly surveyed Ma Sanbao, frozen stiff as a statue, and the subordinates who had survived. He smacked his lips.
“I can’t say I’m not a little disappointed...but I suppose that was enough of a welcome. Don’t you think?”
Ma Sanbao did not answer.
He couldn’t. Right then, it was all he could do to grasp the word filling his blank mind.
*A trap...!*
Yes. This was a trap, and a meticulously prepared one.

And the refined-looking middle-aged man smiling on the hill was unmistakably the one who had laid a trap in the Moving Formation the Grand Sorceress had carved deep into a remote valley in Henan that no one ever visited.
A hunter who had set the simplest, surest, most horrific trap of all.
“Don’t glare at me like that. I’m the disappointed one. If I’d known the Moving Formation’s exact range, I could have finished you all in one stroke.”
The man even let out a theatrical sigh. Ma Sanbao felt his blood boil.
“You’ll regret that you didn’t. I’ll tear you and every last member of your household to pieces.”
The man had not introduced himself, but Ma Sanbao already knew who he was.
The portrait Ma Sanbao had seen during his years in the East Depot and the pure-white fan in the man’s hand left little doubt.
“Crouching Dragon Guest, Zhuge Feng.”
Zhuge Feng, the current Family Head of the Zhuge Clan, widened his eyes.
“Oh? You know me?”
“I do. I remembered you. After today, though, I’ll forget you.”
Ma Sanbao drew up the qi within him.
The trap had cost him more than half his subordinates, but the corpse sorcerers—his most important force—had suffered little damage.
Once the fighting began, there would be more corpses.
Whatever Zhuge Feng had prepared, Ma Sanbao was certain he would be the one to leave this valley alive at sunrise.
At least, he was until a familiar face appeared behind Zhuge Feng.
“Then you remember me, too. Don’t you, Eunuch Ma?”
A chill passed through Ma Sanbao’s chest.
How could he forget a face he had seen for decades? Or the resonant voice of the veteran general who had protected the imperial household through every peril?
But Baek Yeon, the Commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard and the imperial household’s greatest master, was not the only reason Ma Sanbao was shaken.
If the man who served as the imperial household’s sword and shield was here, it meant something else.
Scuff.
A slender figure stepped out from behind the burly veteran.
He looked down at his former servant with the haughty gaze only someone born to noble blood could possess.
No—at the criminal for the ages who had dared to overthrow the imperial household.
“So, was playing traitor worth it?”
At the Son of Heaven’s question, Ma Sanbao groaned.

chapters.title: Chapter 1135
paragraphs: On a hill washed in faint moonlight, his sudden appearance seemed utterly out of place.
Not just to Ma Sanbao. To all of them.
Then the voice that slipped between his pale lips revealed the source of that unease.
“So, was playing traitor worth it?”
His tone was as calm as still water. Yet beneath it lay an authority only a ruler could possess.
It was dignity.

Neither his black robe, blending into the darkness, nor the bamboo hat pulled low over his face could conceal it. He needed no elaborate imperial robe or crown of hanging beads. That dignity was his by birth.
“It’s been a long time, Palace Attendant Ma.”
He spoke down to Ma Sanbao as if looking at him from a dizzying height.
Ma Sanbao stifled a groan at the Son of Heaven’s unexpected appearance, then spoke in a low voice.
“What brings Your Majesty all the way here?”
“I came to take care of some urgent business.”
“Was it important enough to leave the Imperial Capital?”
“How curious. Why don’t you think I prepared thoroughly enough to leave the capital?”
“A mere traitor like you needn’t worry about the capital’s safety. Not while the Twelve Palaces of the Zodiac are guarding it.”
The Son of Heaven fixed his deep, sunken gaze on Ma Sanbao, who had fallen silent.
The Twelve Palaces of the Zodiac.
Twelve Supreme Peak masters who protected the imperial household.

Though few remained after the rebellion led by the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord, now that they knew the Moving Formation’s location, those masters and the Imperial Guards under their command were more than enough.
Provided, of course, that the enemy attacked the capital.
“Enough bluffing. If you’d planned to strike the capital in the first place, you and I wouldn’t be facing each other here. Isn’t that right?”
The remark hit home. Ma Sanbao quietly licked his dry lips.
The Son of Heaven was right.
The instant he received word from the strange birds, Ma Sanbao had erased the Imperial Capital from his mind.

If he captured the capital and took the Son of Heaven, he could bring the world to its knees. But the Murim of the Central Plains, already left with a massive gap in its defenses, was far more tempting prey.
Why take the hard road when a faster, easier one lay open?
And that assumption had been Ma Sanbao’s greatest blunder.
“...Not bad, Zhu Di.”
Speaking the Son of Heaven’s personal name was high treason in itself.
Ma Sanbao didn’t care. He had never once considered himself the Son of Heaven’s subject.
Now, with nowhere left to retreat, he wanted an answer to the one question that remained.
“How did you find this place?”
It wasn’t the Son of Heaven who answered, but Zhuge Feng.
“Two years.”
“What?”
“Ah, don’t misunderstand. I wasn’t calling you a bitch. I know you’re a eunuch, but you certainly look like a man, not a woman.”
Zhuge Feng smiled at Ma Sanbao’s stiffened face and continued.
“Since we discovered the Moving Formation, we’ve searched the whole world with a fine-tooth comb. Not quite two years, actually. More like a year and a half.”

“Oh, yes. When I started this madness, I had exactly the look you have now. My retainers looked even worse. My seniors, the Sword King and Fist King, tried to strangle me. The late Blade King was worse still.”
Zhuge Feng rubbed the back of his neck at the memory. Ma Sanbao stared at him in disbelief.
“You searched for them? You even brought in the Ten Kings?”
“I understand how you feel. But what else could we have done?”
With a sigh, Zhuge Feng gently waved the feather fan in his hand.
The first month or two had been hell.
No, worse. At least hell had sulfur fires burning here and there. They had felt as if they were adrift in the middle of an endless ocean.
But it hadn’t taken long to find their first result.
“We found one after three months. Hidden deep in Mount Huang in Anhui. Fortunately, the search went much faster after that.”
The entire operation had been conducted in the utmost secrecy, using only people who had passed the Hidden Shadow Pavilion’s screening.
Membership in the Nine Sects and One Gang or the Five Great Families made no difference. Not even a Sect Leader was exempt.
They answered to one person alone—the Alliance Leader—and faithfully carried out their assigned tasks.

Myriad-Mile Pursuit, Gung Gibang’s master and the Beggars’ Sect Leader, mobilized every trusted subordinate he could alongside the Lower District Sect to look for places where a Moving Formation might be hidden. The Zhuge Clan’s and Hidden Shadow Pavilion’s strategists used what they brought back to narrow down the locations.
“No matter how difficult a problem is, you can find the answer once you know how to solve it. Fortunately, finding the Moving Formations worked the same way.”
Even for Zhuge Feng, renowned as a prodigy since childhood, it had been an extraordinarily difficult problem. But before long, he worked out the method.
He looked for places few people visited, where qi flowed with unusual strength, where there was room for at least several hundred people, and where no grass grew.
Zhuge Feng selected sites that met those conditions. Once he made his choice, renowned formation masters from the Zhuge Clan and masters with exceptional Qi Sense went to verify them in person.
Supreme Peak masters such as the Azure Sky Sword King, Grand Family Head of the Namgung Family, and the Fist King were among them.
“But no matter how hard we tried, we didn’t have enough people. We had a fair number, but searching the vast Nine Provinces thoroughly while keeping the secret was beyond us.”
Not a single mistake could be allowed.
Even the sturdiest wall could begin to collapse with one tiny crack.
In that sense, each Moving Formation was a vast powder keg. A single one going off could set the whole world ablaze.
Then, a few months ago, help came from an unexpected source. Zhuge Feng could finally put the last of his worries to rest.
“I heard a certain person of high standing told the Alliance Leader he’d do anything he could to help. And he was a tremendous help.”
At Zhuge Feng’s words, the “person of high standing” spoke up.
“Surely you mean the person of *highest* standing?”
“Ah, forgive my discourtesy, Your Majesty.”
“Of course. I’ll forgive anything short of high treason.”
Ma Sanbao had listened blankly to their exchange. Now he clenched his teeth.
*They got me. Completely.*
The enemies in the Central Plains must have waited for this very moment.
Though they could have shut down the Moving Formations they found, they had left them alone and laid a perfect trap instead.
They had let their prey come running, mouths watering, so they could root out their last remaining concern.
“Is that how you dealt with the advance party, too?”
Zhuge Feng gently waved his feather fan.
“Huashan wiped them out as soon as they arrived. The Murim Alliance’s elite, led by the Alliance Leader, took their place.”
“Our information clearly said they’d joined those two bandit bastards.”
“What’s so hard about that? We only needed a similar number of people dressed in black. Word was bound to spread on its own. And it did.”
The ten thousand fanatics who were supposed to join the Green Forest Alliance and the Yangtze River Channel League had died before they ever boarded the league’s ships.
And the Seafaring King, Pa Ryun, had kept the truth thoroughly concealed.

Even subduing his disciple, Ship-Fire Boy Mu Song, had been a way to protect the secret. If Mu Song, who hadn’t been told the plan, acted on his sense of justice, he might expose the fact that the people aboard the rear ships—deliberately kept separate—belonged to the Murim Alliance.
“But then what about the fleet of hundreds of ships the river bandits destroyed...?”
Ma Sanbao trailed off.
The Son of Heaven’s cold smile had given him the answer to his last question.
“I see. So that’s what happened.”
At last, Ma Sanbao understood everything. A hollow laugh escaped him.
He had forgotten for a moment.
Beneath the Son of Heaven’s pale skin, instead of hot, red blood, ran cold iron and blood.
“The palace’s underground prison must be empty by now. Zhu Di, was this your doing?”
The Son of Heaven answered evenly.
“There were so many traitors eating away at the nation that killing them one by one became a chore. They paid a price of their own, so it wasn’t such a bad end for them.”
After the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s rebellion came a purge without precedent in the Great Nation’s history.
The Son of Heaven had made an offer to the many prisoners who survived it and still awaited punishment.
They could die with their families, as the law required, or spend the rest of their lives as slaves. Or they could lift even a little of the stain from their family names.
Naturally, most chose the last option.
Freed from the chains and restraints that bound them, they accepted spears and blades with trembling hands and boarded the Great Nation’s ships.
All the while, they repeated the Son of Heaven’s promise to themselves: because of their choice, someone of their blood would survive to carry on the family name.
“Right. No wonder it went more smoothly than I expected. Rotten as their forces were, it was strange for them to suffer a defeat that crushing.”
They hadn’t been trained soldiers. Even with hundreds of ships and cannons, their annihilation had been inevitable.
Now that he knew the full extent of the audacious plan—one only the Son of Heaven could have carried out, throwing all those prisoners to the enemy as bait—Ma Sanbao could only laugh.
No. He had to laugh.
A hollow laugh, as though he had given up, was the only way to conceal his last chance.
*Not yet. It’s not over yet.*
His mouth smiled. His eyes did not.
Ma Sanbao quickly swept his sunken gaze around.
On the hills encircling them, countless arrowheads poked quietly through the thick grass. He sensed his subordinates holding their breath, waiting for his command.
*They outnumber us at least five to one. Maybe more.*
It didn’t matter.
If he could capture just one of the enemies who had prepared so thoroughly, he could turn this desperate situation around.
No—he might do more than that. He might seize everything.
That was what the Son of Heaven represented.
Besides, Ma Sanbao and his men had no other choice.
“Now—!”
It all happened in an instant.
Ma Sanbao’s mighty shout as he kicked off the ground and shot upward.
The taut bowstrings released their arrows all at once.
And—
*Whoosh!*
Before the countless arrows that couldn’t keep up with his lightning speed had even finished sweeping across the ground, a low whistle of air split through the space above Ma Sanbao’s head.
*No Shadow...!*
Ma Sanbao clenched his teeth at the masked figure who had appeared in his path.
It was him.
Ma Sanbao had never seen his face clearly, but he knew of the Son of Heaven’s hidden bodyguard.
The imperial household’s greatest assassin, who never even revealed his shadow, was bringing down a dagger wrapped in Force beneath the faint moonlight.
Just as Ma Sanbao had expected.
*Shhk!*
With a gruesome sound of torn flesh, the blade sank into his forearm.
Ma Sanbao paid it no mind. He thrust out his half-severed left hand and struck No Shadow.
*Crack!*
No Shadow went flying from the force of the blow. Ma Sanbao drove internal energy into the tips of his feet and released it.
*Boom!*
He shot down toward the hill like a falling star.
The White Illusion Jiangshi Art, grown stronger still since the bloody battle at the imperial palace, let him forget pain and fear.
“Zhu Di!”
Ma Sanbao roared.
A dozen or so arrows shot from his blind spots and buried themselves across his body. Zhuge Feng and Baek Yeon blocked his path. But his corpse-gray eyes remained fixed on one person alone.
The Son of Heaven, his pale face still bearing the unmistakable signs of illness, just as it had the last time Ma Sanbao saw him.
*Shhk! Thud!*
*Crack!*
There was no blood left to spill from a body already little different from a jiangshi. Only chunks of flesh and pieces of bone flew through the air.
But his desperate will remained.
*Slash!*
Baek Yeon’s crescent-bladed polearm bit into Ma Sanbao’s left shoulder and sliced diagonally through his upper body.
*Crack!*
Ma Sanbao’s one remaining hand finally closed around what he wanted.
The Son of Heaven’s throat.
“Everyone, stop.”
Silence fell.
Before the Son of Heaven could draw the sword at his waist, Ma Sanbao had seized and immobilized him with lightning speed. He smiled faintly.
Then he whispered into the ear of the Son of Heaven, whose pressure points he had struck.
“Thank you. You came all the way here yourself, so—”
*Thud.*
Ma Sanbao blinked.
Why?
How could the Son of Heaven move after his pressure points had been struck?
And why, now that they were face-to-face, was the Son of Heaven’s skin so much like his own?
“...You. Don’t tell me—”
*Crack.*
The Son of Heaven slowly twisted the hand that had pierced the center of Ma Sanbao’s chest and spoke.
“A few months ago, someone gave me a great gift. Something you know well.”
“I thought long and hard about it. It was a blessing, but every bit as much a curse.”
The Son of Heaven’s deliberation had not lasted long, though. His only remaining blood relative, the sole heir who would inherit the realm, had made him a request.
“He told me to live a thousand years. Not as the Son of Heaven, but as family—as someone he wanted to stay with for a long time.”
Moved by Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao’s sincerity—no, Imperial Younger Brother Zhu Bao’s—the Son of Heaven made his choice.
Even if it meant breaking a taboo. Even if he might one day regret it, he would stay with his younger brother for as long as he was allowed.
And that choice had brought them to this moment.
“Now I understand why Jin Taekyung gave me the White Illusion Jiangshi Art. It wasn’t just for me... It was for my brother, who would otherwise be left alone again.”
At that moment—
“By the law of the Great Nation, I punish this traitor.”
*Crack!*
The Son of Heaven’s voice was the last Ma Sanbao would ever hear. The world before his eyes went black.

paragraphs: No one could survive having their heart crushed.
That simple truth held even for someone who had mastered the White Illusion Jiangshi Art, one of the foremost among the world’s countless monstrous martial arts and supreme techniques.
Thud.
His body crumpled like a rotten old tree.
The Son of Heaven looked down in silence at the traitor who had finally met his end. Then he pulled his hand from deep inside the man’s chest and spoke.
“Commander.”
The brief call contained no instruction, but it was enough for Baek Yeon, Commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
“At your command.”
The reverence he showed the Son of Heaven, who had personally executed the traitor, came as naturally as flowing water.
So did the crescent-bladed polearm that flashed downward.
*Shhk!*
Flesh and bone parted with a chilling slice.
Baek Yeon beheaded the traitor in a single stroke, then speared the severed head on the tip of his polearm and held it upright.
The traitor’s eyes had frozen wide open before they could close. Now they would watch the scene below the hill to the very end.
*Shh-shh-shh-shh-shhk!*
It wasn’t just one person who thought the sky had suddenly darkened.

Thousands of Imperial Guards, every one of them an elite chosen to serve the Son of Heaven, loosed their powerful bows at once. Their arrows, propelled by internal energy, covered the sky and rained down with tremendous speed and force.
They fell upon the enemies struggling desperately in the shallow basin dozens of *jang* away.
*Thwup-thwup-thwup!*
“Gaaah!”
Blood and screams burst forth without pause.
At the start of the battle, many of the fanatics had taken Temporary Strength Pills. They swung Sword Energy as they closed the distance, but even at full speed, they could not reach the hill.
“Open.”
*Fwoosh.*
At Zhuge Feng’s quiet command, a strange energy drifting through the air rose like heat haze.
Thick fog swallowed the base of the hill in an instant.
The fanatics fell into confusion at the sight of illusions unlike any they had seen before. Then a second command rang out.
“Close.”
*Clack.*
With a cold metallic sound, countless hidden weapons and arrowheads emerged all around them.
The Zhuge Clan’s mechanisms and formations, hailed as the finest in the world, had finally revealed themselves.
The result was a horrific death.
*Fwoosh, splat!*
The fog turned red.
Everything inside was pierced, cut, and smashed to pieces.
From between rocks, beneath the earth, and even the knots in trees, traps sprang from gaps no one would have thought to watch. In moments, the fanatics were driven to their deaths.
A few escaped the fog by using their allies’ corpses as shields, but Zhuge Feng had prepared more than that.
*Fwoosh!*
The Zhuge Clan retainers numbered a mere hundred. The terrifying rate of fire of their Zhuge Repeating Crossbows was more than enough to make up for their small numbers.
Far more than enough.
*Crack-crack-crack!*
In the blink of an eye, riddled bodies piled up.
The battle that had begun in the dead of night was still going on, but what unfolded before everyone’s eyes made even the word *battle* seem inadequate.
A slaughter this one-sided could hardly be called a battle.
And this hellscape was not unfolding only in Henan.
“Looks like it’ll be a long night.”
Zhuge Feng answered the Son of Heaven’s sudden murmur.
“And soon, the sun will rise.”
He was right.
No matter how long the night, day would come. Another day would begin beneath a sun as bright as ever—or brighter.
Tonight, they would eliminate one of the great threats hanging over the Central Plains.
“Though a wise man should never be too certain... I, Zhuge Feng, have no doubt.”
He had put everything he had into this plan. For a long time, Zhuge Feng had waited, deceiving not only the enemy but even his allies.
All for today. For this very moment.
“Wherever the traitors go, they won’t escape death.”
Zhuge Feng spoke with conviction.
They had gathered each province’s elite at every Moving Formation they had found. Wherever Dark Heaven’s dagger was aimed, its forces would be dead before the night was over.
That was especially true of Shanxi, which Zhuge Feng had judged, alongside Henan, to be the enemy’s most likely target.
A giant called the Azure Sky Sword King was leading the forces there.
“It is all thanks to Your Majesty’s help.”
The Son of Heaven gave a quiet laugh at Zhuge Feng’s respectful thanks.
“Is that so? I wonder if the Commander agrees.”
Baek Yeon, standing beside him, answered without hesitation.
“Of course not. They did all the hard work. The Imperial House only lent a hand at the end.”
Zhuge Feng’s mouth fell open at the unexpected answer, but the Son of Heaven’s smile deepened.
“Why?”
“Don’t ask when you already know, Your Majesty.”
“That’s a rather irreverent way to speak. You couldn’t even stop the traitor just now.”
Baek Yeon frowned.
“That was because Your Majesty kept insisting you would deal with him yourself. What, are you going to strip me of my office?”
“That would be inconvenient. I still need you.”
“Your Majesty’s wisdom grows deeper by the day. As your servant, I could not be happier. Though after all the trouble I go through, it’s a shame my salary hasn’t budged in years.”
“My, my. Is that any way for the Commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard to speak? We’ve recovered the traitors’ wealth, so I’ll double your salary.”
“Perhaps I’m getting old. My armor feels heavy today.”
“Triple it.”
“I am overwhelmed by Your Majesty’s grace, Your Majesty.”
Baek Yeon gave a crisp salute, then glanced up at the Son of Heaven.
As if on cue, sovereign and subject burst out laughing. They laughed so heartily that Zhuge Feng, watching the absurd exchange, was left speechless.
But the man born of the noblest bloodline in the world did not mind in the slightest.
The old general who had guarded the Imperial House for decades had every right to speak that way. Besides, everything he had said was true.
“Yes. The Commander is right. I only lent a hand at the end. That isn’t enough to repay even a tenth of the debt I owe.”
The Son of Heaven smiled at the bewildered Zhuge Feng.
In the past, when life had been like walking on thin ice, danger had lurked on every side and he had fought against illness. He had not been able to smile like this.
But now things were different.
No—Jin Taekyung had made them different. He had changed everything and restored the laughter the Son of Heaven had lost long ago.
The Son of Heaven knew that better than anyone. He could not accept Zhuge Feng’s praise, even as a courtesy.
He was alive because of Jin Taekyung. The realm could weather another crisis because of him, too.
“It’s troubling. How am I supposed to repay a debt that keeps growing?”
At the Son of Heaven’s rueful murmur, Zhuge Feng’s gaze grew serious.
“Perhaps... we’re all wondering the same thing.”
The three of them turned to look west.
They could see nothing there, yet each seemed to glimpse one man somewhere thousands of *li* away. Like the faint light beginning to spread over their shoulders.
“The sun’s risen.”
“Yes. Day is breaking.”
The Son of Heaven blinked as though he were seeing light for the first time.
Perhaps it was only his imagination.
The basin lay silent amid pools of blood, thousands of corpses piled like mountains. Yet the sunlight reaching across them seemed brighter than ever.
“Bright.”
Darkness scattered. Light blazed.
The Son of Heaven fervently hoped the countless days ahead would be the same.
And that Jin Taekyung’s fate, which would surely once again leave him standing at the edge of life and death, casting everything he had aside, would be bright as well.
“Great Ming.”
With that new name for the nation, one that would light the way ahead for everyone, the Son of Heaven of the Great Ming Empire let out the breath swelling in his chest.
“Baek Yeon.”
“Your orders, Your Majesty?”
“I think I’ll have to quadruple your salary. What lies ahead will be difficult.”
“What do you mean...?”
“I will not return to the palace.”
“Tell every person in the realm: I will not sit upon the throne until those vile traitors lurking beyond the desert have been rooted out.”
The old general stared at the Son of Heaven, eyes wide. Then he smiled and knelt on one knee.
“I, Baek Yeon, Commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, accept Your Majesty’s imperial decree.”
That day, countless messenger pigeons and mounted couriers crossed the skies and lands of the realm.
Carried by wings and hooves, the imperial decree spread across the realm in just a few days.
No—it shook the realm to its core.
Murim, the common people, even the government.
“By imperial decree!”
Messengers posted proclamations bearing the imperial seal wherever they went. At last, everyone learned of the blade that had been poised at their throats.
And of the one-sided, momentous victory that had begun and ended in a single night.
But victory was not all the Son of Heaven wished to announce.
He would lead an expedition himself.

Back when he was known as the Fourth Prince, the Son of Heaven had already been judged to have the makings of a conqueror. Now, under the new name of Great Ming, he ordered the Imperial Guards to assemble, and his destination was exactly what everyone had expected.
Xinjiang.
The former stronghold of the Demonic Cult, beyond the scorching desert.
The spearheads of the whole realm were aimed at the leader of the traitors, who dared to call himself the Lord of Heaven.

sentences.text: No one could survive having their heart crushed.
That simple truth held even for someone who had mastered the White Illusion Jiangshi Art, one of the foremost among the world’s countless monstrous martial arts and supreme techniques.
Thud.
His body crumpled like a rotten old tree.
The Son of Heaven looked down in silence at the traitor who had finally met his end.
Then he pulled his hand from deep inside the man’s chest and spoke.
“Commander.”
The brief call contained no instruction, but it was enough for Baek Yeon, Commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
“At your command.”
The reverence he showed the Son of Heaven, who had personally executed the traitor, came as naturally as flowing water.
So did the crescent-bladed polearm that flashed downward.
*Shhk!*
Flesh and bone parted with a chilling slice.
Baek Yeon beheaded the traitor in a single stroke, then speared the severed head on the tip of his polearm and held it upright.
The traitor’s eyes had frozen wide open before they could close.
Now they would watch the scene below the hill to the very end.
*Shh-shh-shh-shh-shhk!*
It wasn’t just one person who thought the sky had suddenly darkened.
Thousands of Imperial Guards, every one of them an elite chosen to serve the Son of Heaven, loosed their powerful bows at once.
Their arrows, propelled by internal energy, covered the sky and rained down with tremendous speed and force.
They fell upon the enemies struggling desperately in the shallow basin dozens of *jang* away.
*Thwup-thwup-thwup!*
“Gaaah!”
Blood and screams burst forth without pause.
At the start of the battle, many of the fanatics had taken Temporary Strength Pills.
They swung Sword Energy as they closed the distance, but even at full speed, they could not reach the hill.
“Open.”
*Fwoosh.*
At Zhuge Feng’s quiet command, a strange energy drifting through the air rose like heat haze.
Thick fog swallowed the base of the hill in an instant.
The fanatics fell into confusion at the sight of illusions unlike any they had seen before.
Then a second command rang out.
“Close.”
*Clack.*
With a cold metallic sound, countless hidden weapons and arrowheads emerged all around them.
The Zhuge Clan’s mechanisms and formations, hailed as the finest in the world, had finally revealed themselves.
The result was a horrific death.
*Fwoosh, splat!*
The fog turned red.
Everything inside was pierced, cut, and smashed to pieces.
From between rocks, beneath the earth, and even the knots in trees, traps sprang from gaps no one would have thought to watch.
In moments, the fanatics were driven to their deaths.
A few escaped the fog by using their allies’ corpses as shields, but Zhuge Feng had prepared more than that.
*Fwoosh!*
The Zhuge Clan retainers numbered a mere hundred.
The terrifying rate of fire of their Zhuge Repeating Crossbows was more than enough to make up for their small numbers.
Far more than enough.
*Crack-crack-crack!*
In the blink of an eye, riddled bodies piled up.
The battle that had begun in the dead of night was still going on, but what unfolded before everyone’s eyes made even the word *battle* seem inadequate.
A slaughter this one-sided could hardly be called a battle.
And this hellscape was not unfolding only in Henan.
“Looks like it’ll be a long night.”
Zhuge Feng answered the Son of Heaven’s sudden murmur.
“And soon, the sun will rise.”
He was right.
No matter how long the night, day would come.
Another day would begin beneath a sun as bright as ever—or brighter.
Tonight, they would eliminate one of the great threats hanging over the Central Plains.
“Though a wise man should never be too certain...
I, Zhuge Feng, have no doubt.”
He had put everything he had into this plan.
For a long time, Zhuge Feng had waited, deceiving not only the enemy but even his allies.
All for today.
For this very moment.
“Wherever the traitors go, they won’t escape death.”
Zhuge Feng spoke with conviction.
They had gathered each province’s elite at every Moving Formation they had found.
Wherever Dark Heaven’s dagger was aimed, its forces would be dead before the night was over.
That was especially true of Shanxi, which Zhuge Feng had judged, alongside Henan, to be the enemy’s most likely target.
A giant called the Azure Sky Sword King was leading the forces there.
“It is all thanks to Your Majesty’s help.”
The Son of Heaven gave a quiet laugh at Zhuge Feng’s respectful thanks.
“Is that so?
I wonder if the Commander agrees.”
Baek Yeon, standing beside him, answered without hesitation.
“Of course not.
They did all the hard work.
The Imperial House only lent a hand at the end.”
Zhuge Feng’s mouth fell open at the unexpected answer, but the Son of Heaven’s smile deepened.
“Why?”
“Don’t ask when you already know, Your Majesty.”
“That’s a rather irreverent way to speak.
You couldn’t even stop the traitor just now.”
Baek Yeon frowned.

I still need you.”

chapters.title: Chapter 1137
paragraphs: Many people call the Central Plains the center of the world, but the phrase has a more precise meaning.
The true center of the world is the Imperial Capital.
Because that is where the Son of Heaven resides—the father of all his people, wielding absolute authority.
And in that same sense, Henan, which had shared in Murim’s earliest beginnings and history, could no longer be called the Murim Alliance’s headquarters.
What mattered was not the place, but the people.
The symbolism attached to a place was created by people.
Sword Saint Mae Jonghak felt that keenly through the letters arriving each day from every corner of the realm.
He had also discovered that the higher the piles of paperwork grew, the more desperately he longed for a visitor.
“Come in.”
Beyond the firmly shut door, the owner of a faint presence hesitated briefly before entering the study.
“Pardon me for a moment...”
The visitor trailed off, looking from Mae Jonghak’s sunken eyes to the piles of papers filling the room.
“Hmm. You seem busy.”
“It’s all right. Have a cup of tea before you go.”
“No, I’ll come back later—urk!”
*Whoosh! Grab!*
Mae Jonghak moved in a flash.
Using Huashan’s secret technique, Dark Fragrance Drift, he crossed the room in an instant and seized the visitor’s sleeve.
He spoke with desperate longing in his eyes and voice.
“Have a cup of tea before you go.”
“Please.”
He looked ready to grab the man by the collar if the sleeve wasn’t enough.
The visitor sensed a disturbing madness in Mae Jonghak’s glittering eyes and swallowed nervously.
“All right, all right. Let go and we’ll talk.”
“If you’re lying, I’ll resent you even after I’m dead.”
“Why go that far...? Besides, what good would resenting me do? You’d be dead.”
“That’s true. What kind of tea would you like?”
“Longjing, please.”
“It’s the only kind I have. Just drink that.”
Worried the man might change his mind, Mae Jonghak hurriedly let go of his sleeve. The visitor watched Mae Jonghak prepare the teapot and thought to himself:
*Then why did you even ask...?*
Of course, he already knew. With some people, the more you tried to understand them, the more you only hurt yourself.
It was a lesson he’d learned over the past few months with a certain madman.
“...You’re the spitting image of him. I could’ve sworn I heard he wasn’t your biological grandson.”
“Hm? What did you say?”
“Nothing. Just talking to myself.”
“I understand. The older you get, the more you talk to yourself.”
It was hard to believe this conversation was between a fresh-faced young man and a boy who looked several years younger. But appearances weren’t everything.
The Slaughter Saint knew that better than almost anyone.
“So the Alliance Leader does it too. I suppose we’re all much the same.”
“Hm? Much the same?”
“Didn’t you just say people talk to themselves more as they get older?”
“Oh, that. I meant people in general. I’ve talked to myself since I was a child, so I can’t say I relate.”
“...Is the tea going to take much longer?”
Just as the Slaughter Saint felt his energy rapidly draining away, Mae Jonghak finally set a steaming cup on the table.
“Drink. It isn’t my tea, but the aroma should be quite good.”
Mae Jonghak was right.
Perhaps because it was the tea enjoyed by a man who had been a City Lord, both its aroma and quality were excellent.
The man, who had committed countless acts of corruption, had vanished like dew on the execution grounds. But his tea leaves—and his lavish study—remained.
The study now served as the Murim Alliance’s temporary Alliance Leader’s Hall.
“I hope I’m not taking up too much of your precious time.”
The Slaughter Saint glanced at the towering piles of papers, which looked ready to collapse at any moment. Mae Jonghak tilted his hot teacup and answered.
“Time is always precious. If we’d lost the battle seven days ago, I wouldn’t be enjoying this luxury.”
Watching the wisps of steam rise like heat haze, the Slaughter Saint murmured as if to himself.
“Seven days. Has it really been that long?”
Mae Jonghak wasn’t the only one who’d been busy.

The past week had left everyone, including the Slaughter Saint, scarcely a moment to rest. They’d had to begin dealing with the aftermath before they could recover from the battle’s physical and mental toll.
And Mae Jonghak already knew that the Slaughter Saint, busy treating the wounded, wouldn’t have come without a reason.
“You’ve had time to enjoy the aroma. Well?”
Naturally, he wasn’t asking whether the man liked the tea.
The Slaughter Saint watched Mae Jonghak smile. Then he stirred the internal energy sleeping deep within him.
*Wooooom.*
A wave spread outward, making the air tremble.
Only when an invisible barrier had enclosed them both, shutting out sound, did the Slaughter Saint speak.
“I came to see you about the matter I mentioned before.”
Mae Jonghak’s eyes turned grave.
“Since you came yourself... I take it the news isn’t good.”
The Slaughter Saint’s voice was heavy.
“That’s right.”
“You couldn’t find it after all?”
“Based on what we know so far.”
That left a faint possibility, but Mae Jonghak looked doubtful. So did the Slaughter Saint, who had said it.
As soon as the battle ended, the surviving martial artists, government troops, and countless civilians had thrown themselves into dealing with the aftermath.
More than a hundred thousand people on both sides had been killed or wounded. If all those searching had failed to find *it* in seven days, the chances of finding it later were slim.
“Further searches would be pointless.”
“You mean...”
“I’m not saying we should stop entirely. Keep looking, but cut down on the manpower spent on it.”
The Slaughter Saint nodded quietly.
Mae Jonghak was right. He, too, thought it better to focus on what lay ahead than to keep pouring effort into a search with so little hope of success.
And yet, the unease weighing on him remained.
“I’m worried too. But...”
Seeing the shadow on the Slaughter Saint’s face, Mae Jonghak continued.
“The tide has already turned. The blades of the Central Plains—no, of the whole realm—have finally come together.”
Mae Jonghak reached out. Dozens of missives rose from between the piles of papers and flew toward them.

From the Nine Provinces and Eight Wastes to the Four Seas and Five Lakes, they had crossed vast stretches of sky and land to reach Xining. Each bore a different official seal, but all ended with the same four words.
“Exterminate the Demons and Set Heaven Right.”
Exterminate the demons and set heaven right.
It was the banner the old Murim Alliance had raised, and now those four words united the realm.
Even the empire, newly reborn under the name Great Ming, had embraced them.
“They’re coming. For the same single purpose as us.”
Seven days had passed since their decisive victory after a fierce battle.
But those who had spent the time since living each day as if it were a mere moment were not only the people in Xining.
On the day rivers of blood had flowed through Xining, enemy corpses had piled up like mountains in Henan Province and Shanxi Province.
Ma Sanbao’s head had been taken back to the Imperial Capital. The rest of his body had been torn apart and scattered across the realm.

The Azure Sky Sword King, who had already completed his preparations, had wiped out the enemy without suffering a single casualty. The dozen or so remaining Moving Formations had been shut down before daybreak.
As long as the Demon-Sealing Formation cast by the Zhuge Clan’s formation masters remained in place, the danger posed by the Moving Formations had effectively been eliminated.
It was the Demon-Sealing Formation that had allowed them to seal the first rift in Hubei, after all.
That newfound safety had lit a fuse that had long lain cold.
Under the banners of the Imperial House and the Murim Alliance, the westward advance had begun in earnest.

At the Son of Heaven’s decree that he would personally lead an army against the rebels, a hundred thousand elite Imperial Guards assembled. Martial artists rallied too, led by the Nine Sects and One Gang and the Five Great Families.
Nor did it end there.
Even common people with no power of their own organized volunteer militias to stand against injustice. At last, the will of the realm had come together.
“Xinjiang. We can end everything in that accursed land beyond the desert.”
Mae Jonghak spoke in a low but powerful voice.
“The only way to stop this wheel from turning is to defeat the Lord of Heaven.”
The beginning and end of it all. Its very center.
That was the Lord of Heaven.
An absolute being who had never once shown his true form, yet whose immense shadow covered the realm.
But now that the realm had joined forces and pointed its blades at the Lord of Heaven, heaven’s will was already on their side.
Or so they believed.
*...But why?*
For some reason, the words “Son of Heaven” filled him with an inexplicable sense of foreboding.
He raised his teacup, though the tea had gone cold.
Perhaps he hoped to hide the unease lodged deep in his heart.
As he drank, he turned over the other reason he had come to see Mae Jonghak.
*I still can’t make sense of what the Bow Saint said and did back then.*
More precisely, he doubted anyone could have.
That was why the Slaughter Saint found it even harder to shake from his mind.
She had stood by, almost indifferent, even when Jin Taekyung was in mortal danger. Her words and actions had been impossible to read, as though she had some purpose no one else knew about.
*She’s hiding something. I’m certain of it.*
But seven days had passed, and the Slaughter Saint still had no answer.
The Bow Saint had seldom shown herself since the battle, and Jin Taekyung had yet to regain consciousness.
*What should I do?*
Still deep in thought, the Slaughter Saint drained his tea.
He was about to speak to Mae Jonghak, who was watching him in silence as though he had sensed something.
Or tried to.
*Thud-thud-thud-thud!*
Heavy, hurried footsteps sounded. A huge man burst into the study.
*Crash!*
He smashed the door to pieces and shouted.
“Alliance Leader! Taishan saw it! With my own two eyes!”
The Slaughter Saint recognized the familiar face, sighed, and closed his mouth. Mae Jonghak felt his brief respite come to an end and answered mournfully.
“I see. What did you see?”
At Taishan’s next words, both men’s eyes widened.
“The Pavilion Master! The Pavilion Master woke up!”
