It was such a goddamn awful memory.*
Of course it was.
Back then, I’d been bursting with anticipation.
This wasn’t some run-of-the-mill Quest.
The item had been given to me as a Reward for a **[System Update]**.
*I’d gone through all that shit because of an update I didn’t even know existed.*
Right after defeating the Doppelganger in the modern world, I’d been sent straight to Murim.
It hadn’t been my choice.
The System Update had started without warning and forced me to Log In.
The System stayed dead throughout the update, only returning to normal after I’d wrapped up the events in the imperial palace.
And after going through all that bullshit, how do you think I felt when I got this piece of trash as my Reward?
*Considering how I felt back then, it’s a miracle I didn’t throw it away.*
More accurately, it wasn’t that I didn’t throw it away.
I couldn’t.
It was an update reward, after all.
I’d held onto a sliver of hope that it might have something hidden up its sleeve.
But it didn’t take long for that last flicker of hope to burn out completely.
The pocket watch was... actual garbage.
It was filthy and worn no matter how closely I looked, and clearly broken no matter how long I stared.
I examined it like a judge on an antiques appraisal show scrutinizing a national treasure, but the only unusual thing I found was one faint line inscribed on the back.
*A broken clock is right twice a day.*
Twice a day, my ass.
After a week of watching the second hand stay exactly where it was, I shoved this sturdy piece of trash deep into my Inventory.
Whoever made it, I was sure I’d beat the shit out of him if he ever showed his face.
*But... why is it showing up here again?
And like this, out of nowhere?*
I narrowed my eyes at the holographic window floating in the air.
**Item Window**
**[Pocket Watch of Unknown Make]**
**Type:** Special Item **Grade:** None **Restrictions:** None **Description:** A pocket watch made by someone unknown.
Extremely sturdy.
At a glance, it looks like an old, broken watch.
On closer inspection, it holds a secret that has yet to be uncovered.
The newly updated item information.
Actually, calling this an update seemed a little generous.
Only a few characters had been added or changed.
*The item type, and the last line of the description.*
The change was tiny.
It had gone from a Common Item to a Special Item, and the sentence “Even on closer inspection, it looks like a broken watch” had been replaced with new information.
That was all.
But the meaning behind that change didn’t feel small at all.
Especially when I thought about how this useless piece of junk had come back into my hands.
*The Helper.
The endless, infinite space.
And finally, the pocket watch.*
I kept repeating those three keywords in my head, which was already crowded with thoughts, when—
Tap, scuff, tap.
Irregular footsteps drew closer through the slightly open door, and an uninvited guest arrived.
“Buuuurp.
Whew.
I’m drunk.”
A near-mummy—no, Hyuk Mujin—appeared with a burp like a lion’s roar and looked at Jeok Cheongang and me through half-lidded eyes.
“Well, well, you’re here, are ya?
Hehe.”
Before I could say anything, Jeok Cheongang spoke in a dignified tone.
“If you’re drunk, go sleep it off.
Unless you want the shit beaten out of you.”
Hyuk Mujin answered.
“Nah.”
Who knew one word could leave both me and Jeok Cheongang so dumbfounded?
But Hyuk Mujin, who’d just accomplished what no great fiend had ever managed, didn’t stop there.
“Uuugh.”
“Hey, don’t you dare...”
“Bwaaaaargh!”
“...I said don’t.”
What the hell was wrong with this guy?
Jeok Cheongang recoiled in alarm as vomit poured out like Niagara Falls.
I sighed and patted Mujin on the back.
When he’d finished making a whole scene, he lifted his head.
“Huh?
Isn’t this that watch?
Are ya finally givin’ it to me?”
He’d spotted the pocket watch around my neck.
Then he said something I never would’ve expected.
“But did ya finally get it up and running?”
“You crazy bastard, why are you talking about getting it up all of a sudden—wait, what did you say?”
“You repaired it, didn’t ya?”
With his tongue thoroughly twisted, Hyuk Mujin mumbled and grinned as he grabbed the pocket watch swaying before him.
“Ya did.
It’s showing a different time than the last time I saw it.”
What did he just say?

chapters.title: Chapter 1144
paragraphs: Was this what it felt like to have ice water dumped over your head?
I stood frozen by the last thing I’d expected to hear. Then I grabbed Hyuk Mujin by the shoulder as he grinned to himself.
“What do you mean by that?”
Whoosh.
As I spoke in a low voice, I sent a thread of internal energy into him. Focus returned to the eyes of the man who’d been swimming in drink.
“Y-yes?”
“Say it again. What you just said.”
The alcohol had already fled.
Facing my completely serious expression, Hyuk Mujin swallowed hard.
“What I just said? Which part... Ah, the time?”
“Yeah. This thing. Do you remember it?”
I took the pocket watch from around my neck and held it close to his face. He nodded hastily.

“Of course. That was probably when we were staying at the Imperial Palace...? I begged you for it like crazy because I wanted it so badly, but you said you’d think about it, Captain. Then you never brought it out again.”
Of course he remembered.
I’d made up some story about it being a valuable item from the Western Regions, and he’d pestered me for it practically every day after that.
“I’d pretty much given up when I heard you were giving it to Young Lady Ju. I didn’t know you still had it.”
That was when it happened.
Then, as he turned the pocket watch this way and that, still apparently fascinated by it, he finally said what I’d been waiting to hear.
“Still, no matter how valuable it is, what woman would want a broken watch as a gift? You should fix it before you give it to her.”
“...Fix it?”
“Huh? Am I wrong? The last time I saw it, this long hand here was—yeah, right about there.”
I followed his finger to the hour hand and felt my face stiffen.
“Captain? Did I do something wrong?”
“No. More importantly...”
“I’m sure of it. Why would I lie about something like this?”
“Right. You wouldn’t.”
That was the end of the conversation.
I muttered to myself and waved him away without another word. Hyuk Mujin understood the gesture and withdrew. Watching him go, I fell into thought.
*Yeah. He’s right.*
My gaze dropped to the pocket watch resting in my palm.
Why hadn’t I noticed it immediately?
There was no minute hand, as any ordinary watch would have, or even any numbers. But its one and only hand had moved a notch from its original position.
Not forward. Backward.
*Unless it was designed from the start to move counterclockwise...*
Had it gone around once—or several times—before stopping here?
And if so, what did that mean?
*That old man definitely knew something.*
The updated item information said the pocket watch held a secret, and The Helper had clearly known what it was. That must have been why he’d handed it to me as a gift.
But...
But how had he known something even I didn’t?
And how had a pocket watch buried deep in my Inventory for months found its way back to me like this?
“...No way.”
My heart suddenly began to pound, and my lips went dry.
Jeok Cheongang responded to the words that had escaped me, but my mind had gone blank except for the tangled thoughts I was struggling to unravel.
And finally—
An unbelievable theory struck me like lightning.
Swift and decisive as the king’s blade that had cut through the Gordian knot no one else could untie.
That endless, infinite space.
The pocket watch that had begun to move without anyone knowing.
And The Helper—an old man whose identity was a mystery, yet whose martial prowess surpassed anyone I’d ever met.
Our meeting within my consciousness had been brief, but I’d felt his presence. It was like a colossal wall.
Not even the Three Saints, the greatest masters under Heaven, had made me feel anything so overwhelmingly terrifying.
And there was only one person who could stand above the Three Saints.
*The Martial God.*
I swallowed.
A shiver ran from the crown of my head to my toes as I recalled the theory I’d formed about him less than half a shichen ago.
*The System may have recognized Cheon Taemin’s unconscious state as a form of death.*
If that was true—
And if, for some reason, his consciousness had been preserved in the System—
Then I’d already met Cheon Taemin. The Martial God.
In that infinite space where he’d been staying.
No—in the Inventory.
*Good call.*
The voice I’d heard long ago echoed in my ears like a hallucination.
Along with the meaningless noise that had sounded at the end of my nightmare three days ago.
*Tick.*
A chill unlike anything I’d ever felt climbed my spine. I stared at the pocket watch, my gaze distant.
I thought about what the dream I’d had that day meant.
Why The Helper—the old man I now suspected was Cheon Taemin—had reminded me of a pocket watch I’d nearly forgotten.
And I knew the only way to answer all these questions.
“I have something to tell you.”
After a long silence, my one sentence made Jeok Cheongang’s gaze sink deep.
The grand banquet, where everyone had drunk together to their hearts’ content, lasted only one night. But no one in Xining was sorry to see it end.
Blood was thicker than water, and stronger than wine. A few tubs of wine could never make them forget the blood already shed.
Not when they thought of the blood still to come.
“All preparations are complete.”
High atop the city wall, Sword Saint Mae Jonghak began in a calm voice.
Not a breath of wind stirred.
Beyond the wall, countless troops had gathered across the fields beneath scores—hundreds—of banners. Their eyes, bleary with drink the night before, now burned like torches.
“Since the dark clouds of Dark Heaven first loomed over us, the realm has been plunged into turmoil and filled with screams. We’ve shed more blood than any of us can count.”
It was true.
Dark Heaven had risen only a little over two years ago. Yet the blood shed in that short time rivaled what had been spilled during the Great Faction War, which had lasted more than a decade.
“We’ve seen with our own eyes and heard with our own ears what their vile schemes have wrought.”
The conflict in Shanxi had been only the beginning.
Shaolin Temple in Henan had burned, taking the life of the eminent monk known as the Dharma King.
Soon after, all of Sichuan was drenched in blood. Then came Hubei and distant Nanman.
The Imperial Capital, Hebei, and even Gansu had been invaded.
“And at last, the will of the entire realm has gathered here in Qinghai.”
His voice, carried endlessly outward by his powerful internal energy, brought tears to the eyes of everyone listening.
They knew.
They knew how much blood it had cost to bring them here.
And they knew how precious and meaningful the blood they would shed from now on would be.
“We will hesitate no longer. We will not retreat.”
Fervor spread through the crowd.
This was their will—the will of the realm.
“We will fight not for victory, but to protect.”
Families who’d been with them since birth had died. Friends who’d supported them through hard times had died. Neighbors who’d traded smiles with them whenever they met had died.
And anyone fortunate enough to have escaped such loss would soon face it too, unless they fought back.
Unless they brought down the Lord of Heaven and the dark clouds that threatened to swallow the realm.
This was a war to protect. A holy war to exterminate fiends without equal in all history—and a mandate from Heaven.
“So I ask you...”
Shing.
A snow-white blade emerged from its sword case.
A purple glow surrounded Mae Jonghak as a vast wave of aura burst from him.
No—at his side, everyone standing tall upon the wall unleashed the countless feelings and surging auras they’d held back.
Along with the Alliance Leader’s azure dragon’s roar, which swept across the dry skies of Qinghai.
“Who among you will retreat in the face of injustice?!”
At that instant—
Clang, clang, clang, clang!
The darkened fields flashed like the sun.
Countless swords and spears rose high enough to pierce the sky. The troops’ rumbling shouts and the force of their auras set the motionless banners flapping.
Yes.
At last, the wind was blowing.
A wind born in the Nine Provinces and Eight Directions swept in, bearing cold steel and the bloody scent of vengeance.
It rushed toward the cursed forbidden land beyond the distant desert.
Boom, boom, boom!
To the deepest, fiercest beat of war drums yet, an army of more than two hundred thousand advanced across the vast wilderness.
Murim.
No—the sight of a coalition unprecedented in the continent’s history marching as one was magnificent enough to send a shiver through everyone on the wall.
But one man’s eyes still trembled.
*Damn it.*
Jin Taekyung felt a weight settle in his chest.
This should be the end. Why did it feel like a beginning?
After countless hardships, the united blade of the realm was finally aimed at the Lord of Heaven. Why did he feel as though he were walking along the edge of a cliff?
*Now’s my only chance.*
Unease pressed against a corner of his mind like a massive boulder, along with questions he still couldn’t answer.
There was only one way to resolve them and move forward.
*Master.*
At Taekyung’s quiet Sound Transmission, Jeok Cheongang gave a small nod.
*So you’ve decided to do it after all.*
That was all, and it was enough.
Before dawn, Master and Disciple had shared a long, deep conversation. They had no secrets from each other.
“Go on.”
As his Disciple climbed into the carriage they’d prepared in advance, Jeok Cheongang smiled faintly and added, “This old man will be right here, waiting with everyone.”
His Disciple answered with a smile just like his Master’s.
“I’ll be back.”
And soon, the Disciple fell asleep.
A sleep so deep and vivid that he wouldn’t know it even if someone shook him awake.

chapters.title: Chapter 1145
paragraphs: The Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, silently looked down at his Disciple, who lay comfortably before him.
His eyelids were firmly shut. His chest rose and fell with each quiet breath.
To anyone else, Jin Taekyung was fast asleep, oblivious to the world. But Jeok Cheongang knew what they did not.
His Disciple had gone not into a dream, but to another world.
*The realm of immortals.*
Jeok Cheongang clearly remembered the shock of first hearing the truth from his Disciple’s own lips.
No—he could never forget it.

A world where skyscrapers hundreds of *jang* tall stood together like a forest; where the footsteps of humanity reached beyond the sky and into the universe; where supernatural powers that defied all reason ruled the land.
It was a world Jeok Cheongang could scarcely imagine.
But the place where his Disciple had been born and raised was plainly not as peaceful or beautiful as he had first thought.
“I have to go.”
The previous night, Jin Taekyung’s face had been more solemn than Jeok Cheongang had ever seen it when he said he intended to return home.
Even his Master had never seen him like that.
“Has something happened in the realm of immortals?”
“I don’t know. Not yet.”
“Not yet, you say. From the way you put it, something bad must be happening.”
“It’s only a hunch, but yes.”
Jin Taekyung had brushed it off as *only a hunch*, but Jeok Cheongang, who knew him better than anyone, understood.
His Disciple never lied.
Behind his usual lighthearted manner, which sometimes bordered on frivolous, lurked a beast alert to even the smallest change around him.
That was why Jeok Cheongang could sense the immense anxiety and burden pressing down on Jin Taekyung’s shoulders. He could feel, too, how his own heart had dropped when he saw his Disciple like that.
Perhaps that was why he had suddenly pictured his Disciple ten days ago, his body hanging limp in Jeok Cheongang’s arms.
“Then say it properly this time.”
“What?”
“You just said you were leaving. As if you might never return.”
Perhaps Jin Taekyung had been trying to spare his Master needless worry.
Jeok Cheongang had not heard everything about the place called the realm of immortals, but he knew one thing for certain.
However different the two worlds were, if the soul was erased, the body died too.
More than anything, he feared finding his Disciple one day in a sleep from which he would never wake.
After a moment of silence that seemed to last forever, Jin Taekyung smiled and answered.
“Then... I’ll be back. I promise.”
Why, then, did Jeok Cheongang still feel so heavyhearted?
He had heard the answer he wanted. Yet the weight remained through a sleepless night, and it remained now as he kept watch beside his Disciple on the long journey.
*Another month, at the soonest.*
That was how long it would take an army of more than two hundred thousand to cross the vast Taklamakan Desert in Xinjiang.

It was only an estimate, of course. But the coalition army had finished its preparations and calculations down to the last detail. It would press across the desert with unstoppable momentum and reach its destination.
Tianshan—the place regarded as cursed for the past thousand years.
*Whatever danger waits there, it doesn’t matter. This old man will protect you.*
Those who know what they must do have no fear.
A Master belonged beside his Disciple, and Jeok Cheongang would not leave this spot until Jin Taekyung woke.
Nor would the others, who had arrived and taken up their positions without a word.
“What are you staring at?”
Jeok Cheongang answered the Slaughter Saint, who sat in one corner of the carriage with his eyes half-closed.
“There’s an uninvited guest planted right there. I was wondering who the hell he was.”
“Uninvited? Why would I be uninvited?”
“Because the owner of the carriage didn’t invite you.”
The Slaughter Saint snorted and nodded toward Jin Taekyung.
“You’re mistaken. The owner of the carriage isn’t you. It’s that fellow lying over there. And this carriage was a gift from the Emperor and the Zhuge Clan, not you.”
“But I’m his Master.”
“By that logic, so am I. I taught him something valuable once.”
“You mean that Ghost-whatever footwork technique? It wasn’t much good.”
“What? Not much good? Your lot at the Fire Gate Clan—”
“*Your lot?* You snot-nosed brat. How dare you speak to an elder like that—”

It was a bewildering exchange for two old masters whose combined ages exceeded two hundred, especially inside a carriage drawn by the eight finest imperial sweat-blood horses. Yet Jeok Cheongang felt warmth spreading through his heart.
*Do you see? Your efforts and pain weren’t in vain.*
Not even one shichen had passed since the army began its full-scale march, yet the eight-horse carriage at the very back of the long, seemingly endless column had already received plenty of visitors.
Members of the Embroidered Uniform Guard who protected the Emperor’s closest confidants. Masters of Murim, including the Nine Sects and One Gang.
Every one of them ranked among the most skilled in the vast army, and each had come asking to join the carriage’s escort.
To repay a debt.
To show even a little respect for the great devotion and effort the owner of the carriage had shown until now.
If Jeok Cheongang hadn’t sent them away with threats, there might have been more than a thousand of the finest guards surrounding the carriage by now.
A handful, of course, had stood their ground without so much as twitching an eyebrow at his threats.
“Good grief, there they go again.”
“They’ve got plenty of energy.”
“Shh. They’ll hear you.”
Familiar voices drifted through the gap in the carriage door. Jeok Cheongang felt a sudden swell of emotion and, before he knew it, let out a quiet laugh.
“Why are you laughing all of a sudden? You sound like a crazy old man.”
“Who knows.”
Even the Slaughter Saint’s sour jab could not wipe the smile from his face. Perhaps it was because he was happy.
In this harsh world, he was not the only one who treasured his Disciple as much as himself and looked out for him. The joy of knowing that was small, and enormous.
Jeok Cheongang had long ago turned his back on the world and kept his distance from people. He did not want his one and only Disciple to walk the same path.
No. This boy had to be different.
He had to pursue righteousness, practice chivalry, and win people’s hearts.
Now and in the years to come.
Always. Forever.
To see that wish fulfilled, his Master could do anything.
Even if hell waited beyond those scorching sands.
*Without fail.*
By now, Jeok Cheongang’s eyes had sunk deep as he watched the vast desert outside the window.
Rumble.

She could even hear the faint delight in that flat voice, a voice that froze the soul merely to hear it.
“You must have felt the wave.”
“What surprises you so, Grand Sorceress?”
The darkness stirred and gently wrapped around the shadow’s—no, the Grand Sorceress’s—shoulder.

The Grand Sorceress’s trembling eyes dropped to her own hand.

Ssssh.

Softly. Coolly.
“Once again, the heavens have opened.”

sentences.text: The Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, silently looked down at his Disciple, who lay comfortably before him.
His eyelids were firmly shut.
His chest rose and fell with each quiet breath.
To anyone else, Jin Taekyung was fast asleep, oblivious to the world.
But Jeok Cheongang knew what they did not.
His Disciple had gone not into a dream, but to another world.
*The realm of immortals.*
Jeok Cheongang clearly remembered the shock of first hearing the truth from his Disciple’s own lips.
No—he could never forget it.

A world where skyscrapers hundreds of *jang* tall stood together like a forest; where the footsteps of humanity reached beyond the sky and into the universe; where supernatural powers that defied all reason ruled the land.
It was a world Jeok Cheongang could scarcely imagine.
But the place where his Disciple had been born and raised was plainly not as peaceful or beautiful as he had first thought.
“I have to go.”
The previous night, Jin Taekyung’s face had been more solemn than Jeok Cheongang had ever seen it when he said he intended to return home.
Even his Master had never seen him like that.
“Has something happened in the realm of immortals?”
“I don’t know.
Not yet.”
“Not yet, you say.
From the way you put it, something bad must be happening.”
“It’s only a hunch, but yes.”
Jin Taekyung had brushed it off as *only a hunch*, but Jeok Cheongang, who knew him better than anyone, understood.
His Disciple never lied.
Behind his usual lighthearted manner, which sometimes bordered on frivolous, lurked a beast alert to even the smallest change around him.
That was why Jeok Cheongang could sense the immense anxiety and burden pressing down on Jin Taekyung’s shoulders.
He could feel, too, how his own heart had dropped when he saw his Disciple like that.
Perhaps that was why he had suddenly pictured his Disciple ten days ago, his body hanging limp in Jeok Cheongang’s arms.
“Then say it properly this time.”
“What?”
“You just said you were leaving.
As if you might never return.”
Perhaps Jin Taekyung had been trying to spare his Master needless worry.
Jeok Cheongang had not heard everything about the place called the realm of immortals, but he knew one thing for certain.
However different the two worlds were, if the soul was erased, the body died too.
More than anything, he feared finding his Disciple one day in a sleep from which he would never wake.
After a moment of silence that seemed to last forever, Jin Taekyung smiled and answered.
“Then...
I’ll be back.
I promise.”
Why, then, did Jeok Cheongang still feel so heavyhearted?
He had heard the answer he wanted.
Yet the weight remained through a sleepless night, and it remained now as he kept watch beside his Disciple on the long journey.
*Another month, at the soonest.*
That was how long it would take an army of more than two hundred thousand to cross the vast Taklamakan Desert in Xinjiang.
It was only an estimate, of course.
But the coalition army had finished its preparations and calculations down to the last detail.
It would press across the desert with unstoppable momentum and reach its destination.
Tianshan—the place regarded as cursed for the past thousand years.
*Whatever danger waits there, it doesn’t matter.
This old man will protect you.*
Those who know what they must do have no fear.
A Master belonged beside his Disciple, and Jeok Cheongang would not leave this spot until Jin Taekyung woke.
Nor would the others, who had arrived and taken up their positions without a word.
“What are you staring at?”
Jeok Cheongang answered the Slaughter Saint, who sat in one corner of the carriage with his eyes half-closed.
“There’s an uninvited guest planted right there.
I was wondering who the hell he was.”
“Uninvited?
Why would I be uninvited?”
“Because the owner of the carriage didn’t invite you.”
The Slaughter Saint snorted and nodded toward Jin Taekyung.
“You’re mistaken.
The owner of the carriage isn’t you.
It’s that fellow lying over there.
And this carriage was a gift from the Emperor and the Zhuge Clan, not you.”
“But I’m his Master.”
“By that logic, so am I.
I taught him something valuable once.”
“You mean that Ghost-whatever footwork technique?
It wasn’t much good.”
“What?
Not much good?
Your lot at the Fire Gate Clan—”
“*Your lot?* You snot-nosed brat.
How dare you speak to an elder like that—”
It was a bewildering exchange for two old masters whose combined ages exceeded two hundred, especially inside a carriage drawn by the eight finest imperial sweat-blood horses.
Yet Jeok Cheongang felt warmth spreading through his heart.
*Do you see?
Your efforts and pain weren’t in vain.*
Not even one shichen had passed since the army began its full-scale march, yet the eight-horse carriage at the very back of the long, seemingly endless column had already received plenty of visitors.
Members of the Embroidered Uniform Guard who protected the Emperor’s closest confidants.
Masters of Murim, including the Nine Sects and One Gang.
Every one of them ranked among the most skilled in the vast army, and each had come asking to join the carriage’s escort.
To repay a debt.
To show even a little respect for the great devotion and effort the owner of the carriage had shown until now.
If Jeok Cheongang hadn’t sent them away with threats, there might have been more than a thousand of the finest guards surrounding the carriage by now.
A handful, of course, had stood their ground without so much as twitching an eyebrow at his threats.
“Good grief, there they go again.”
“They’ve got plenty of energy.”
“Shh.
They’ll hear you.”
Familiar voices drifted through the gap in the carriage door.
Jeok Cheongang felt a sudden swell of emotion and, before he knew it, let out a quiet laugh.
“Why are you laughing all of a sudden?
You sound like a crazy old man.”
“Who knows.”
Even the Slaughter Saint’s sour jab could not wipe the smile from his face.
Perhaps it was because he was happy.

The joy of knowing that was small, and enormous.
Jeok Cheongang had long ago turned his back on the world and kept his distance from people.
He did not want his one and only Disciple to walk the same path.
No.
This boy had to be different.
He had to pursue righteousness, practice chivalry, and win people’s hearts.
Now and in the years to come.
Always.
Forever.

Even if hell waited beyond those scorching sands.

chapters.title: Chapter 1146
paragraphs: In a dark, narrow room, a man stood before a full-length mirror, silently staring at its smooth surface.
Tall and slender, with sharply defined features.
He had seen his reflection countless times over the past thirty-odd years. But what gripped him now was not familiarity. It was bitterness and anger.
“Why did it have to be you?”
The faint words slipped from his lips without warning.
Normally, he would never have muttered to himself. This time, he didn’t care.
“You’re not the one who should be here.”
Every word felt like breathing fire.
It ached deep in his chest, as though an invisible awl were digging into him. Beads of sweat had gathered without his noticing and rolled down his cheeks.
Like his heart. Endlessly.
“You’re not qualified.”
It was true.
Unlike the handful of people with the necessary “qualifications,” he had neither overwhelming strength nor the experience of a battle-hardened veteran.
But acknowledging that was one thing. He knew better than anyone how heavily this responsibility weighed on his shoulders, and how much this mission mattered.
That was when his trembling eyes suddenly flashed.
Crunch.
A sickening sound of torn flesh, and the taste of blood filled his mouth.
He spat out a mouthful of blood and faced the mirror again.
A man with a deep, unwavering gaze stared back at him now.
He looked uncannily like someone bound to him by the longest and closest of ties—and yet someone who had felt farther away than anyone else in the world.
But even that brief thought was a luxury for the man. For Choi Minwoo.
Crack.
A faint tremor traveled down from the ceiling, and hairline fractures spread across the full-length mirror like a spiderweb.
Sensing that the time had finally come, Choi Minwoo turned his back on his distorted reflection and flung open the rusted iron door that had briefly kept the harsh reality outside at bay.
Creeeak.
In the middle of a corridor barely wide enough for two grown men to stand shoulder to shoulder, a hulking figure wrapped from head to toe in a military poncho gave Choi Minwoo a nod.
“Right on time.”
“Sorry to keep you waiting. I needed a moment to prepare.”
“No need to apologize. You’re in charge here. Though...”
The figure glanced at the dust drifting slowly down from the ceiling, stirred by a tremor that had grown slightly stronger.
“Any later and we’d have been in trouble. Let’s go.”
As if they’d planned it, they quickly set off, trading words as they made their way through the winding, ant-nest-like corridors.
“What happened?”
The hulking figure answered Choi Minwoo in a subdued voice.
“I’d like to say it’s just a sandstorm...”
“It’s them.”
“Damn it. Yeah.”
Why did his worst suspicions never turn out to be wrong?
But Choi Minwoo had left his self-reproach and complaints behind at the broken mirror. He steeled himself and asked another question.
“How many?”
“From what we’ve been able to tell, at least several thousand.”
Several thousand.
It sounded like an absurdly broad estimate, but communications and every radar network had been down for some time. Choi Minwoo accepted the figure without question.
The hulking figure’s abilities were unlike anyone else’s in this old, worn-out underground bomb shelter. He was also someone Choi Minwoo trusted enough to entrust with his own life.
“...Several thousand?”
If there were already several thousand as far as they could tell, the number could exceed ten thousand, depending on the situation.
At Choi Minwoo’s darkening gaze, the hulking figure made an effort to shake his head.
“They might just be a scouting party. Those guys always move around in swarms like ants.”
It was a reasonable guess.
The enemy had already swallowed up a vast stretch of desert. Their numbers were terrifying, and growing by the day.
*Even if they aren’t here to attack, they could simply be passing through on their way to another city. Our routes might have crossed by chance.*
Choi Minwoo walked on in silence, lost in thought.

They were staying in an underground bomb shelter secretly built by the US military during the Gulf War. It had been abandoned for more than fifty years after the war ended, and the Great Cataclysm had reshaped the land so thoroughly that even its existence had been forgotten.
Until a group hurrying across the desert happened to find its entrance beneath a sand dune.
*If we only found it by luck, what are the chances the enemy knows it’s here?*
Slim to none.
The only thing that bothered him was the communication Magic they had barely managed to establish not long ago. But given who had sent it, the chance of the enemy detecting it was close to zero.
*Which means...*
At last, Choi Minwoo reached a conclusion.
This was a coincidence.
As the hulking figure had said, they were probably a scouting party, or their paths had simply crossed.
All Choi Minwoo and the others had to do was wait.
They could hold their breath in this old, musty shelter, let sand and dust rain down on their heads, and prepare for a fight just in case. Before long, peace would return.
The uninvited guests would pass right over them without ever finding the doorbell to their hidden home. Choi Minwoo could lead the others out of the shelter without a single casualty.
In just a few hours.
Yes.
That was the best choice.
*...Then why?*
The hulking figure’s eyes widened when Choi Minwoo suddenly stopped walking.
“What’s wrong? Is there a problem?”
After a brief silence, Choi Minwoo answered.
“No. There isn’t.”
“Damn, you scared me. We’re almost there. Let’s join the others before they start chirping like frightened chicks.”
Shaking his head, the hulking figure started down the final corridor to the central chamber.
That was when Choi Minwoo noticed how his back bulged beneath the poncho, as though he were a hunchback.
And at the same moment, his tightly shut lips parted.
“What do you think the best choice is?”
“What?”
The hulking figure turned at the unexpected question. Beneath the hood pulled almost to his nose, hair the color of molten gold spilled out.
“What’s brought this on all of a sudden...?”
“I can’t tell what’s right or wrong. What’s the difference between the best choice and the worst?”
Choi Minwoo continued in a hoarse voice. His eyes had begun to tremble, just like the ones he’d seen in the mirror.
“Even now, more than ten times our number are coming this way. But if we keep quiet and wait, there won’t be any unnecessary casualties. They don’t know we’re here.”
Rumble.
The growing tremors shook the ceiling. The rumbling had grown stronger with every step they’d taken down the corridor.
“If we wait just ten more minutes, it’ll all be over. For us, at least.”
The last words came out weakly. The hulking figure’s gaze deepened.
“Say what you want to say.”
“Whatever they’re after, blood is going to be spilled somewhere nearby. Even with their numbers, they wouldn’t move thousands of troops for no reason.”
“Now that you mention it, you’re right. So?”

“Once we’re through this corridor, I’ll give the order as their commander. If they want to make it home alive, they’re to hold their breath and wait. They’re not to get involved, whether the enemy is chasing helpless civilians or Hunters.”
The words poured out of Choi Minwoo like water through a broken dam. He drew a deep breath.
Then he saw the hulking figure’s mouth in the dim light of a bulb nearing the end of its life.
“Yeah. I see what you mean. So...”
He was smiling.
“If you’re done talking bullshit, tell me what you really want to say.”
“Come on, say it and get it off your chest. Like that guy we know so well.”
With the rumbling growing louder by the second, the hulking figure dropped onto the shaking floor, as if he wouldn’t move another step until Choi Minwoo answered.
“What, can’t you do it like him?”
Choi Minwoo clenched his trembling fist instead of answering.

He knew exactly who the hulking figure meant without hearing his name. He had watched Jin Taekyung from close by for a long time. He knew that, whatever crisis Taekyung faced, he always took responsibility for his actions.
And that was a gap Choi Minwoo could never close.
“Hunter Jin Taekyung... is different from me.”
“How?”
“I’m weak. I can’t compare to him. And I have a mission I absolutely have to succeed at, as the commander here.”
“Responsibility matters. But that’s got nothing to do with it.”
Before Choi Minwoo could respond to the cryptic remark, the hulking figure added quietly:
“The others still here are already planning to rush out and fight. Every last one of them.”

“I stopped by on my way here and told them how many enemies there were. First thing they did was grab their equipment. They said there had to be a reason that many bastards were swarming around. Know what’s even funnier?”
The hulking figure let out a short laugh.
“I told them to wait for their commander’s orders. They said you’d be thinking the same thing anyway.”
He rose and approached Choi Minwoo, who stood frozen like a statue.
But he wasn’t the only one to move.
“When are we heading out?”
Hunters had appeared at the far end of the corridor, their heads poking around the corner. The hulking figure shrugged at Choi Minwoo.
“There you have it.”
Choi Minwoo looked silently from him to the Hunters, who had already finished their preparations.
Then, slowly—
Very slowly, as a thunderous rumbling shook everything around them, he drew the sword at his waist.
“This is my answer.”
At that moment—
Hiss. Slash!
The aura surging fiercely along the blade split the shelter’s concrete wall like tofu.
KABOOM!
The explosion sent debris flying.
Beyond the shattered wall came blazing sunlight and the blood of cursed monsters.
“I like you. For a human.”
The hulking figure—the Skeleton King—laughed aloud and patted the large backpack hidden beneath his poncho.
“Don’t worry. I’ll keep you safe, you human who sleeps too much for no reason.”
And he shot toward the enemies.
Or he was about to.
If not for the answer no one had expected.
“Dad’s not sleeping.”

They’re not to get involved, whether the enemy is chasing helpless civilians or Hunters.”
The words poured out of Choi Minwoo like water through a broken dam.
He drew a deep breath.
Then he saw the hulking figure’s mouth in the dim light of a bulb nearing the end of its life.
“Yeah.
I see what you mean.
He was smiling.
“If you’re done talking bullshit, tell me what you really want to say.”
“Come on, say it and get it off your chest.
Like that guy we know so well.”
With the rumbling growing louder by the second, the hulking figure dropped onto the shaking floor, as if he wouldn’t move another step until Choi Minwoo answered.
“What, can’t you do it like him?”
Choi Minwoo clenched his trembling fist instead of answering.
He knew exactly who the hulking figure meant without hearing his name.
He had watched Jin Taekyung from close by for a long time.
He knew that, whatever crisis Taekyung faced, he always took responsibility for his actions.
And that was a gap Choi Minwoo could never close.
“Hunter Jin Taekyung... is different from me.”
“How?”
“I’m weak.
I can’t compare to him.
And I have a mission I absolutely have to succeed at, as the commander here.”
“Responsibility matters.
But that’s got nothing to do with it.”
Before Choi Minwoo could respond to the cryptic remark, the hulking figure added quietly:
“The others still here are already planning to rush out and fight.
Every last one of them.”
“I stopped by on my way here and told them how many enemies there were.
First thing they did was grab their equipment.
They said there had to be a reason that many bastards were swarming around.
Know what’s even funnier?”
The hulking figure let out a short laugh.
“I told them to wait for their commander’s orders.
They said you’d be thinking the same thing anyway.”
He rose and approached Choi Minwoo, who stood frozen like a statue.
But he wasn’t the only one to move.
“When are we heading out?”
Hunters had appeared at the far end of the corridor, their heads poking around the corner.
The hulking figure shrugged at Choi Minwoo.
“There you have it.”
Choi Minwoo looked silently from him to the Hunters, who had already finished their preparations.
Then, slowly—
Very slowly, as a thunderous rumbling shook everything around them, he drew the sword at his waist.
“This is my answer.”
At that moment—
Hiss.
Slash!
The aura surging fiercely along the blade split the shelter’s concrete wall like tofu.
KABOOM!
The explosion sent debris flying.
Beyond the shattered wall came blazing sunlight and the blood of cursed monsters.
“I like you.
For a human.”
The hulking figure—the Skeleton King—laughed aloud and patted the large backpack hidden beneath his poncho.
“Don’t worry.
I’ll keep you safe, you human who sleeps too much for no reason.”
And he shot toward the enemies.
Or he was about to.
If not for the answer no one had expected.
“Dad’s not sleeping.”

chapters.title: Chapter 1147
paragraphs: In that brief moment, split into smaller and smaller moments, the Skeleton King thought:
*Have I been feeling a little weak lately?*
Yes. He must have heard wrong.
They said that humans—strictly speaking, he wasn’t human, and certainly not an animal—sometimes heard things that weren’t there when their bodies and minds were weak.
Besides, they were about to fight enemies who outnumbered them by more than ten to one. With the odds so bad he’d borrow a cat’s paw if he could, hearing things was hardly strange.
That guy—
No, Jin Taekyung was the most reliable person in the world to him.
But...
*There’s no way he’s woken up.*
It was all wishful thinking.
They’d faced countless dangers on the way to this old, musty underground bomb shelter, but every time, Jin Taekyung’s eyelids had stayed firmly shut without so much as a twitch.
The Skeleton King had even begun to worry that he might never wake up at all.
*That damn human.*
Just as he thought it bitterly to himself—
Whoosh!
With a sharp whistle, the flow of time that had briefly stopped came rushing back like a flood.
KABOOM!
A powerful impact shook the space around them.
The Skeleton King’s expression darkened as he canceled out a dozen or so streaks of light flying through the air.
*This is...*
There was no mistaking it.
Speed and strength on a level entirely different from ordinary monsters.

The Bone Sword trembling in his grasp told him that *those guys* were among the thousands of monsters. It told him, too, that this battle—now past the point of no return—would be even harder than expected.
“Shit, it’s them!”
“Everyone, switch to a defensive formation!”
They were quick to judge, and quick to act.

Every Hunter here was a skilled veteran with plenty of combat experience. At the almost simultaneous shouts from the Skeleton King and Choi Minwoo, the Hunters charging behind their commander moved at once, without the slightest hesitation or sign of panic.
Or they did until a low voice stopped them in their tracks.
“Maintain the attack formation.”
Midway through switching to a defensive formation, the Hunters looked at one another in confusion.
First, because the order had suddenly changed.
Second, because Choi Minwoo—the only one there with the authority to give orders—looked just as strange as they did. Stranger, even.
And third—
*I’ve heard that voice somewhere before.*
They were sure of it. The voice sounded unfamiliar, yet somehow caught the ear at once. Though low and hoarse, there was something about it they couldn’t mistake.
Perhaps that was why the veteran Hunters, all of them battle-hardened, couldn’t hide their dismay.
And why they left a fatal opening for the enemies right in front of them.
—Grrrrrrrr!
Thousands of monsters surged toward them like a wave, roaring. Ghouls, Orcs, Lizardmen, and Manticores swung claws and weapons that could tear through steel like paper.
And then—
Whoosh.
A dazzling streak of light shot toward the fearsome monsters.
BOOM!
Flesh and bone exploded into hundreds, then thousands of pieces. Countless dying screams rose with sprays of blue-green blood.
In the thick mist of blood that enveloped them in an instant, those who witnessed the unbelievable scene suddenly understood.
Who had given the order they’d just heard.
Why that low, hoarse voice had felt so familiar.
“Hey.”
Over the shoulder of the Skeleton King, who stood rigid as a statue, a young man poked his head out of the backpack he’d been carrying.
“You were pretending not to hear me on purpose, weren’t you?”
Honestly, at first I thought I was dreaming.
Dreaming of a time before I was even born, when I was busy squirming around in Mom’s belly.
I mean, who would think to fold up a sleeping person and stuff them whole into a huge backpack?
And judging by the turtle-shell bondage they’d done with those famously tough ogre tendons—like something out of a certain kind of Japanese video—whoever did this wasn’t just crazy.
Of course, I knew exactly who that lunatic was.
“This bastard’s tastes are seriously... No, let’s talk about that later.”
“You, you...!”
Leaving the Skeleton King stammering behind me with a look like he’d seen a ghost, I put strength back into my stiff body.
Crack, crack.

I snapped the ogre tendons binding me from head to toe like strands of thread, tore through the backpack made of equally tough hide, and stood on my own two feet. Only then did I feel like I could breathe.
*How long was I like that?*
I had questions lined up on the tip of my tongue. But I knew this wasn’t the time to ask.
From the moment I regained consciousness until now, the stench boiling all around me and the thick magical power had been enough to make me nauseous.
“Team Leader.”
I gave a slight nod in greeting. Team Leader Choi, watching me with a jumble of emotions on his face, finally let out the breath he’d been holding.
“Everyone, form up for an attack.”
At once, the air around us began to boil.
The Skeleton King and Team Leader Choi, whom I hadn’t seen in ages, stood alongside some two hundred Hunters of various races. Eyes alight, they raised their weapons and took their places.
Like a single arrow.
And the direction it would fly was already decided.
CRUNCH, clack!
White Flame returned to my hand after piercing dozens of monsters, just as it had on its way out. It trembled in my grasp as though it sensed what was about to come.
“Let’s go.”
That was all I said.
Nothing more, nothing less.
The thought became a sound, the sound slipped past my lips—and in that instant, I was already charging at the enemies.
Whoosh.
One step.
I closed the twenty-meter gap in an instant and brought White Flame down without hesitation.
Fwoosh!
Space warped before the deep-blue flames now burning along the spearhead. Terrible heat swallowed the monsters, and pillars of fire erupted from cracks in the ground, now as hot as a field of lava.
KABOOM!
Explosions and thunderous noise. Screams burst out all around.
But I paid no attention to the massive shock wave or the chaos.
No—more accurately, none of my allies did.
Whoosh, whoosh, whoosh!
We left the flying sparks and mangled scraps of flesh behind. The two hundred or so Hunters charged like the wind and tore the monsters apart with strength even I hadn’t expected.
Whoooooosh!

In a split second, countless streaks of light dazzled my eyes. Ogre hide—said to be impenetrable even to an anti-materiel sniper rifle—and Manticore tails split like tofu, scattering in every direction.
Slash, splatter!
The monsters’ encirclement crumbled amid fountains of dark blood.
At its center, the Hunters’ weapons shone fiercely with a power I knew well.
*Aura?*
My eyes widened despite myself.
There was no mistaking it. Aura, also known as Sword Energy.
A hallmark of A-rank Hunters in the modern world and the exclusive domain of Peak masters in Murim, it flowed along their weapons.
Not just ten or twenty of them. Every one of the two hundred or so Hunters.
*Why are there this many A-rank Hunters gathered here? The last place I remember being was more than a thousand kilometers from even the nearest ally.*
What on earth had happened while I was gone?
I tried to recall what I knew of the modern world, but it was hard to make sense of the situation.
No.
Before I could even begin to understand the reality in front of me, another unexpected factor got in the way.
Ssssh.
A chillingly low whistle reached my ears. My body moved before my brain could react, bringing down White Flame’s spearhead, which had paused for only an instant.
Slash, KABOOM!
It all happened in a flash.
I cut through a crescent-shaped mass of magical power flying toward me. The concentrated, sticky-cold energy swallowed the monsters to either side.
And then—
Splash.
A group came into view, stepping through a puddle of blue-green blood.
“...What are they?”
Team Leader Choi and the Skeleton King, who had moved up on either side of me, answered the question that had slipped out on instinct.
“It’s them.”
“Be careful, human. They’re nothing like the monsters you know.”
I looked at the uninvited guests instead of answering.
There were seven of them.
They looked... human. More so than even Lizardmen, who were called humanoid monsters because they walked on two legs.
But they weren’t human.
It wasn’t just their height, well over two meters, or their bulging muscles. It wasn’t even that every one of them had exactly the same height and build, as though they’d come off a production line.
*What is that energy?*
Magical power too dense to be human, yet far too pure to be a monster’s.
The Skeleton King was right. Each of them was strong enough to rival a Named Monster, with magical power purer than any monster’s I’d ever encountered.
Like living things born with genes entirely free of flaws.
But...
“Yeah. They’re definitely different.”
The Skeleton King hadn’t been entirely right.
Step.
They weren’t the only ones on a different level.
And he had the wrong idea about who needed to be careful.
Slash.
I moved in an instant no one there could see or sense, feeling the sensation travel up the spearhead as I thought to myself:
*Six left.*

chapters.title: Chapter 1148
paragraphs: For a martial artist, growing stronger meant more than sharper senses. It meant greater concentration, too.
The terrifying focus to pour everything he had into a single instant, no matter what was happening around him, with only one thought in mind.
That was Jin Taekyung now.
Ding.
A familiar chime rang in his ears.
But his senses, honed as keen as a blade forged by a master craftsman, didn’t dull in the slightest.
If anything, they sharpened further.
*What was that?*
The sudden appearance of the mysterious Named Monsters.
He’d already killed one, but what came first wasn’t satisfaction. It was the heavy impact he’d felt through his spear and an inexplicable wariness. He moved faster still.
Flash.
A flawless Shifting Form and Position left not even an afterimage.
Six bolts of magical power fired a beat too late and pierced empty air. At the same instant, White Flame spewed fire again in Jin Taekyung’s hands.
Fwoosh—KABOOM!
Space warped along the spearhead’s slanting downward arc. Deep-blue flames, carrying a tremendous amount of Scorching Yang Qi, sliced through another Named Monster.
Or so it seemed.
Then Jin Taekyung felt the powerful recoil through the spearhead.
CRUNCH!
Eyes wide, he watched the Named Monster hurtle away.
And he understood the wariness he’d felt when he killed the first one.
*They’re tough.*
He didn’t mean their movements or their aura. Their bodies were, quite literally, damn tough.
Tough enough that even he, after bringing down countless enemies, could hardly believe it.
*White Flame can’t even cut all the way through?*
What kind of weapon was White Flame?
It was a ridiculously overpowered item he’d never have laid eyes on if the System hadn’t showered him with rewards early on. In Murim, no amount of money could buy a treasure like it.
Even modern artifacts decked out with cutting-edge technology and every kind of Magic couldn’t match the sharpness and strength of White Flame itself.
Yet its Force-wreathed spearhead couldn’t slice through these monsters like tofu. Their bones in particular were denser than he’d ever imagined.
The monster had suffered a horrific wound, of course. But it was still standing when it should have been split cleanly from collarbone to pelvis. That alone shocked Jin Taekyung.
Its incredible regenerative ability, already restoring the wound in an instant, was just a bonus.
“How is this even possible?”
The question escaped his lips. The Skeleton King, who had joined him by now, answered.
“I thought the same thing at first. But think about it. It’s not so hard to understand.”
“Why not?”
“If a human as monstrous as you exists, why can’t monsters like them?”
“Are you kidding? I’m an exception.”
“Do you have to say something that puts me off my food like it’s the most natural thing in the world?”
“Off your food? You’ve really become Korean. Weren’t you supposed to be playing a foreigner?”
The question had been based on reasonable evidence, but Mr. Stone-King, from Atlanta, Georgia, had just learned a lot from a marvel of civilization called a smartphone.
“I’m Korean American.”
“...You’ve gotten pretty good with words since I last saw you.”
“Words aren’t the only thing I’ve gotten better at.”
WHOOOOSH.
No sooner had he spoken than a tremendous mass of magical power swelled around him.
Jin Taekyung blinked at the unmistakable difference between his power now and before. The Skeleton King shrugged.
“What? Trembling at my might?”
“...What the hell happened while I was gone?”
“A lot. But I can’t tell you about it right now.”
He was right about that much.
Not far away, Choi Minwoo was leading the Hunters in a fierce battle against the monsters, while the six Named Monsters had formed a semicircle around them.
Ssshhh.
Magical power, dense enough to take shape, rippled like fog.
Behind the skull masks covering their faces, emotionless eyes fixed on the two of them like blades.
“Go for the neck. It’s the easiest part to cut.”
With the Skeleton King now at his back, Jin Taekyung adjusted his grip on the spear.
“I know.”
“We’ll take half each. Three for me, three for you.”
“Can you handle that? You’re weak as hell.”
“Arrogant human. Did you plant a knife in your tongue?”
The Skeleton King stopped grumbling. Then he added, so quietly Jin Taekyung could barely hear him:
“Still... it’s good to see you.”
*What was that?*
“I said I’m damn glad to see you again, even if it had to be like this.”
Jin Taekyung tried to think of an answer, then simply laughed.
Before an awkward silence could settle, he pushed off the ground and charged at the enemy.
And, just as his monster friend had done, he answered in a voice barely above a whisper.
“Yeah. Me too.”
It all happened almost at once.
Whoosh!
The wind rushing over him swallowed his voice. Jin Taekyung shot forward faster than sound and reached the monsters a step ahead of the Skeleton King.
KABOOM!
Three swords met one spearhead with a deafening crash.
It was no even match. The monsters gave ground under the force of the blow, and Jin Taekyung kept advancing.
KABOOM! KABOOM! CRUNCH!
Amid the successive crashes, one Named Monster failed to keep up with his strength and speed and dropped to its knees. Jin Taekyung didn’t hesitate.
Slash!
He felt the heavy resistance through the spearhead.
He put even more strength than usual into the strike, and a head in a pure-white skull mask rose into the air.
Two swords were already swinging at him from either side, but they came half a beat too late to reach him.
No—the punch he threw after they’d begun to swing struck empty air first.
WHUMP!
Compressed air exploded.
As if he’d struck a mountain to hit the cow behind it, the shock wave burst outward, driving the monsters back and opening a gap.
An opening that lasted only an instant, but could decide who lived and who died.
Whoosh!
The sequence of movements didn’t need so much as a preparatory motion.
With physical abilities that made even *superhuman* sound inadequate, Jin Taekyung threw his spear.
THUNK!
It shot through the air as though plunging from above and pierced another Named Monster.
Just as he’d intended, the spearhead slipped precisely between its bones.
CRUNCH!
Skin and flesh tougher than the hide of a large monster like an ogre were no use this time.

White Flame’s Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron spearhead punched through its target and drove deep into the ground. Leaving the monster thrashing like a fish on a harpoon, Jin Taekyung pushed off the ground again.
And used the ability granted to him alone.
*Inventory open. Summon. Summon. Summon.*
Whoosh, whoosh, whoosh!
A dozen or so daggers streaked through the air like beams of light.
The only Named Monster still on its feet swung a sword brimming with magical power and knocked every dagger aside.
By then, it was too late.
Slip.
Moving with the subtle principles of Ghost Illusory Slaughter Step, Jin Taekyung slipped deep inside its reach and swung the last dagger, the one he’d kept in his hand.
He spoke quietly.
“You’re damn tough, but...”
Slash!
“That doesn’t mean you’re strong.”
THUD.
The towering figure, well over two meters tall, crumpled to the ground.
And at that moment—
Rumble.
A vast tremor shook space itself, and a dazzling flash spread above everyone’s heads.
Maybe it was thanks to the enlightenment I’d gained during the past few months in Murim.
I felt a strange sense of familiarity before anyone else did. At the same time, I sensed an immense aura suddenly looming high overhead.
*Shit, again?*
Naturally, my first thought was that another unexpected enemy had arrived.
Another powerful being like the mysterious Named Monsters I’d brought down, and the ones the Skeleton King was still fighting.
Maybe that was why everyone on the ground froze as the tremendous rumbling shook the sky.
But why?
A terrible possibility had flashed through my mind like lightning, yet the red warning light my instincts always set off remained quiet, even as the flash swallowed the sky.
No. The larger that flash grew, the calmer I felt.
The Skeleton King, who had just taken down his second Named Monster and was locked in a desperate fight with the last one, didn’t seem to feel the same way.
“Uh? Uh, hey!”
His pupils were shaking like an earthquake measuring 8.0, tsunami included.
He glanced up at the sky with a look that said, *What the hell is that?* Then he shouted at me, standing stock-still.
“What are you doing? Quit gawking and do something!”
“Okay.”
I obediently raised both hands and waved.
At the sky.
“What are you doing, you bastard?!”
“Saying hello.”
“...What?”
My helpful explanation didn’t seem to clear things up. I grinned at him.
“Someone came a long way to get here. I should at least say hello.”
“What the hell are you—!”

WHOOOOOSH!

Toward the countless streaks of light pouring down like lightning, like arrows, with a fierce whistle—aimed only at the monsters.

sentences.text: For a martial artist, growing stronger meant more than sharper senses.
It meant greater concentration, too.
The terrifying focus to pour everything he had into a single instant, no matter what was happening around him, with only one thought in mind.
That was Jin Taekyung now.
Ding.
A familiar chime rang in his ears.
But his senses, honed as keen as a blade forged by a master craftsman, didn’t dull in the slightest.
If anything, they sharpened further.
*What was that?*
The sudden appearance of the mysterious Named Monsters.
He’d already killed one, but what came first wasn’t satisfaction.
It was the heavy impact he’d felt through his spear and an inexplicable wariness.
He moved faster still.
Flash.
A flawless Shifting Form and Position left not even an afterimage.
Six bolts of magical power fired a beat too late and pierced empty air.
At the same instant, White Flame spewed fire again in Jin Taekyung’s hands.
Fwoosh—KABOOM!
Space warped along the spearhead’s slanting downward arc.
Deep-blue flames, carrying a tremendous amount of Scorching Yang Qi, sliced through another Named Monster.
Or so it seemed.
Then Jin Taekyung felt the powerful recoil through the spearhead.
CRUNCH!
Eyes wide, he watched the Named Monster hurtle away.
And he understood the wariness he’d felt when he killed the first one.
*They’re tough.*
He didn’t mean their movements or their aura.
Their bodies were, quite literally, damn tough.
Tough enough that even he, after bringing down countless enemies, could hardly believe it.
*White Flame can’t even cut all the way through?*
What kind of weapon was White Flame?
It was a ridiculously overpowered item he’d never have laid eyes on if the System hadn’t showered him with rewards early on.
In Murim, no amount of money could buy a treasure like it.
Even modern artifacts decked out with cutting-edge technology and every kind of Magic couldn’t match the sharpness and strength of White Flame itself.
Yet its Force-wreathed spearhead couldn’t slice through these monsters like tofu.
Their bones in particular were denser than he’d ever imagined.
The monster had suffered a horrific wound, of course.
But it was still standing when it should have been split cleanly from collarbone to pelvis.
That alone shocked Jin Taekyung.
Its incredible regenerative ability, already restoring the wound in an instant, was just a bonus.
“How is this even possible?”
The question escaped his lips.
The Skeleton King, who had joined him by now, answered.
“I thought the same thing at first.
But think about it.
It’s not so hard to understand.”
“Why not?”
“If a human as monstrous as you exists, why can’t monsters like them?”
“Are you kidding?
I’m an exception.”
“Do you have to say something that puts me off my food like it’s the most natural thing in the world?”
“Off your food?
You’ve really become Korean.
Weren’t you supposed to be playing a foreigner?”
The question had been based on reasonable evidence, but Mr.
Stone-King, from Atlanta, Georgia, had just learned a lot from a marvel of civilization called a smartphone.
“I’m Korean American.”
“...You’ve gotten pretty good with words since I last saw you.”
“Words aren’t the only thing I’ve gotten better at.”
WHOOOOSH.
No sooner had he spoken than a tremendous mass of magical power swelled around him.
Jin Taekyung blinked at the unmistakable difference between his power now and before.
The Skeleton King shrugged.
“What?
Trembling at my might?”
“...What the hell happened while I was gone?”
“A lot.
But I can’t tell you about it right now.”
He was right about that much.
Not far away, Choi Minwoo was leading the Hunters in a fierce battle against the monsters, while the six Named Monsters had formed a semicircle around them.
Ssshhh.
Magical power, dense enough to take shape, rippled like fog.
Behind the skull masks covering their faces, emotionless eyes fixed on the two of them like blades.
“Go for the neck.
It’s the easiest part to cut.”
With the Skeleton King now at his back, Jin Taekyung adjusted his grip on the spear.
“I know.”
“We’ll take half each.
Three for me, three for you.”
“Can you handle that?
You’re weak as hell.”
“Arrogant human.
Did you plant a knife in your tongue?”
The Skeleton King stopped grumbling.
Then he added, so quietly Jin Taekyung could barely hear him:
“Still... it’s good to see you.”
*What was that?*
“I said I’m damn glad to see you again, even if it had to be like this.”
Jin Taekyung tried to think of an answer, then simply laughed.
Before an awkward silence could settle, he pushed off the ground and charged at the enemy.
And, just as his monster friend had done, he answered in a voice barely above a whisper.
“Yeah.
Me too.”
It all happened almost at once.
Whoosh!
The wind rushing over him swallowed his voice.
Jin Taekyung shot forward faster than sound and reached the monsters a step ahead of the Skeleton King.
KABOOM!
Three swords met one spearhead with a deafening crash.
It was no even match.
The monsters gave ground under the force of the blow, and Jin Taekyung kept advancing.
KABOOM!
KABOOM!
CRUNCH!
Amid the successive crashes, one Named Monster failed to keep up with his strength and speed and dropped to its knees.
Jin Taekyung didn’t hesitate.
Slash!
He felt the heavy resistance through the spearhead.
He put even more strength than usual into the strike, and a head in a pure-white skull mask rose into the air.
Two swords were already swinging at him from either side, but they came half a beat too late to reach him.
No—the punch he threw after they’d begun to swing struck empty air first.
WHUMP!
Compressed air exploded.
As if he’d struck a mountain to hit the cow behind it, the shock wave burst outward, driving the monsters back and opening a gap.
An opening that lasted only an instant, but could decide who lived and who died.
Whoosh!
The sequence of movements didn’t need so much as a preparatory motion.
With physical abilities that made even *superhuman* sound inadequate, Jin Taekyung threw his spear.
THUNK!
It shot through the air as though plunging from above and pierced another Named Monster.
Just as he’d intended, the spearhead slipped precisely between its bones.
CRUNCH!
Skin and flesh tougher than the hide of a large monster like an ogre were no use this time.
White Flame’s Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron spearhead punched through its target and drove deep into the ground.
Leaving the monster thrashing like a fish on a harpoon, Jin Taekyung pushed off the ground again.
And used the ability granted to him alone.
*Inventory open.
Summon.
Summon.
Summon.*
Whoosh, whoosh, whoosh!
A dozen or so daggers streaked through the air like beams of light.
The only Named Monster still on its feet swung a sword brimming with magical power and knocked every dagger aside.
By then, it was too late.
Slip.
Moving with the subtle principles of Ghost Illusory Slaughter Step, Jin Taekyung slipped deep inside its reach and swung the last dagger, the one he’d kept in his hand.
He spoke quietly.
“You’re damn tough, but...”
Slash!
“That doesn’t mean you’re strong.”
THUD.
The towering figure, well over two meters tall, crumpled to the ground.
And at that moment—
Rumble.
A vast tremor shook space itself, and a dazzling flash spread above everyone’s heads.
Maybe it was thanks to the enlightenment I’d gained during the past few months in Murim.
I felt a strange sense of familiarity before anyone else did.
At the same time, I sensed an immense aura suddenly looming high overhead.
*Shit, again?*
Naturally, my first thought was that another unexpected enemy had arrived.
Another powerful being like the mysterious Named Monsters I’d brought down, and the ones the Skeleton King was still fighting.
Maybe that was why everyone on the ground froze as the tremendous rumbling shook the sky.
But why?
A terrible possibility had flashed through my mind like lightning, yet the red warning light my instincts always set off remained quiet, even as the flash swallowed the sky.
No.
The larger that flash grew, the calmer I felt.
The Skeleton King, who had just taken down his second Named Monster and was locked in a desperate fight with the last one, didn’t seem to feel the same way.
“Uh?
Uh, hey!”
His pupils were shaking like an earthquake measuring 8.0, tsunami included.
He glanced up at the sky with a look that said, *What the hell is that?* Then he shouted at me, standing stock-still.
“What are you doing?
Quit gawking and do something!”
“Okay.”
I obediently raised both hands and waved.
At the sky.
“What are you doing, you bastard?!”
“Saying hello.”
“...What?”
My helpful explanation didn’t seem to clear things up.
I grinned at him.
“Someone came a long way to get here.
I should at least say hello.”
“What the hell are you—!”
The Skeleton King could hold it in no longer.
He burst out in anger—
At that very moment—
FLASH!
The light gathering in the sky exploded.
Within the blinding flash that spread in every direction, a different, destructive energy suddenly surged.
WHOOOOOSH!
I opened my arms wider still.
Toward the countless streaks of light pouring down like lightning, like arrows, with a fierce whistle—aimed only at the monsters.
Toward the one who had brought all this about.
My friend, and a great Grand Mage.

chapters.title: Chapter 1149
paragraphs: The battle didn’t take long to end.

By the time most of the seven named monsters leading the enemy were dead or incapacitated, the tide had already turned. Then humanity’s greatest War Mage arrived and smashed the monster army’s life support.
KWA-BOOOOM!
Attack spells rained down without pause from dozens of meters overhead, tearing up the ground and sending blood spraying. His aim was nearly perfect, as if he were sniping his targets.
That was the end of the battle.
What followed was a one-sided massacre.
“Charge! Wipe them all out!”
CRUNCH!
With me, the Skeleton King, and Team Leader Choi at their center, some three hundred Hunters swept forward like a wave and swallowed enemies more than ten times their number.
Slash, splatter!

I cut down or stabbed every enemy that came into view. The medium and large monsters that trusted their strength and fought to the end, and the ones who had finally lost their nerve and turned to run.
No exceptions. No mercy.
After a little over thirty minutes of pursuit and slaughter, not a single monster stood on two feet in the blood-soaked desert.
Well.
Actually, there was one.
“Thankfully, we didn’t suffer any casualties... What’s that insolent look for, human?”
The Skeleton King had started toward me, then hesitated and stopped. I glanced over at him.
“Hmm. It’s nothing.”
“Looks like something to me.”
“There are exceptions to every rule. Right?”
“Where’d that come from?”
“It’s a thing. It has nothing to do with you, so don’t ask.”
His eyes narrowed; he’d clearly noticed something suspicious. Thankfully, I was spared any further interrogation when a huge shadow fell across me like a lifeline from heaven.
“Gentlemen. I have a question for you.”
Dark skin like dark chocolate. Enormous muscles. And a staff that looked more vicious than most close-combat weapons.
The towering Grand Mage descended slowly through the air. When he spoke again, his voice trembled.
“What I’m looking at isn’t some damn mirage or illusion spell, is it?”
He stared at me in disbelief. I slowly held out a fist.
“Why don’t you check?”
“Oh, damn it. Jin?”
Magic Johnson, the Grand Mage from the United States, pulled me into a tight hug instead of bumping fists.
Squeeze.
The firm, heavy thing pressing into my stomach was probably his staff.
It had to be.
It took Magic Johnson quite a while to calm down. Fortunately, his excitement had come entirely from the joy of seeing me again.
Yeah. Even for a black guy, that size and hardness would be ridiculous.
“Dear God. I can see you standing here, and I still can’t believe it. When did you wake up?”
He was only just regaining his composure. I’d barely escaped the enormous arms of this Grand Mage of the physical school, and I couldn’t help glancing at the staff tucked into his belt as I answered.
“Not long ago. It still doesn’t feel real.”
“Ah, I see. The last time I managed to get in touch, I hadn’t heard you’d woken up.”
“What?”
Something about that phrasing made the dread I’d been trying to suppress stir inside me.
This was the modern world. Humanity had prospered so much that even *global community* seemed too small a phrase for it.
With Magic added to the advanced technology we already possessed, civilization had risen from the ashes of the Great Cataclysm brighter than at any other point in human history.
And yet...
*The last time he managed to get in touch?*
For a moment, I couldn’t make sense of it.
Magic Johnson was a Grand Mage. One of only three masters of Magic among billions of people—no, only two now.

True, as a War Mage, most of his Magic was geared toward combat. But a Grand Mage could turn imagination into reality. One teleportation spell could carry him hundreds, even thousands, of kilometers. Given the right conditions, he could contact someone just as far away whenever he wanted.
So his choice of words wasn’t merely strange. It was ominous.
He sounded like a signalman who’d barely managed to reach his allies through a broken radio.
Everything about this was telling me the same thing.
It was finally time to face reality.
“Johnson.”
“Yeah?”
“When was that last contact?”
“Well...”
Magic Johnson trailed off. Then, as if something had just occurred to him, he turned to the Skeleton King beside him.
“Could it be...?”
The Skeleton King muttered as though making an excuse.
“Damn it. I didn’t have time to tell you.”
“...Shit.”
“I couldn’t have told you, either.”
More precisely, I hadn’t been able to bring myself to ask.
I’d been that afraid. That scared.
*How long?*
What had happened while I was gone? How much time had passed?
I let out a quiet, trembling breath. Magic Johnson looked at me and sighed deeply.
“Fuck.”
It hurt to tell me. It would hurt to hear it.
But putting it off would only make it worse.
“Tell me. Right now.”
And the very next moment, the answer I’d been waiting for came from over Magic Johnson’s shoulder.
“The last contact was a day ago. Twenty-one hours ago, to be exact.”
Team Leader Choi.
Monster blood and bits of flesh had dried on his armor and sword. His gaze was drier than sand, and it pierced me like an awl.
“The first contact was three hours before that.”
Twenty-four hours. One day.

The numbers leaving Team Leader Choi’s lips seemed to grow thousands of times heavier, crushing my chest. My vision went white—whiter than all the flashes Magic Johnson had unleashed on the monsters combined.
*No way.*
A difference in the flow of time far beyond any ratio we’d seen before.
But that wasn’t all.
Even before Team Leader Choi spoke again, I knew instinctively that a crueler truth was coming.
In the vast silence pressing down around us, he drew a deep breath. His voice trembled as he continued.
“Today is the tenth day since you lost consciousness.”
At that moment—
Dum, dum, dum.
A war drum sounded, low and ominous. Before my eyes appeared a new kind of System window, unlike any I’d seen in Murim.

**System** A trigger has activated due to the failure of the Main Quest, Cataclysm. **Mission:** Prevent the Summoning (Failed) You defeated the “Final Abyss” Doppelganger, but did not complete the mission. As a result of the Main Quest’s failure, the boundary of the Demon Realm has partially opened. Unknown beings are invading this world. A rift is in progress. Its progress will change when certain conditions are met and can be checked through the System.
The words were the same ones that had been etched clearly in my last memory of the modern world.
But a new holographic window appeared over them, bearing the name of a being I’d never seen or heard of.
**System** An unknown being willingly answers the summoning. The immense shadow of Black Dragon Duke Morgoth has fallen over this world. Would you like to view the new Main Quest, Rift and Collapse?
Frozen like a statue, I suddenly remembered.
The enormous wings I’d seen in that meaningless nightmare on my last night in Murim.
The dragon’s roar, shaking the sky swallowed by darkness.
The man was black as pitch.

His hair reached his calves, and his eyes looked as though they’d been set with obsidian. The only part of him that wasn’t black was his irises. They shone silver, whiter than white, and were captivating enough to make anyone feel as though they might be drawn in.
Anyone, that is, except the old man calmly watching him enter his office.
Step. Step.
Footsteps echoed in the silence.
The man crossed the long carpet. Only when he came right up to the old man did the old man speak.
“You have no manners.”
The man answered with a look, and the old man went on.
“A guest should wipe his shoes before coming in. You’ve dirtied the carpet.”
“Ah.”

At the man’s soft exclamation, something stirred in the old man’s chest. If not for the blood and scraps of human flesh scattered along his path, the old man might even have taken an immense liking to him.
“My apologies. I’m still a little clumsy with things like this.”
The man smiled gently and offered his hand. Despite what he’d just said, the movement was perfectly natural.
“Ah, have I got it wrong again? I was told this is how you do things.”
The man tilted his head. After a moment’s silence, the old man replied.
“No. I was only surprised by how practiced you are. Your appearance, too—and that handshake.”
The movement was more than natural. It carried grace and elegance. And the man himself might well have been the most beautiful human being in the world.
But the old man knew better.
He had seen with his own eyes what the man before him had done barely ten minutes earlier: erased his beloved Red Square with a single gesture.
“So, Morgoth. What brings you here?”
Vladimir Furin, Russia’s dictator, gritted his teeth as he clasped the hand of the monster wearing a human face.
